title: [Bug] backgroundcontroller doesn't run with MutatingPolicies
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.18.0

### Kubernetes Version

1.34.x

### Kubernetes Platform

KinD

### Kyverno Rule Type

Mutate

### Description

The Background controller doesn't mutate resources if the source spec is a `MutatingPolicy`. There is no UpdateRequest created and there are no events whatsoever in the backgroundcontroller about it. When migrating back to a `ClusterPolicy`, this works like a charm. 

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a default KinD cluster (but issue in all K8s distro's) and install Kyverno
2. Add the needed RBAC to the background controller:
```
  backgroundController:
    rbac:
      clusterRole:
        extraResources:
          - apiGroups: ["storage.k8s.io"]
            resources: ["storageclasses"]
            verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "update", "patch"]
```
3. Create this MutatingPolicy:
```
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: MutatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: add-label-storageclasses
spec:
  evaluation:
    background:
      enabled: true
    mutateExisting:
      enabled: true
  matchConditions:
    - expression: |-
        object.metadata.name in [
          "standard"
        ]
      name: is-ocs-storageclass
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups:
          - storage.k8s.io
        apiVersions:
          - v1
        operations:
          - CREATE
          - UPDATE
        resources:
          - storageclasses
  mutations:
    - applyConfiguration:
        expression: |-
          Object{
            metadata: Object.metadata{
              labels: {
                "configuration": "Custom"
              }
            }
          }
      patchType: ApplyConfiguration
```
3. Wait for the background controller interval; by default 1hr. See that the label is not appended to the storageclass `Default`.
4. To verify with a similar ClusterPolicy, create the following:
```
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: add-label-storageclasses
spec:
  admission: true
  background: true
  emitWarning: false
  mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate: true
  rules:
    - match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds:
                - StorageClass
              names:
                - default
      mutate:
        patchStrategicMerge:
          metadata:
            labels:
              configuration: 'clusterpolicyTest'
        targets:
          - apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
            kind: StorageClass
            name: standard
      name: add-label-ocs-storageclasses
      skipBackgroundRequests: true
  validationFailureAction: Audit
```
When the background controller runs at it's interval, you see the needed `UpdateRequests` in the namespace of kyverno, and the storage class `default` gets adjusted with the `configuration: 'clusterpolicyTest'` label.

### Expected behavior

The MutatingPolicy should also trigger the Background controller and should append the configured label to the StorageClass as described above.

### Screenshots

_No response_

title: [Bug] kyverno-policies vpol `restrict-seccomp-strict` reports violation when `seccompProfile` is set at pod level only
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.18.0

### Description

**Chart versions:** kyverno 3.8.1 (appVersion v1.18.1), kyverno-policies 3.8.0
**Policy type:** `ValidatingPolicy` (`policyType: ValidatingPolicy`)
**Kubernetes server version:** v1.32.x (client v1.34.1)

### Description

The PSS restricted specification states ([upstream docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/#restricted)):

> The container fields may be undefined/nil if the pod-level `spec.securityContext.seccompProfile.type` field is set appropriately.

The `restrict-seccomp-strict` ValidatingPolicy reports a violation for pods that set `seccompProfile.type` at pod level only, with no per-container override. The Kubernetes PSS admission controller (enforce mode) admits the same pod without any warning or error.

### Steps to reproduce
1) Install kyverno
2) install kyverno-policies via helm, values:
```yaml
policyType: ValidatingPolicy
podSecurityStandard: restricted
validationFailureAction: Audit
```
3) Apply a namespace with PSS restricted enforced:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: pss-kyverno-test
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce-version: latest
```

4) Apply a pod with seccompProfile at pod level only (all other restricted requirements met):

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: pss-seccomp-test
  namespace: pss-kyverno-test
spec:
  securityContext:
    seccompProfile:
      type: RuntimeDefault
    runAsNonRoot: true
    runAsUser: 65534
  containers:
    - name: pause
      image: busybox:1.37
      command: ["sleep", "infinity"]
      securityContext:
        allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
        capabilities:
          drop: [ALL]
      resources:
        requests:
          cpu: 1m
          memory: 4Mi
        limits:
          memory: 4Mi
```

#### Observed behavior

Pod is admitted by Kubernetes without warnings. Kyverno PolicyReport contains:

policy: restrict-seccomp-strict
message: Seccomp profile must be explicitly set. The fields
  spec.securityContext.seccompProfile.type,
  spec.containers[*].securityContext.seccompProfile.type, ...
  must be set to `RuntimeDefault` or `Localhost`.

#### Expected behavior

No violation. The pod-level seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault satisfies the PSS restricted
requirement per the Kubernetes specification.

#### Negative test

Removing seccompProfile entirely causes Kubernetes to reject the pod:

```
Error from server (Forbidden): error when creating "pod.yaml": pods "pss-seccomp-test" is forbidden: violates PodSecurity "restricted:latest": seccompProfile (pod or container "pause" must set securityContext.seccompProfile.type to "RuntimeDefault" or "Localhost")
```

This confirms Kubernetes treats pod-level-only as compliant and absent as non-compliant.

title: [Bug]  Admission controller bootstrap deadlock on AKS cluster after restart
body: ### Kyverno Version 1.16.4 ### Kubernetes Version 1.34.x ### Kubernetes Platform AKS ### Kyverno Rule Type Validate ### Description ### Kyverno Version 1.14.4 (Helm chart 3.4.4) After a AKS cluster stop/start (scheduled weekend shutdown), the Kyverno admission controller enters a bootstrap deadlock and cannot self-recover. Other workloads in non-excluded namespaces also fail to schedule. The stale ValidatingWebhookConfiguration and MutatingWebhookConfiguration persisted in etcd with failurePolicy: Fail, causing the API server to reject all pod creation requests since the webhook endpoint was unreachable. This effectively blocked all deployments on the cluster. Manual deletion of the stale webhook configurations only resolves the deadlock. Mitigations Attempted (none resolve the deadlock): 1. Namespace exclusion on webhooks: config: webhooks: namespaceSelector: matchExpressions: - key: kubernetes.io/metadata.name operator: NotIn values: - kube-system - kyverno - monitoring excludeKyvernoNamespace: true 2. resourceFilters excluding kyverno namespace: resourceFilters: - '[*/*,kube-system,*]' - '[*/*,kyverno,*]' 3. AKS admission enforcer disabled: webhookAnnotations: 'admissions.enforcer/disabled': 'true' ### Steps to reproduce Note: This issue is intermittent. - Deploy Kyverno 1.14.4 on AKS - Configure policies with failurePolicy: Fail (default) - Stop the AKS cluster (all nodes deallocated, all pods terminated) - Start the AKS cluster (nodes come up fresh, no pods running) - Observe: Kyverno admission controller pods cannot start due to webhook deadlock - Cluster deadlock ### Expected behavior Kyverno admission controller should self-recover on cluster start without manual intervention. title: [Bug] ValidatingPolicy autogen not working with namespaceSelector
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.18.0

### Description

We are in the process of migrating our existing ClusterPolicies to the new policy types and noted that the autogen feature does not work when we use a namespaceSelector. We are running into this error with the following policy:

```yaml

kind: ValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: validate-container-names
  annotations:
    policies.kyverno.io/title: 'Validate container names'
    policies.kyverno.io/category: 'other'
    policies.kyverno.io/scored: 'true'
    policies.kyverno.io/subject: 'Pod'
    # policies.kyverno.io/minversion: ''
    policies.kyverno.io/description: |
      Validates every container of product pod templates against the following rules:
        - Every pod must have a main container
        - Every initContainer's name should end with -init suffix
    kyverno.io/kyverno-version: '1.13'
    kyverno.io/kubernetes-version: '1.30-1.32'

spec:
  # Selection
  matchConditions:
    # Skip pod, we only make the policy for pods to leverage autogen
    - name: is-not-pod
      expression: |
        request.resource.resource != 'pods'

    # - name: is-product-namespace
    #   expression: >-
    #     namespaceObject.?metadata.labels['kubernetes.io/namespace-type'].orValue('') == 'product'
  matchConstraints:
    namespaceSelector:
      matchExpressions:
        - key: kubernetes.io/namespace-type
          operator: In
          values:
            - product
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: ['']
        apiVersions: ['v1']
        operations: ['CREATE', 'UPDATE']
        resources: ['pods']

  # behavior
  validationActions:
    - Deny
  evaluation:
    admission:
      enabled: true
    background:
      enabled: false
    mode: Kubernetes
  webhookConfiguration:
    timeoutSeconds: 10
  autogen:
    validatingAdmissionPolicy:
      enabled: true
    podControllers:
      controllers:
        - deployments
        - jobs
        - cronjobs

  # Validation
  validations:
    - message: >
        Every pod must have a main container.
      reason: Invalid
      expression: |
        object.spec.containers.exists(c,
          c.name == 'main'
        )

    - message: >
        Every initContainer's name should end with -init suffix.
      reason: Invalid
      expression: |
        !has(object.spec.initContainers) || object.spec.initContainers.all(c,
          c.name.matches('^.+-init$')

```

When we use `matchConditions` and apply the same policy, autogen works as intended but it is not ideal because the webhooks would be evaluated for every apply on every namespace.

title: [Bug] Helm: enabling reportsServer fails to render with "Image tags must be strings" (3.8.x regression)
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.18.0

### Description

Enabling reports-server on the 3.8.x chart makes helm fail at template render.  Just setting                                       `reportsServer.enabled=true` is enough.

### Repro

```bash
helm template kyverno kyverno/kyverno --version 3.8.1 -n kyverno --set reportsServer.enabled=true
```

### Output

```text
Error: execution error at (kyverno/templates/reports-controller/deployment.yaml:94:12): Image tags must be strings.
```

`helm install` fails the same way. The init container is in all four controller deployments, render just stops at the reports-controller one.

### Expected

Renders and installs reports-server, like 3.7.0 did.

### Cause

With `reportsServer.enabled=true` and `waitForReady` (default true), each controller gets a `wait-for-reports-server` init container. Its image is built in `templates/reports-server/_helpers.tpl` (`kyverno.reportsServer.initContainer`, line 22):

```yaml
image: {{ include "kyverno.image" (dict ... "image" .Values.test.image "defaultTag" .Values.test.image.tag) | quote }}
```

It passes `.Values.test.image.tag` as the `defaultTag` (its own fallback). In 3.8.x `test.image.tag` defaults to `~`/null (`values.yaml:573`), so `kyverno.image` gets `$tag = default null null = null`, and the guard in `_helpers/_image.tpl` does `fail "Image tags must be strings."`.

3.7.0 didn't hit this because it pinned `test.image.tag: 'v0.1.0'` (`values.yaml:536`). It got changed to `~` in 3.8.x, so this is a regression.

Confirmed on chart 3.8.0 and 3.8.1 (app v1.18.0 and v1.18.1) and still reproduces on main. Helm v4.2.0.

### Workaround

```bash
--set-string test.image.tag=latest
```

or:

```bash
--set reportsServer.waitForReady=false
```

to skip the init container.

(`--set-string` because a numeric tag gets coerced to a float and trips the same guard.)

### Suggested fix

Either re-pin `test.image.tag` to a real string like 3.7.0 did, or change `kyverno.reportsServer.initContainer` to pass a real fallback instead of the tag as its own `defaultTag`.

Side note: there's also a harmless:

```text
warning: skipped value for reports-server.imagePullSecrets: Not a table
```

(parent `imagePullSecrets` is a map, the subchart's is a list). Unrelated to this failure, just flagging it.

title: [Bug] Creating a NamespacedMutatingPolicy and MutatingPolicy without matching condition causes webhook name to be duplicated
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.18.0

### Kubernetes Version

1.34.x

### Kubernetes Platform

Other (specify in description)

### Kyverno Rule Type

Mutate

### Description

This is a RKE2 cluster.

We first created a `NamespacedMutatingPolicy`:
```
> kubectl get namespacedmutatingpolicy -A
NAMESPACE         NAME                                               AGE   READY
longhorn-system   longhorn-instance-manager-termination-protection   14d 
```

This generates a valid MutatingWebhookConfiguration (I'll omit some generated bits for brevity):
```yaml
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: MutatingWebhookConfiguration
metadata:
  annotations:
    admissions.enforcer/disabled: "true"
  labels:
    webhook.kyverno.io/managed-by: kyverno
  name: kyverno-resource-mutating-webhook-cfg
webhooks:
- admissionReviewVersions:
  - v1
  clientConfig:
    caBundle: OMMITED
    service:
      name: kyverno-svc
      namespace: kyverno
      path: /nmpol/longhorn-instance-manager-termination-protection
      port: 443
  failurePolicy: Fail
  matchPolicy: Equivalent
  name: mpol.validate.kyverno.svc-fail
  namespaceSelector:
    matchExpressions:
    - key: kubernetes.io/metadata.name
      operator: NotIn
      values:
      - kube-system
    - key: kubernetes.io/metadata.name
      operator: NotIn
      values:
      - kyverno
  objectSelector:
    matchLabels:
      longhorn.io/component: instance-manager
      longhorn.io/managed-by: longhorn-manager
  reinvocationPolicy: Never
  rules:
  - apiGroups:
    - ""
    apiVersions:
    - v1
    operations:
    - CREATE
    resources:
    - pods
    scope: '*'
  sideEffects: NoneOnDryRun
  timeoutSeconds: 10
```

Note the name: `mpol.validate.kyverno.svc-fail`.

Then, we try to create a cluster-wide `MutatingPolicy`:
```
> kubectl get mutatingpolicy
NAME             AGE   READY
proxy-registry   39m   true
```

Despite that `true` in the READY column, the admission controllers error nonstop (see logs bellow) and the policy is not applied.

It seems that the controller ignores the name of the policy and namespace when updating the mutating webhook, and simply tries to create a new one with the same name.

We have a separate cluster where we applied only the `proxy-registry` `MutatingPolicy`, and that webhook looks like this:
```yaml
webhooks:
- admissionReviewVersions:
  - v1
  clientConfig:
    caBundle: OMMITED FOR BREVITY
    service:
      name: kyverno-svc
      namespace: kyverno
      path: /mpol/proxy-registry
      port: 443
  failurePolicy: Fail
  matchPolicy: Equivalent
  name: mpol.validate.kyverno.svc-fail
  namespaceSelector:
    matchExpressions:
    - key: kubernetes.io/metadata.name
      operator: NotIn
      values:
      - kube-system
    - key: kubernetes.io/metadata.name
      operator: NotIn
      values:
      - kyverno
  objectSelector: {}
  reinvocationPolicy: Never
  rules:
    - OMMITED FOR BREVITY
  sideEffects: NoneOnDryRun
  timeoutSeconds: 10
```

Note, once again, the name `mpol.validate.kyverno.svc-fail`.

Issue https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/issues/15445 seems similar, but maybe that was only namespaced policies? I don't see the global mutating policies applying name prefixes or suffixes.

I also noticed that when recreating the `NamespacedMutatingPolicy`, we get an error on the logs (also see bellow), but it "seems" to work.

~~I'm also failing at replicating this on a Minikube cluster and fresh install. I'll note that the first policy (the namespaced one) was applied when Kyverno was in version 1.17.1, then it was upgraded to 1.18.0 for the cluster-wide policy. We then downgraded to 1.17.2, thinking it was a regression, but no dice.~~

I was able to replicate the problem specifically with this policy. It generates a policy with the `mpol.validate.kyverno.svc-fail` name, no namespace and name suffix:
```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: NamespacedMutatingPolicy
metadata:
  annotations:
    policies.kyverno.io/category: Reliability
    policies.kyverno.io/description: Injects the label nethermind.io/termination-protection="true"
      onto any Pod bearing the Longhorn instance-manager labels, at creation time
      only. Used in conjunction with the Termination Protection validating policy
      in this namespace
    policies.kyverno.io/severity: high
    policies.kyverno.io/title: Longhorn Instance Manager Termination Protection
  name: longhorn-instance-manager-termination-protection
  namespace: longhorn-system
spec:
  matchConstraints:
    objectSelector:
      matchLabels:
        longhorn.io/component: instance-manager
        longhorn.io/managed-by: longhorn-manager
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups:
      - ""
      apiVersions:
      - v1
      operations:
      - CREATE
      resources:
      - pods
  mutations:
  - applyConfiguration:
      expression: |-
        Object{
          metadata: Object.metadata{
            labels: {"termination-protection": "true"}
          }
        }
    patchType: ApplyConfiguration
```

Then I added this snippet
```yaml
  matchConditions:
  - name: always-true
    expression: "true"
```

And suddenly...
```yaml
name: mpol.validate.kyverno.svc-fail-finegrained-longhorn-system-longhorn-instance-manager-termination-protection
```

So it seems the issue seems to be that the controller tries to group up both namespaced and non namespaced policies in the same webhook, with the same name.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a `NamespacedMutatingPolicy` with the example above, no matching conditions
2. Create a `MutatingPolicy` with no matching conditions
3. The controller should fail at patching the MutatingWebhookConfiguration
4. Add a matching condition to the policies
5. The correct name is created, controller patches successfully

The controller should successfully handle both policies existing at the same time

title: GeneratingPolicy with generateExisting panics background controller when matchConstraints targets a resource the SA cannot list
body:
# [Bug] GeneratingPolicy with `generateExisting` panics background controller when `matchConstraints` targets a resource the SA cannot list

## Kyverno Version

1.17.0 , 1.18.0 and older versions

## Kubernetes Version

1.34.x

## Kubernetes Platform

EKS

## Kyverno Rule Type

Generate

---

## Description

When a `GeneratingPolicy` (`policies.kyverno.io/v1`) has `spec.evaluation.generateExisting.enabled: true` and `matchConstraints.resourceRules` targets `customresourcedefinitions`, the background controller calls `ListResource` on CRDs cluster-wide. However, the `kyverno-background-controller` ServiceAccount only has `get` on CRDs — not `list` or `watch` — so the API server returns `403 Forbidden`.

The upstream bug is in `pkg/policy/gpol.go:103–107`: the error branch logs but is missing a `continue` statement, so execution falls through and immediately dereferences the nil result, causing:

```
runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
```

Both background controller replicas enter `CrashLoopBackOff`, which causes significant disruption as the background controller is responsible for processing all generate rules.

**Notes on scope:**

- The bug only fires with `generateExisting: true`. Without it, applying the policy doesn't crash the controller.
- The bug fires even when no matching CRD exists in the cluster. `ListResource` is called before any `matchConditions` are evaluated, so the cluster-wide list itself is what fails.
- A `403 Forbidden` from the API server is something controllers encounter regularly (RBAC narrowed, CRD removed mid-reconcile, etc.). It should not cause a panic.
- The default Kyverno chart grants only `get` on CRDs to the background controller, so a `GeneratingPolicy` triggering on CRDs crashes the controller out of the box.

> Related: #15722 — a separate `generateExisting` issue (UR race condition causing generated resources to be deleted immediately after creation). Same surface area, different code path; the fixes are independent.

---

## Steps to Reproduce

Install Kyverno via the official Helm chart 3.7.x (Kyverno 1.18.0) with default RBAC, then apply:

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: GeneratingPolicy
metadata:
  name: repro-gpol-panic
spec:
  evaluation:
    generateExisting:
      enabled: true
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: ["apiextensions.k8s.io"]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
        resources: ["customresourcedefinitions"]
  matchConditions:
    - name: never-matches
      expression: "object.metadata.name == 'crd-that-does-not-exist'"
  generate:
    - expression: |-
        generator.Apply("", [
          {
            "apiVersion": dyn("v1"),
            "kind": dyn("ConfigMap"),
            "metadata": dyn({
              "name": dyn("would-be-generated"),
              "namespace": dyn("default")
            })
          }
        ])
```

The cluster does not need to have any matching CRD — the `LIST` fails before any matching happens. `matchConditions` is set to a name that doesn't exist so the policy stays harmless if the bug is fixed.

Within ~60 seconds the background controller starts crashlooping. Confirm via:

```bash
kubectl logs -n kyverno \
  -l app.kubernetes.io/component=background-controller \
  --previous --tail=200
```

The stack trace points at `pkg/policy/gpol.go:107`.

---

## Expected Behavior

`getGpolTriggers` should skip the failing GVR and continue with the rest of the trigger rules. Optionally, emit a `PolicyError` event so the missing RBAC is visible to operators.

---

## Suggested Fix

Add `continue` after the error log:

```go
resources, err := pc.client.ListResource(context.TODO(), groupVersion.String(), gvk.Kind, "", objectSelector)
if err != nil {
    pc.log.Error(err, "failed to list resources", "groupVersion", groupVersion, "kind", gvk.Kind)
+   continue
}
for i, res := range resources.Items {
```

The same pattern is already used for the `restMapper.KindFor` error branch a few lines up.

Additionally, the default Helm chart RBAC for `kyverno-background-controller` should be updated to include `list` and `watch` on `customresourcedefinitions`, since triggering on CRDs is a common use case.

---

## Kyverno Logs

```
ERR github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/policy/gpol.go:105 > failed to list resources
  error="customresourcedefinitions.apiextensions.k8s.io is forbidden:
  User \"system:serviceaccount:kyverno:kyverno-background-controller\"
  cannot list resource \"customresourcedefinitions\" in API group
  \"apiextensions.k8s.io\" at the cluster scope"
  groupVersion=apiextensions.k8s.io/v1 kind=CustomResourceDefinition
  logger=PolicyController

panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference [recovered, repanicked]
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x8 pc=0x3dcaa13]

goroutine 396 [running]:
...
github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/policy.(*policyController).getGpolTriggers(0xc000cd5800, 0xc000583220)
        github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/policy/gpol.go:107 +0x513
github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/policy.(*policyController).handleGenerateExisting(0xc000cd5800, 0xc00004bd40)
        github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/policy/gpol.go:63 +0x10c
github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/policy.(*policyController).syncPolicy(0xc000cd5800, {0xc008cb4990, 0x24})
        github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/policy/policy_controller.go:441 +0x865
```

---

## Workaround

Grant `list` and `watch` on `customresourcedefinitions` to the `kyverno-background-controller` ServiceAccount via an additive `ClusterRole`:

```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: kyverno:background-controller:additional-permissions
rules:
  - apiGroups: ["apiextensions.k8s.io"]
    resources:
      - customresourcedefinitions
    verbs:
      - list
      - watch
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: kyverno:background-controller:additional-permissions
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: kyverno:background-controller:additional-permissions
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: kyverno-background-controller
    namespace: kyverno
```

This unblocks the CRD trigger case but must be repeated per resource type for any other non-listable resource. The two-line code fix above is the real resolution.

---

## Slack Discussion

_No response_

---

## Troubleshooting

- [x] I have read and followed the documentation AND the [[troubleshooting guide](https://kyverno.io/docs/troubleshooting/)](https://kyverno.io/docs/troubleshooting/).
- [x] I have searched other issues in this repository and mine is not recorded.

title: [Bug] chart cert-manager delegation leaves in-process certmanager controller active, causing TLS Secret ping-pong
body:
### Kyverno Version

chart 3.7.2 (current latest on `https://kyverno.github.io/kyverno/`), also reproduces on 3.7.1. App version v1.17.2.

### Kubernetes Version

1.30 / 1.31 (reproduces on both)

### Kubernetes Platform

Vanilla kubeadm cluster (TwinX research cluster).

### Description

When enabling cert-manager delegation via `admissionController.certManager.enabled=true`, the chart still wires `--caSecretName` / `--tlsSecretName` args into the admission and cleanup controller containers, so the in-process `certmanager-controller` module remains active. This leads to a fight over the TLS Secrets between cert-manager and the in-process module:

1. cert-manager issues a certificate into `kyverno-svc.<ns>.svc.kyverno-tls-pair`.
2. The in-process controller overwrites the Secret with its own self-managed key/cert.
3. cert-manager then detects `Secret contains a private key that does not match the current CertificateRequest` and reissues.
4. The cycle repeats — I observed roughly 220 iterations in 14 minutes on our cluster before rolling back the delegation.

`values.yaml` has no option to disable the in-process certmanager controller (e.g. `disableCertManager`, `certRenewer.enabled`), so this cannot be resolved from values alone.

### Steps to Reproduce

\`\`\`bash
helm template kyverno kyverno/kyverno --version 3.7.2 \\
  --set admissionController.certManager.enabled=true \\
  | grep -E \"caSecretName|tlsSecretName\"
\`\`\`

Expected when delegating to cert-manager: no `--caSecretName` / `--tlsSecretName` args on the controller containers (or an explicit flag that disables the in-process module).

Actual output (4 occurrences on both 3.7.1 and 3.7.2):

\`\`\`
- --caSecretName=kyverno-svc.default.svc.kyverno-tls-ca
- --tlsSecretName=kyverno-svc.default.svc.kyverno-tls-pair
- --caSecretName=kyverno-cleanup-controller.default.svc.kyverno-tls-ca
- --tlsSecretName=kyverno-cleanup-controller.default.svc.kyverno-tls-pair
\`\`\`

### Expected Behavior

When `admissionController.certManager.enabled=true` (and equivalently for `cleanupController.certManager.enabled`), the chart should either:

1. Omit `--caSecretName` / `--tlsSecretName` args entirely so the in-process module no longer manages those Secrets, or
2. Add an explicit flag (e.g. `--disable-cert-manager`) and pass it conditionally when cert-manager delegation is enabled.

### Workaround

Set `admissionController.certManager.enabled=false` and stay on the self-managed cert mode.

### Related searches

I couldn't find an existing issue for this exact behavior. Closest searches in this repo:
- `cert-manager` → #9074, #15730 (unrelated)
- `caSecretName` → #15244 (chore, unrelated)
- `certManager.enabled` → no results

If maintainers agree on the direction (option 1 vs. option 2 above), I'm happy to open a PR adding the corresponding values toggle and gating the args on it.

title: Bug: Context leak in dynamic resource watcher
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.16.4



## Describe the bug

While reviewing the report controllers, I noticed a context propagation issue in the `resource-report-controller`. 

In `pkg/controllers/report/resource/controller.go`, the `startWatcher` function correctly accepts a `ctx context.Context` parameter to manage the lifecycle of the dynamic watchers. However, the function ignores this `ctx` when actually spinning up the underlying Kubernetes watch connections and the `RetryWatcher`. 

Instead, it hardcodes `context.Background()` and `context.TODO()`:

```go
func (c *controller) startWatcher(ctx context.Context, logger logr.Logger, gvr schema.GroupVersionResource, gvk schema.GroupVersionKind, errChan chan schema.GroupVersionResource) (*watcher, error) {
    // ...
	watchFunc := func(options metav1.ListOptions) (watch.Interface, error) {
		logger.V(3).Info("creating watcher...")
        // Hardcoded context.Background()
		watch, err := c.client.GetDynamicInterface().Resource(gvr).Watch(context.Background(), options) 
		// ...
	}
    // Hardcoded context.TODO()
	watchInterface, err := watchTools.NewRetryWatcherWithContext(context.TODO(), resourceVersion, &cache.ListWatch{WatchFunc: watchFunc})
    // ...
}
```
Because the context tree is broken, if the controller context times out or gets cancelled gracefully, the RetryWatcher and the active API server watch connections will not receive the ctx.Done() signal. Although there is a manual .Stop() call elsewhere in the cleanup logic, ignoring the parent context can still lead to hanging connections or leaked goroutines during edge cases or shutdown events.

## Steps to reproduce
This is a static code issue located in pkg/controllers/report/resource/controller.go inside startWatcher.

## Expected behavior
The RetryWatcher and the Watch() call should use the parent ctx passed into the function to ensure proper Go context cancellation and resource cleanup.

## Proposed Fix
Replace the hardcoded contexts with the provided ctx argument:

1. Update watchFunc to use Watch(ctx, options) instead of context.Background().
2. Update the NewRetryWatcherWithContext call to use ctx instead of context.TODO().

title: [Bug] Autogen corrupts CEL expressions with double-replacement on combined spec and metadata queries
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.16.4



## Describe the bug

When Kyverno auto-generates CEL-based rules for Pod controllers (Deployments, DaemonSets, CronJobs, etc.), it sometimes corrupts the generated CEL expression by doing a "double replacement" on the field paths. 

This specifically happens if an expression gets processed multiple times or references both `object.spec` and `object.metadata`. The root cause seems to be that `bytes.ReplaceAll` is used in `pkg/cel/autogen/replacement.go` (and `pkg/autogen/v1/rule.go`) without any word-boundary protection. 

Because the replacements happen sequentially, and the `metadata` replacement's `To` value actually contains the word `spec` (e.g. `spec.template.metadata`), a subsequent pass can re-match the `spec` part inside the newly written string. 

For example, on a CronJob autogen:
1. `object.metadata.name` gets replaced with `object.spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.metadata.name`
2. If `object.spec` gets evaluated again (or if there are multiple chained passes), it grabs the `object.spec` right out of that new string and expands it *again*, resulting in a mangled path like:
   `object.spec.jobTemplate.spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec.template.metadata.name`

This creates a structurally invalid CEL expression, which causes the policy to silently fail or error out during admission.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a `ValidatingPolicy` (with `validationFailureAction: Enforce`) that checks both `spec` and `metadata` in a single CEL expression:
```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1beta1
kind: ValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-labels-and-no-privileged
spec:
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups: [""]
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
      resources: ["pods"]
  validations:
  - expression: >
      object.spec.containers.all(c,
        !has(c.securityContext) || !c.securityContext.privileged
      ) && has(object.metadata.labels)
    message: "Privileged containers not allowed and labels are required"
```

2. Apply the policy.
3. Inspect the auto-generated rules (especially the autogen-cronjob ones).
4. Notice that the CEL expressions contain corrupted, duplicated paths instead of the correct `spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.metadata` path.
## Expected behavior
The CEL field paths should be translated exactly once for the target controller without re-expanding already replaced text.

## Actual behavior
The string replacement logic acts greedily on already-replaced text because bytes.ReplaceAll doesn't check word boundaries, corrupting the CEL path.
## Suggested Fix
Switching from sequential bytes.ReplaceAll calls to strings.NewReplacer in pkg/cel/autogen/replacement.go would solve this elegantly, since strings.NewReplacer does a single-pass, non-overlapping substitution:


```go
func Apply(data []byte, replacements ...Replacement) []byte {
    oldnew := make([]string, 0, len(replacements)*4)
    for _, r := range replacements {
        oldnew = append(oldnew,
            "object."+r.From, "object."+r.To,
            "oldObject."+r.From, "oldObject."+r.To,
        )
    }
    return []byte(strings.NewReplacer(oldnew...).Replace(string(data)))
}
```

title: [Bug] IVPOL bundle verification silently drops user-provided tsaCertChain on the keyless path
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.18.0

### Description

When Kyverno's `ImageValidatingPolicy` (IVPOL) verifies a sigstore bundle (`signatureFormat: bundle` / v3-bundle attestations attached as OCI 1.1 referrers), the keyless path silently drops the user-provided `tsaCertChain`. Bundles whose timestamp is signed by a TSA outside any TUF root — e.g. GitHub `actions/attest-build-provenance` on private repos, which uses GitHub's per-tenant TSA — fail to verify with no indication that the configured chain was ignored.

### Reproduction

Verify a v3-bundle attestation on an image whose RFC3161 timestamp is signed by a TSA *not* present in the TUF-fetched trusted root, providing the TSA chain via `Cosign.CTLog.TSACertChain`. User-facing config shape:

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1beta1
kind: ImageValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: verify-private-attestations
spec:
  matchConditions:
    - name: image
      expression: "..."
  attestors:
    - name: github
      cosign:
        keyless:
          identities:
            - issuer: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
              subject: https://github.com/MY_ORG/MY_REPO/.github/workflows/build.yml@refs/heads/main
        ctLog:
          # Any TSA cert chain whose leaf is not part of the TUF-fetched
          # trusted root. The headline real-world case is GitHub's
          # per-tenant TSA chain used by actions/attest-build-provenance
          # on private repos (Subject: O=GitHub, Inc., CN=TSA Timestamping;
          # not present in any public sigstore TUF root and not part of any
          # GitHub-published trusted_root.json that also includes Fulcio /
          # Rekor).
          tsaCertChain: |
            <PEM-encoded leaf + intermediates + self-signed root>
  attestations:
    - name: slsa
      inToto:
        type: https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1
```

The image carries a v3 sigstore bundle (e.g. produced by `actions/attest-build-provenance@v2` on a private repo, attached as an OCI 1.1 referrer). Verification fails — the resulting error is downstream of cosign and doesn't mention the dropped chain.

For a self-contained programmatic reproducer that doesn't depend on a specific image or TSA, the unit tests in #16084 and #16048 generate a synthetic CA + TSA-leaf chain, build the same `cosign.CheckOpts` shape, and assert the resulting `TrustedMaterial.TimestampingAuthorities()` either does (with the fix) or doesn't (without) include the configured leaf.

### Expected behavior

The TSA chain provided in `Cosign.CTLog.TSACertChain` is honoured during signed-timestamp verification. Bundles whose timestamp is signed by the configured TSA verify successfully (assuming all other checks pass).

### Actual behavior

The chain is silently dropped at the cosign-as-library layer. Signed-timestamp verification fails because sigstore-go's verifier doesn't see the configured TSA in its trusted material.

### Root cause

`pkg/image/verifiers/ivpol/cosign/opts.go`'s `checkOptions` populates `cosign.CheckOpts` with both:

1. `TrustedMaterial` from `getTrustedRootFromTUF` (the public TUF root) — line 144-148.
2. `TSACertificate / TSAIntermediateCertificates / TSARootCertificates` from the parsed `att.CTLog.TSACertChain` — line 95-117.

When `cOpts.NewBundleFormat` is true (auto-detected when v3 bundles are attached, `verifier.go:31-43`), `verifier.go:73-77` calls `cosign.VerifyImageAttestations`, which dispatches to `verifyImageAttestationsSigstoreBundle` → `VerifyNewBundle` → `co.verificationOptions()`. That last call wraps `co.TrustedMaterial` directly without folding in the legacy `TSACertificate / TSARootCertificates / TSAIntermediateCertificates` fields:

```go
// pkg/cosign/verify.go:232-233 in cosign v3
vTrustedMaterial := &verifyTrustedMaterial{TrustedMaterial: co.TrustedMaterial}
```

The wrapped material is handed to `verify.NewVerifier`, which looks up timestamping authorities via `TrustedMaterial.TimestampingAuthorities()`. The caller's TSA chain — which only lives in the legacy CheckOpts fields — is never seen.

This is the same root cause as [sigstore/cosign#4847](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/issues/4847) (the TSA-chain regression). [@steiza's comment on that issue](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/issues/4847#issuecomment-3500670921) recommends that callers verifying bundles in Go use `sigstore-go` directly rather than relying on cosign-as-library.

### Affected configurations

- IVPOL with a `Cosign` attestor that has both `Keyless` (so `TrustedMaterial` is set) and `CTLog.TSACertChain` (so the legacy TSA fields are set).
- The image carries a v3 sigstore bundle as an OCI 1.1 referrer (so `NewBundleFormat` is auto-detected as `true`).
- The TSA cert chain is *not* part of the configured TUF root.

The headline real-world case is GitHub `actions/attest-build-provenance` on private repos. The workflow attests with GitHub's per-tenant TSA, which isn't in the public sigstore TUF root nor in any GitHub TUF mirror that ships a unified trusted_root.json including it.

Also reproducible on `main` HEAD as of `7f70ad5d5`.

### Candidate fixes

Two PRs exist; both produce the same end-user outcome on the affected case.

- **#16084 (proposed) — migrate IVPOL's bundle path to sigstore-go directly.** Mirrors the sigstore-go-direct shape that CPOL already uses, and aligns with [@steiza's recommendation on sigstore/cosign#4847](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/issues/4847#issuecomment-3500670921) ("cosign is intended to be used as a CLI, not a library"). ~700 LoC. Adds a small dispatch refactor to `verifier.go`. The architecturally cleaner option — also inoculates IVPOL against future cosign-as-library regressions in this codepath.

- **#16048 (alternative) — minimal-scope workaround.** Stays on cosign-as-library and composes the TSA chain into `TrustedMaterial` via a `TrustedMaterialCollection` before assigning to `opts.TrustedMaterial`. ~200 LoC, no change to `verifier.go`. The TSA chain reaches sigstore-go through cosign's existing `verificationOptions` wrapping because `TrustedMaterialCollection.TimestampingAuthorities()` aggregates from all members. Available if the project would rather not take the larger refactor now.

#### Third option: wait for an upstream cosign fix

[sigstore/cosign#4847](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/issues/4847) is the upstream tracking issue; [sigstore/cosign#4849](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/pull/4849) is one candidate fix at the cosign-library layer (~16 LoC). If accepted, both Kyverno PRs (#16084 and #16048) become moot — every cosign-as-library consumer benefits, not just IVPOL. Caveats: the maintainer position on that thread is sceptical of cosign-as-library use ("cosign is intended to be used as a CLI, not a library"), so acceptance and timing are uncertain; even if it lands, propagation to a Kyverno release would take a cosign release + `go.mod` bump + Kyverno release. Worth knowing about during triage but not a blocker for landing one of the Kyverno-side fixes if the maintainers prefer.

title: [Bug] ValidatingPolicy ignores full-exemption PolicyException when resource also matched by image-scoped PolicyException
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.18.0

### Description

When a ValidatingPolicy evaluates a resource where multiple PolicyExceptions applies, a full-exemption PolicyException (one with no `images` nor `allowedValues` specified) will be silently overridden by a partial exception (one with `images` or `allowedValues` specified). The resource ends up being evaluated against the policy instead of being skipped entirely, leading to unexpected denials.

### Steps to reproduce

Below is a set of resources which illustrates the problem using `kyverno test`.

*policies.yaml* - ValidatingPolicy that disallows `:latest` image tags unless explictly permitted by `exceptions.allowedImages`
```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: ValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: disallow-latest-tag
spec:
  validationActions:
    - Deny
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups:
          - ""
        apiVersions:
          - "*"
        operations:
          - CREATE
          - UPDATE
        resources:
          - pods
  validations:
    - expression: >-
        object.spec.containers.all(c, c.image in exceptions.allowedImages || !c.image.endsWith(':latest'))
      message: Container images must not use the 'latest' tag unless explicitly allowed by a PolicyException.
```

*policyexceptions.yaml* - two PolicyExceptions targeting the same ValidatingPolicy
```yaml
# Partial exception: allows image-a:latest specifically.
# Matches any pod that has at least one container whose image starts with 'image-a:'.
# Because it specifies `images`, it does not fully exempt the resource — other containers
# still need to satisfy the policy unless covered by their own exception.
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: PolicyException
metadata:
  name: allow-image-a-with-latest
spec:
  policyRefs:
    - name: disallow-latest-tag
      kind: ValidatingPolicy
  images:
    - image-a:latest
  matchConditions:
    - name: allow-image-a-with-latest
      expression: >-
        has(object.spec.containers) && object.spec.containers.exists(c, c.image.startsWith('image-a:'))
---
# Full-exemption exception: no `images` restriction, intended to skip the policy
# entirely for pods carrying the skip label, regardless of which images they use.
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: PolicyException
metadata:
  name: skip-disallow-latest-tag-for-labelled-pods
spec:
  policyRefs:
    - name: disallow-latest-tag
      kind: ValidatingPolicy
  matchConditions:
    - name: skip-if-labelled
      expression: >-
        has(object.metadata.labels) && 'skip-policy-disallow-latest-tag' in object.metadata.labels && object.metadata.labels['skip-policy-disallow-latest-tag'] == "true"
```

*pods.yaml* - four pods covering relevant combinations
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: cnt-a-latest-cnt-b-versioned
spec:
  containers:
    - name: container-a
      image: image-a:latest
    - name: container-b
      image: image-b:1.0.0
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: cnt-a-latest-cnt-b-latest
spec:
  containers:
    - name: container-a
      image: image-a:latest
    - name: container-b
      image: image-b:latest
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: cnt-a-latest-cnt-b-latest-with-skip-label
  labels:
    skip-policy-disallow-latest-tag: "true"
spec:
  containers:
    - name: container-a
      image: image-a:latest
    - name: container-b
      image: image-b:latest
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: cnt-b-latest-with-skip-label
  labels:
    skip-policy-disallow-latest-tag: "true"
spec:
  containers:
    - name: container-b
      image: image-b:latest
```

*kyverno-test.yaml* - Kyverno test setup
```yaml
apiVersion: cli.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: policyexception-inffective-allowed-images
policies:
  - ./policies.yaml
exceptions:
  - ./policyexceptions.yaml
resources:
  - ./pods.yaml
results:
  # Baseline: image-a:latest is covered by allowedImages; image-b:1.0.0 has no :latest tag. Policy passes.
  - policy: disallow-latest-tag
    isValidatingPolicy: true
    resources:
      - cnt-a-latest-cnt-b-versioned
    kind: Pod
    result: pass

  # Expected denial: allow-image-a-with-latest covers image-a:latest, but image-b:latest is not
  # in allowedImages and is not in any full-exemption exception. Policy must deny.
  - policy: disallow-latest-tag
    isValidatingPolicy: true
    resources:
      - cnt-a-latest-cnt-b-latest
    kind: Pod
    result: fail

  # BUG: both exceptions match (allow-image-a-with-latest AND skip-disallow-latest-tag-for-labelled-pods).
  # The full-exemption exception should skip the policy entirely, but the non-empty allowedImages
  # from the other exception prevents the skip. Actual result is fail instead of skip.
  - policy: disallow-latest-tag
    isValidatingPolicy: true
    resources:
      - cnt-a-latest-cnt-b-latest-with-skip-label
    kind: Pod
    result: skip

  # Correctly skipped: only the full-exemption exception matches (no image-a container means
  # allow-image-a-with-latest does not match). Combined allowedImages is empty, so the
  # resource is excluded from policy evaluation as expected.
  - policy: disallow-latest-tag
    isValidatingPolicy: true
    resources:
      - cnt-b-latest-with-skip-label
    kind: Pod
    result: skip
```

Resources as files: [policies.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27517995/policies.yaml) [kyverno-test.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27517986/kyverno-test.yaml) [policyexceptions.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27517998/policyexceptions.yaml) [pods.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27517990/pods.yaml)


Run the kyverno test shows one test failing:

```sh
$ kyverno test . --detailed-results
Loading test  ( kyverno-test.yaml ) ...
  Loading values/variables ...
  Loading policies ...
  Loading resources ...
  Loading exceptions ...
  Applying 1 policy to 4 resources with 2 exceptions ...
  Checking results ...

│────│─────────────────────│───────────│──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────│────────│─────────────────────│────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────│
│ ID │ POLICY              │ RULE      │ RESOURCE                                                 │ RESULT │ REASON              │ MESSAGE                                                                                        │
│────│─────────────────────│───────────│──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────│────────│─────────────────────│────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────│
│ 1  │ disallow-latest-tag │           │ v1/Pod/default/cnt-a-latest-cnt-b-versioned              │ Pass   │ Ok                  │ success                                                                                        │
│ 2  │ disallow-latest-tag │           │ v1/Pod/default/cnt-a-latest-cnt-b-latest                 │ Pass   │ Ok                  │ Container images must not use the 'latest' tag unless explicitly allowed by a PolicyException. │
│ 3  │ disallow-latest-tag │           │ v1/Pod/default/cnt-a-latest-cnt-b-latest-with-skip-label │ Fail   │ Want skip, got fail │ Container images must not use the 'latest' tag unless explicitly allowed by a PolicyException. │
│ 4  │ disallow-latest-tag │ exception │ v1/Pod/default/cnt-b-latest-with-skip-label              │ Pass   │ Ok                  │ rule is skipped due to policy exception: skip-disallow-latest-tag-for-labelled-pods            │
│────│─────────────────────│───────────│──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────│────────│─────────────────────│────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────│


Test Summary: 3 tests passed and 1 tests failed

Error: 1 tests failed
```

### Expected behavior

`cnt-a-latest-cnt-b-latest-with-skip-label` (test 3) should be *skipped*. The pod carries the label `skip-policy-disallow-latest-tag: "true"`, which satisfies `skip-disallow-latest-tag-for-labelled-pods` — a full-exemption exception with no
  images defined. That exception alone should be sufficient to fully exempt the resource from policy evaluation.

### Actual behaviour

The `cnt-a-latest-cnt-b-latest-with-skip-label` resource is *denied* (result: `Fail`). The policy is evaluated with `allowedImages = ["image-a:latest"]` (contributed by the other matched exception), causing `image-b:latest` to fail the validation expression.

This is in contrast to `cnt-b-latest-with-skip-label` (test 4) which demo that the full-exemption exception works correctly in isolation: that pod has no `image-a` container, so `allow-image-a-with-latest` does not match it, the combined `allowedImages` stays empty, and the resource is correctly skipped.

body:

title: [Improvement] Modify ImageValidatingPolicy to use Secret informer cache instead of making a REST `GET` to the API server
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.2

### Description

ImageValidatingPolicy resolves imagePullSecrets via a direct REST `GET` to the API server on every admission request, instead of using the secret informer cache the way the legacy `ClusterPolicy.verifyImages` rule does, this caused us  to quckly exhaust kyverno's client-side rate limiter, causing admission webhook timeouts. We should ideally move to using secret informer cache (like the legacy ClusterPolicy already does), since the informer cache should be more performant in general?

title: [Bug] GeneratingPolicy synchronize watcher permanently dies with generateExisting and many namespaces
body:
Note - this issue has been troubleshooted with AI assistance and the text below this paragraph is AI generated/human reviewed. I can vouch for the primary issue content and iterations that led to the reproduction script. I've included the LLM's take on RCA and proposed remediations in a comment in case it is useful to the code owners.

### Kyverno Version

1.17.2

## Metadata
- **Kyverno Version:** 1.17.2 (also confirmed on 1.18.0)
- **Kubernetes Version:** 1.35.x (kind), 1.30.x (AKS)
- **Kubernetes Platform:** KinD (reproduction), AKS (originally observed)
- **Kyverno Rule Type:** Generate

## Description

When a `GeneratingPolicy` with `synchronize: true` and `generateExisting: true` is deployed to a cluster with many namespaces (~50+), the background controller's dynamic watcher for the generated resource type (e.g., `v1/configmaps`) permanently dies. After this occurs:

- **Source-change propagation stops entirely.** Updating the source ConfigMap never reaches existing clones.
- **New namespace creation still works** (admission-time generation is unaffected).
- **The failure is permanent** — the watcher is never recreated, even across background controller restarts, because each restart re-processes all existing namespaces and re-triggers the same failure.

We observed this on an AKS cluster with ~90 namespaces, and have a minimal reproduction on a kind cluster with 50 namespaces.

## Steps to reproduce

A self-contained reproduction script is detailed below. It requires `kind`, `helm`, `kubectl`, and `python3`.

```bash
./kyverno-sync-bug-repro.sh       # defaults: 50 namespaces, chart 3.7.2 (kyverno v.1.17.2)
./kyverno-sync-bug-repro.sh 50 3.8.0  # test against v1.18.0
```

**Summary of what the script does:**

1. Creates a kind cluster and installs Kyverno with chart version 3.7.2
2. Grants the background controller RBAC for ConfigMap CRUD (required for GeneratingPolicy to function — not included in default Helm chart RBAC)
3. Creates a source namespace with a ConfigMap
4. Applies a GeneratingPolicy with `synchronize: true` and `generateExisting: true`
5. Creates 50 namespaces (triggers `generateExisting` processing)
6. Waits up to 120s for clone generation — **only ~43/50 clones are created**
7. Verifies source-change sync works for a clone that was created — **PASS**
8. Restarts the background controller (triggers reprocessing of all namespaces)
9. Verifies source-change sync after restart — **FAIL** (120s timeout, clone never updated)

<details>
<summary>Full reproduction script (kyverno-sync-bug-repro.sh)</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Reproduction script for Kyverno GeneratingPolicy synchronize bug
# Affects: v1.17.2 (chart 3.7.2), v1.17.1 (chart 3.7.1), v1.18.0 (chart 3.8.0)
#
# Prerequisites: kind, helm, kubectl, python3
#
# Usage:
#   ./kyverno-sync-bug-repro.sh [NS_COUNT] [CHART_VERSION]
#   ./kyverno-sync-bug-repro.sh 50 3.7.2    # default
#   ./kyverno-sync-bug-repro.sh 50 3.8.0    # test v1.18.0
#
# Expected result: "RESULT: Sync FAILED after restart — bug REPRODUCED"

CLUSTER_NAME="kyverno-sync-repro"
NS_COUNT="${1:-50}"
KYVERNO_VERSION="${2:-3.7.2}"

cleanup() {
  echo ""
  echo "=== Cleaning up ==="
  kind delete cluster --name "$CLUSTER_NAME" 2>/dev/null || true
}
trap cleanup EXIT

echo "=== Environment ==="
echo "  kind: $(kind version)"
echo "  helm: $(helm version --short 2>/dev/null)"
echo "  kubectl: $(kubectl version --client -o json 2>/dev/null | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["clientVersion"]["gitVersion"])' 2>/dev/null || kubectl version --client --short 2>/dev/null)"
echo "  Kyverno chart: $KYVERNO_VERSION"
echo "  NS_COUNT: $NS_COUNT"
echo ""

echo "=== Step 1: Create kind cluster ==="
kind create cluster --name "$CLUSTER_NAME"
CTX="kind-${CLUSTER_NAME}"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 2: Install Kyverno $KYVERNO_VERSION ==="
helm repo add kyverno https://kyverno.github.io/kyverno/ --force-update >/dev/null 2>&1
helm install kyverno kyverno/kyverno -n kyverno --create-namespace \
  --kube-context "$CTX" \
  --version "$KYVERNO_VERSION" \
  --set admissionController.replicas=1 \
  --set backgroundController.resources.limits.memory=512Mi \
  --wait --timeout 120s

echo ""
echo "=== Step 3: Grant background controller generate RBAC ==="
kubectl --context "$CTX" apply -f - <<'RBAC'
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: kyverno-generate-repro
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["secrets", "configmaps"]
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "create", "update", "patch", "delete"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: kyverno-generate-repro
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: kyverno-generate-repro
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: kyverno-background-controller
    namespace: kyverno
RBAC

echo ""
echo "=== Step 4: Create source namespace and ConfigMap ==="
kubectl --context "$CTX" create ns source-ns
kubectl --context "$CTX" create configmap test-config -n source-ns \
  --from-literal=key1=original --from-literal=key2=value2

echo ""
echo "=== Step 4b: Wait for Kyverno webhooks to be ready ==="
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  if kubectl --context "$CTX" get --raw /readyz 2>/dev/null | grep -q ok; then
    if kubectl --context "$CTX" get endpoints kyverno-svc -n kyverno \
         -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
      echo "Kyverno webhook endpoint ready (iteration $i)"
      break
    fi
  fi
  echo "  Waiting for webhook... ($i/30)"
  sleep 5
done
sleep 5

echo ""
echo "=== Step 5: Apply GeneratingPolicy with synchronize + generateExisting ==="
kubectl --context "$CTX" apply -f - <<'POLICY'
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: GeneratingPolicy
metadata:
  name: sync-test-config
spec:
  evaluation:
    synchronize:
      enabled: true
    generateExisting:
      enabled: true
    orphanDownstreamOnPolicyDelete:
      enabled: true
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        resources: ["namespaces"]
        operations: [CREATE]
  matchConditions:
    - name: not-source
      expression: "object.metadata.name != 'source-ns'"
  variables:
    - name: targetNs
      expression: "object.metadata.name"
    - name: src
      expression: 'resource.Get("v1", "configmaps", "source-ns", "test-config")'
  generate:
    - expression: "generator.Apply(variables.targetNs, [variables.src])"
POLICY

echo ""
echo "=== Step 6: Wait for policy to be ready ==="
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  ready=$(kubectl --context "$CTX" get generatingpolicies.policies.kyverno.io sync-test-config \
    -o jsonpath='{.status.conditionStatus.ready}' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ "$ready" = "true" ]; then
    echo "Policy ready (iteration $i)"
    break
  fi
  sleep 2
done

echo ""
echo "=== Step 7: Create $NS_COUNT namespaces ==="
for i in $(seq 1 "$NS_COUNT"); do
  kubectl --context "$CTX" create ns "test-ns-$(printf '%03d' $i)" 2>/dev/null &
done
wait
echo "Created $NS_COUNT namespaces"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 8: Wait for clones to be generated ==="
echo "Waiting up to 120s for background controller to process all namespaces..."
for i in $(seq 1 24); do
  CLONE_COUNT=$(kubectl --context "$CTX" get cm --all-namespaces \
    --field-selector metadata.name=test-config -o json \
    | python3 -c "import json,sys; items=json.load(sys.stdin)['items']; print(len([i for i in items if i['metadata']['namespace'] != 'source-ns']))")
  echo "  ($i/24) Clones: $CLONE_COUNT / $NS_COUNT"
  if [ "$CLONE_COUNT" -ge "$NS_COUNT" ]; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 5
done
echo "Clones found: $CLONE_COUNT / $NS_COUNT"

SAMPLE_NS=$(kubectl --context "$CTX" get cm --all-namespaces \
  --field-selector metadata.name=test-config -o json \
  | python3 -c "import json,sys; items=json.load(sys.stdin)['items']; ns=[i['metadata']['namespace'] for i in items if i['metadata']['namespace'] != 'source-ns']; print(ns[0] if ns else '')")
if [ -z "$SAMPLE_NS" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: No clones were created at all"
  exit 1
fi
echo "Using sample namespace: $SAMPLE_NS"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 9: Verify sync works BEFORE restart ==="
kubectl --context "$CTX" patch configmap test-config -n source-ns \
  --type merge -p '{"data":{"key1":"pre-restart-update"}}'
echo "Source patched with key1=pre-restart-update"
echo "Waiting up to 30s for pre-restart sync..."
PRE_SYNCED=false
for i in $(seq 1 10); do
  PRE_VAL=$(kubectl --context "$CTX" get cm test-config -n "$SAMPLE_NS" \
    -o jsonpath='{.data.key1}' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ "$PRE_VAL" = "pre-restart-update" ]; then
    echo "PASS: Sync works before restart (iteration $i)"
    PRE_SYNCED=true
    break
  fi
  sleep 3
done
if [ "$PRE_SYNCED" != "true" ]; then
  echo "NOTE: Sync did not propagate within 30s before restart"
fi

echo ""
echo "=== Step 10: Restart background controller ==="
kubectl --context "$CTX" rollout restart deploy/kyverno-background-controller -n kyverno
kubectl --context "$CTX" rollout status deploy/kyverno-background-controller -n kyverno --timeout=60s
echo "Waiting 30s for controller to initialize..."
sleep 30

echo ""
echo "=== Step 11: Check watcher lifecycle after restart ==="
echo "--- Dynamic watcher events (ANSI stripped) ---"
kubectl --context "$CTX" logs deploy/kyverno-background-controller -n kyverno \
  | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' \
  | grep "processing generated\|start watcher\|watcher stopped\|Resource deleted\|Resource added\|Resource updated\|deleting downstream\|watcher already" \
  | head -40 || true
echo ""

echo ""
echo "=== Step 12: Test sync AFTER restart ==="
kubectl --context "$CTX" patch configmap test-config -n source-ns \
  --type merge -p '{"data":{"key1":"post-restart-update"}}'
echo "Source patched with key1=post-restart-update at $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
echo "Waiting up to 120s for propagation to $SAMPLE_NS..."
SYNCED=false
for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  val=$(kubectl --context "$CTX" get cm test-config -n "$SAMPLE_NS" \
    -o jsonpath='{.data.key1}' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ "$val" = "post-restart-update" ]; then
    echo "Sync propagated at $(date +%H:%M:%S) (iteration $i)"
    SYNCED=true
    break
  fi
  sleep 3
done

echo ""
echo "=== Results ==="
if [ "$SYNCED" = "true" ]; then
  echo "RESULT: Sync worked after restart — bug did NOT reproduce"
  echo "Try increasing NS_COUNT (current: $NS_COUNT) or adding background churn"
else
  POST_VAL=$(kubectl --context "$CTX" get cm test-config -n "$SAMPLE_NS" \
    -o jsonpath='{.data.key1}' 2>/dev/null || echo "MISSING")
  echo "RESULT: Sync FAILED after restart — bug REPRODUCED"
  echo "  Sample namespace: $SAMPLE_NS"
  echo "  Source has: key1=post-restart-update"
  echo "  Clone has:  key1=$POST_VAL"
  echo ""
  echo "--- Full watcher log (ANSI stripped) ---"
  kubectl --context "$CTX" logs deploy/kyverno-background-controller -n kyverno \
    | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' \
    | grep -E "dynamic_watcher|deleting downstream|processing generated|generate_controller|watcher stopped|watcher already" \
    | tail -50 || true
fi
```

</details>

## Expected behavior

1. All 50 clones should be created when `generateExisting: true` is set.
2. After restarting the background controller, source-change propagation should resume. Updating the source ConfigMap should propagate to all synchronized clones.
3. The dynamic watcher for `v1/configmaps` should remain alive (or be recreated) after processing UpdateRequests.

## Kyverno logs

Watcher lifecycle after the background controller restart shows rapid start/stop cycling — each UR processing iteration creates a watcher that immediately dies:

```
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z TRC generate_controller.go:83 > start processing UR policy=sync-test-config ur=ur-cq4nr
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z TRC generate_controller.go:83 > start processing UR policy=sync-test-config ur=ur-gddsj
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z TRC dynamic_watcher.go:85  > processing generated resource gvr="/v1, Resource=configmaps" name=test-config
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z TRC dynamic_watcher.go:339 > start watcher ... resourceVersion=2077
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z INF dynamic_watcher.go:377 > Resource added  name=test-config
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z TRC dynamic_watcher.go:85  > processing generated resource gvr="/v1, Resource=configmaps" name=test-config
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z TRC dynamic_watcher.go:90  > watcher already exists for GVR gvr="/v1, Resource=configmaps"
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z TRC dynamic_watcher.go:85  > processing generated resource gvr="/v1, Resource=configmaps" name=test-config
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z TRC dynamic_watcher.go:339 > start watcher ... resourceVersion=2081
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z INF dynamic_watcher.go:470 > Resource deleted  name=test-config
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z TRC dynamic_watcher.go:371 > watcher stopped  resourceVersion=2077
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z INF dynamic_watcher.go:470 > Resource deleted  name=test-config
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z TRC dynamic_watcher.go:371 > watcher stopped  resourceVersion=2081
... (continues for ~20 iterations over 5 seconds, resourceVersion climbing 2077 → 2194)
2026-05-07T22:06:40Z TRC dynamic_watcher.go:371 > watcher stopped  resourceVersion=2194
```

Note the `watcher already exists for GVR` log line at `dynamic_watcher.go:90`. The dead entry from a previously stopped watcher is still in the `dynamicWatchers` map, so `SyncWatchers` skips creating a replacement.

After the final `watcher stopped`, no new watcher is ever created. No `Resource updated` events appear after the cycling completes — confirming the watcher is permanently dead and source changes are never observed.

title: [Bug] Trouble installing Kyverno Helm Chart version: 3.8.0 # App Version v1.18.0
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.18.0

### Description

1. I had to explicitly pass in the image tags for the various components
      - chart _image.tpl fails typeIs "string" check on null tag defaults
      - test.image initContainer passes null as defaultTag instead of Chart.AppVersion
      - circular init container dependency between reports-server and admission controller
```
apiVersion: helm.crossplane.io/v1beta1
kind: Release
metadata:
  name: staging-kyverno
  annotations:
    crossplane.io/external-name: kyverno
spec:
  providerConfigRef:
    name: staging-helm-to-eks
  forProvider:
    chart:
      name: kyverno
      repository: https://kyverno.github.io/kyverno/
      # WARNING: 3.7.0 has broken arm64: https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/issues/15188
      # version: 3.6.2 # App version v1.16.2. (January 9, 2026): https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/charts/kyverno/Chart.yaml
      # WARNING: 3.8.0 requires explicit image tags and probe tuning due to chart bugs:
      #   - chart _image.tpl fails typeIs "string" check on null tag defaults
      #   - test.image initContainer passes null as defaultTag instead of Chart.AppVersion
      #   - circular init container dependency between reports-server and admission controller
      #   - reports-server acts as aggregated API server, requires SubjectAccessReview on every
      #     probe hit which needs generous timeoutSeconds to avoid liveness kill loop
      version: 3.8.0 # App Version v1.18.0 (April 29, 2026): https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/release-1.18/charts/kyverno/Chart.yaml
    namespace: kyverno
    values:
      installCRDs: true
      admissionController:
        image:
          tag: "v1.18.0" # Required: chart _image.tpl fails typeIs "string" check on null default
      crds:
        install: true
      reportsServer:
        enabled: true
        image:
          tag: "v1.18.0" # Required: null tag default fails typeIs "string" check
      reportsController:
        image:
          tag: "v1.18.0" # Required: null tag default fails typeIs "string" check
      test:
        image:
          tag: "v1.18.0" # Required: actual root cause - initContainer passes null as defaultTag instead of Chart.AppVersion
    # NOTE: This chart has a lot of options including Monitoring, which we should enable in the future.
```
2.  Title: reportsServer liveness/readiness probes crash loop due to SubjectAccessReview timeout in webhook authorization mode (chart v3.8.0)
Describe the bug
When reportsServer.enabled: true is set in the Kyverno Helm chart v3.8.0, the reports-server enters a crash loop caused by liveness and readiness probe timeouts. The root cause is that the reports-server operates as a Kubernetes aggregated API server using webhook authorization mode. In this mode, every incoming request — including kubelet health check probes — triggers a SubjectAccessReview (SAR) call back to the kube-apiserver to authorize the request.
Under any apiserver load or during initialization, the SAR call is canceled before it completes. The /livez and /readyz handlers return no response, the kubelet fails the liveness probe, and the pod is restarted. Because all other Kyverno components (admission controller, background controller, cleanup controller, reports controller) have a wait-for-reports-server init container, they are all blocked from starting, taking down the entire Kyverno stack.
To Reproduce

Install Kyverno chart v3.8.0 with reportsServer.enabled: true
Observe reports-server entering crash loop immediately after startup
Observe all other Kyverno components stuck in Init state
Check reports-server logs — every /livez and /readyz request shows:

Failed to make webhook authorizer request: Post "https://<apiserver>:443/apis/authorization.k8s.io/v1/subjectaccessreviews?timeout=10s": context canceled
post-timeout activity - GET "/livez" result: <nil>
Expected behavior
Health check endpoints /livez and /readyz should not require authorization. The reports-server deployment should include --authorization-always-allow-paths=/metrics,/livez,/readyz by default, consistent with how other aggregated API servers such as metrics-server handle probe authorization.
Actual behavior
The default deployment args only include --authorization-always-allow-paths=/metrics, omitting /livez and /readyz. Every probe hit triggers a SAR call that times out under load, causing a permanent crash loop.
Workaround
Patch the reports-server deployment to add /livez and /readyz to --authorization-always-allow-paths:
--authorization-always-allow-paths=/metrics,/livez,/readyz
Proposed fix
Either update the default args in the reports-server deployment template to include /livez and /readyz in --authorization-always-allow-paths, or expose reportsServer.extraArgs in the chart values schema so users can configure this without a post-render patch.
Environment

Kyverno chart version: 3.8.0
Kyverno app version: v1.18.0
Kubernetes version: v1.20.12 (EKS)
Cloud provider: AWS EKS

title: [Bug] admissionController crashes due to unconditional v1alpha1.MutatingAdmissionPolicy informer cache sync
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.2

### Description

The admission controller fails to start on Kubernetes 1.34+ because it unconditionally registers and waits for cache sync of `v1alpha1.MutatingAdmissionPolicy`, which was promoted to v1beta1 in Kubernetes 1.34. The controller exits with a fatal error regardless of the --generateMutatingAdmissionPolicy flag value.

To Reproduce

Run Kyverno chart v3.7.2 (v1.17.2) on a Kubernetes 1.34 cluster
Observe admission controller pod stuck in 0/1 / CrashLoopBackOff

The admission controller should either:

Conditionally register the MutatingAdmissionPolicy informer only when --generateMutatingAdmissionPolicy=true, or
Use v1beta1.MutatingAdmissionPolicy on clusters that serve it (with version discovery), or
Gracefully skip cache sync for APIs not served by the cluster


In my setup, the admission controller crashes at startup:
```

ERR k8s.io/client-go@v0.35.1/tools/cache/reflector.go:204 > Failed to watch error="failed to list *v1alpha1.MutatingAdmissionPolicy: the server could not find the requested resource"
ERR k8s.io/client-go@v0.35.1/tools/cache/reflector.go:204 > Failed to watch error="failed to list *v1alpha1.MutatingAdmissionPolicyBinding: the server could not find the requested resource"
ERR github.com/kyverno/kyverno/cmd/internal/informer.go:30 > failed to wait for cache sync type=*v1alpha1.MutatingAdmissionPolicy
ERR github.com/kyverno/kyverno/cmd/internal/informer.go:30 > failed to wait for cache sync type=*v1alpha1.MutatingAdmissionPolicyBinding
ERR github.com/kyverno/kyverno/cmd/kyverno/main.go:634 > failed to wait for cache sync error="failed to wait for cache sync"
```

Note that the feature flag has no effect. With --generateMutatingAdmissionPolicy=false the informer is still registered and the cache sync is still waited on:

```
$ kubectl get deploy -n kyverno kyverno-admission-controller -o yaml | grep -i generate
        - --generateValidatingAdmissionPolicy=true
        - --generateMutatingAdmissionPolicy=false
```


I can see that this was also reported on the community Slack channel twice:

https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/CLGR9BJU9/p1773749540483199

https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/CLGR9BJU9/p1771597927193229

I was supposed to be fixed in v1.17.2 by https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/issues/15364, but I think that this change was not cherry picked (https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pull/15799#issuecomment-4225272525)

With Kyverno v1.18, the deployment works fine, on the same setup.

Cherry picking the changes would probably solve the issue.

https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/CLGR9BJU9/p1773749540483199, https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/CLGR9BJU9/p1771597927193229

title: [Bug] ImageValidatingPolicy CEL evaluation produces no logs even at --v=6
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.18.0

### Kubernetes Version

1.35.x

### Kubernetes Platform

EKS

### Kyverno Rule Type

verifyImages

### Description

When debugging `ImageValidatingPolicy` failures, there are no logs for CEL function execution (`verifyImageSignatures()`, `verifyAttestationSignatures()`), even with Kyverno admission controller log level set to `-v=6`.
This makes it impossible to debug why `ImageValidatingPolicy` CEL functions return unexpected results (in our case, returning 0 when signatures/attestations exist).
In contrast, `ClusterPolicy` (legacy API) produces extensive verification logs at the same verbosity level.

_Any chance ImageValidatingPolicy CEL functions are evaluated by Kubernetes API server's ValidatingAdmissionPolicy controller rather than Kyverno's admission controller? If this is the case, documentation should clarify where to find these logs for troubleshooting._

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set Kyverno admission controller to `-v=6`:
    ```
    helm upgrade kyverno kyverno/kyverno -n kyverno --reuse-values --set features.logging.verbosity=6
   ```
2. Create an ImageValidatingPolicy:
    ```yaml
    apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
    kind: ImageValidatingPolicy
    metadata:
      name: test-image-verification
    spec:
      validationActions: [Audit]
      matchConstraints:
        resourceRules:
        - apiGroups: ['']
          apiVersions: ['v1']
          operations: [CREATE]
          resources: [pods]
      matchImageReferences:
      - glob: 'myregistry.io/*'
      credentials:
        allowInsecureRegistry: false
        providers:
          - amazon
      attestors:
      - name: kms
        cosign:
          ctlog:
            insecureIgnoreTlog: true
          key:
            kms: 'awskms:///alias/my-key'
      validations:
      - expression: |
          images.containers.map(image, verifyImageSignatures(image, [attestors.kms])).all(result, result > 0)
        message: "Image must be signed"
    ```
3. Create a test pod that matches the policy
4. Search Kyverno admission controller logs:
    ```
    kubectl logs -n kyverno deployment/kyverno-admission-controller | grep -i "test-image-verification\|verifyImageSignatures\|cel"
    ```

### Expected behavior

Should see logs similar to ClusterPolicy verification, such as:
  - CEL expression evaluation start
  - Calling verifyImageSignatures() function
  - Image verification attempts
  - Function return values
  - Expression evaluation result

  Example of what ClusterPolicy shows:
```jsonl
{"message":"verifying image signatures"}
{"message":"cosign verifier built","ignoreTlog":true}
{"message":"image attestors verification succeeded","verifiedCount":1}
```

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Kyverno logs
None, except this one:
```json
{"logger":"EventGenerator","kind":"ImageValidatingPolicy","name":"test-image-verification","reason":"PolicyViolation","note":"[test-image-verification] fail; Image must be signed"}
```

title: [Bug] IVPOL demands Rekor URL when InsecureIgnoreTlog: true
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.18.0

### Kubernetes Version

1.35.x

### Kubernetes Platform

GKE

### Kyverno Rule Type

verifyImages

### Description

When applying an `ImageValidatingPolicy` that sets `ctlog.insecureIgnoreTlog: true` but does **not** set `ctlog.url`, the policy is rejected with `getting Rekor public keys: rekor URL must be provided`.

This is inconsistent with the behaviour of `ClusterPolicy` `verifyImages`, which accepts the same combination — `insecureIgnoreTlog: true` + no `url` — and skips the Rekor client setup entirely (since the user has explicitly opted out of Rekor verification).

The mismatch matters in practice for anyone using IVPOL against an out-of-tree TSA — for example, GitHub Actions Artifact Attestations on private repositories use GitHub's private TSA and have **no Rekor entry by design**. There is no real `rekor.url` to provide. The current behaviour forces users to embed a placeholder URL like `https://rekor.sigstore.dev` in their policy purely to satisfy validation; the placeholder is never contacted but it leaks implementation detail into user-facing CRs and creates confusion about whether Rekor is actually being used.

The corresponding CPOL `verifyImages` policy works correctly today.


### Steps to reproduce


1. Apply an `ImageValidatingPolicy` with `ctlog.insecureIgnoreTlog: true` and no `ctlog.url`. Minimal example:

   ```yaml
   apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
   kind: ImageValidatingPolicy
   metadata:
     name: verify-keyless-no-rekor
   spec:
     validationActions: [Audit]
     matchConstraints:
       resourceRules:
         - apiGroups: [""]
           apiVersions: [v1]
           operations: [CREATE, UPDATE]
           resources: [pods]
     attestors:
       - name: gh
         cosign:
           keyless:
             identities:
               - issuer: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
                 subjectRegExp: https://github.com/example-org/.*/\.github/workflows/.*
           ctlog:
             insecureIgnoreSCT: true
             insecureIgnoreTlog: true
             # No url — the user has explicitly opted out of Rekor.
             # GitHub-attested images on private repos have no Rekor entry.
     attestations:
       - name: provenance
         intoto:
           type: https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1
   ```

2. Observe the policy is rejected at admission time.

3. Workaround that demonstrates the bug-vs-intent gap: add `url: https://rekor.sigstore.dev` to the `ctlog` block. The policy is accepted and verification proceeds — even though the placeholder URL is never contacted because `insecureIgnoreTlog: true` is set.

4. The same `ctlog` configuration on a `ClusterPolicy` `verifyImages` rule is accepted without the placeholder URL.


### Expected behavior

When `ctlog.insecureIgnoreTlog: true` is set, the policy should be accepted regardless of whether `ctlog.url` is present. The user has explicitly opted out of Rekor verification; a URL that will never be contacted should not be required.

This matches:

- the behaviour of `ClusterPolicy` `verifyImages` today, which gates Rekor client setup behind `!ignoreTlog`
- the natural reading of `insecureIgnoreTlog: true` ("ignore Rekor entirely")
