title: [Bug] Leader election starved by global client-go rate limits during cold start with multiple replicas of admission controller
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.2

### Description

## Summary

Kyverno controller pods enter CrashLoopBackOff after a `kubectl rollout restart` when running multiple replicas. The pods successfully acquire the leader lease but lose it ~36 seconds later because informer LIST bursts exhaust the shared client-go rate limiter, preventing lease renewal PUT requests from executing within their context deadline.

## Environment

- Cloud Provider: AKS
- Kyverno version: `v1.17.1`
- Replicas: 3 per controller (admission-controller, controlled by HPA with `minReplicas=3`)
- CRD count: ~15+ Kyverno CRD types, ~1936 policyreports, plus admissionreports, backgroundscanreports, ephemeralreports, etc.

## How to Reproduce

This is admittedly not super straightforward to reproduce on a laptop with something like `kind`. I think you could drop `--clientRateLimitQPS` to something around 2-5 and `--clientRateLimitBurst` to 10-20, then:

- Run 3 replicas
- Install a large volume of policies and get the Informer to register a high volume of watches on the API
- Run `kubectl rollout restart` on the admission controller Deployment

## Symptoms

```
2026-04-29T22:31:31Z TRC starting controller name=ttl-controller-manager workers=3
2026-04-29T22:32:07Z ERR Failed to update lease optimistically, falling back to slow path
    error="Put \"https://10.0.0.1:443/.../leases/kyverno-cleanup-controller\": context deadline exceeded"
2026-04-29T22:32:07Z ERR Error retrieving lease lock
    error="client rate limiter Wait returned an error: context deadline exceeded"
2026-04-29T22:32:07Z INF Failed to renew lease err="context deadline exceeded"
2026-04-29T22:32:07Z TRC leadership lost, stopped leading
```

In that 30-something second period, there appears to be a large burst in QPS that occurs, at which point the leader lease is lost.

## Workarounds

For now, it's probably just increasing the values for `clientRateLimitQPS` and `clientRateLimitBurst`

title: ImageValidatingPolicy: UNAUTHORIZED to access Harbor repository despite valid imagePullSecrets and working cosign
body:
### Kyverno Version

***

**Title:** ImageValidatingPolicy: UNAUTHORIZED to access Harbor repository despite valid imagePullSecrets and working cosign

```markdown
### Kyverno Version

v1.17.0 (chart kyverno-3.7.0, admission controller image `reg.kyverno.io/kyverno/kyverno:v1.17.0`)

### Kubernetes Version

(please fill in, e.g.) v1.27.x

### Kubernetes Platform

(please fill in) Bare metal / kOps / EKS / etc.

### Kyverno Policy Type

ImageValidatingPolicy (image verification library)

---

### Description

When using an ImageValidatingPolicy with Cosign attestor against a private Harbor registry, Kyverno fails image verification with an `UNAUTHORIZED` error when trying to GET the image manifest. At the same time:

- `cosign verify` with the same public key and Harbor robot account **succeeds**.
- A regular Kubernetes Pod can **pull** the same image using the same imagePullSecret.
- Kyverno admission controller is started with `--imagePullSecrets=<my-secret>` and has RBAC permissions to read secrets.

This looks very similar to existing issues with `verifyImages` and Harbor, but for the new ImageValidatingPolicy/image verification library. [web:53][web:20][web:71][web:39]

---

### Setup Details

#### Registry

- Harbor at `https://aispi-harbor.nces.by`
- Project: `aispi`
- Repository: `aispi/security-webhook`
- Image: `aispi-harbor.nces.by/aispi/security-webhook:1.2`
- Signed with Cosign using:

```bash
IMAGE_URL="aispi-harbor.nces.by/aispi/security-webhook:1.2"
export COSIGN_PASSWORD="123456"

cosign sign --key cosign.key \
  --registry-username='robot$aispi+kyverno' \
  --registry-password='1111111111111111' \
  "${IMAGE_URL}"
```

`cosign verify --key cosign.pub "${IMAGE_URL}"` succeeds. [web:94][web:131]

#### Harbor Robot Account

- Name: `robot$aispi+kyverno`
- Has permission to pull from `aispi/security-webhook`.

#### Kubernetes Secret

Namespace: `kyverno`

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: harbor-aispi-robot
  namespace: kyverno
type: kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson
data:
  .dockerconfigjson: 
```

Decoded `.dockerconfigjson`:

```json
{
  "auths": {
    "aispi-harbor.nces.by": {
      "username": "robot$aispi+kyverno",
      "password": "**",
      "email": "robot@aispi-harbor.local",
      "auth": "..."
    }
  }
}
```

#### Kyverno Helm Values (relevant part)

```yaml
admissionController:
  container:
    extraArgs:
      v: "4"

imageVerification:
  imagePullSecrets: {}
  existingImagePullSecrets:
    - harbor-aispi-robot
```

Kyverno admission controller Deployment:

```yaml
containers:
- name: kyverno
  args:
    - --imagePullSecrets=harbor-aispi-robot
    - --allowInsecureRegistry=false
    - --registryCredentialHelpers=default,google,amazon,azure,github
    - --enableReporting=validate,mutate,mutateExisting,imageVerify,generate
    - --v=4
  image: reg.kyverno.io/kyverno/kyverno:v1.17.0
  ...
```

#### RBAC

ServiceAccount: `system:serviceaccount:kyverno:kyverno-admission-controller`

Role in `kyverno` namespace (simplified):

```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: kyverno-image-verification-secrets
  namespace: kyverno
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["secrets"]
    verbs: ["get", "list"]
***
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: kyverno-image-verification-secrets
  namespace: kyverno
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Role
  name: kyverno-image-verification-secrets
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: kyverno-admission-controller
    namespace: kyverno
```

After adding this RBAC, the previous `forbidden` error for reading the secret disappeared. [file:122][web:115]

---

### ImageValidatingPolicy

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: ImageValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: verify-security-webhook-image
spec:
  webhookConfiguration:
    timeoutSeconds: 30

  validationActions:
    - Deny

  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
        resources: ["pods"]

  matchImageReferences:
    - glob: "aispi-harbor.nces.by/aispi/security-webhook:*"

  credentials:
    secrets:
      - harbor-aispi-robot

  attestors:
    - name: cosign
      cosign:
        key:
          hashAlgorithm: sha256
          data: |
            -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
            MFkwEwYHKoZIzj0CAQYIKoZIzj0DAQcDQgAEsQQeb08W4QYGX3dQh39vXGY2NjVM
            EAp9BtPu3b/VGUTwYA0qReO21nXLNA9X5BXdpA8cK0Fuk1BwecShqcNxxA==
            -----END PUBLIC KEY-----
        source:
          repository: "aispi-harbor.nces.by/aispi/security-webhook"

  validationConfigurations:
    required: true
    mutateDigest: false
    verifyDigest: false

  validations:
    - expression: >-
        object.metadata.namespace != "security-webhooks" ||
        images.containers
          .filter(image, image.startsWith("aispi-harbor.nces.by/aispi/security-webhook:"))
          .map(image, verifyImageSignatures(image, [attestors.cosign]))
          .all(result, result > 0)
      message: "image aispi-harbor.nces.by/aispi/security-webhook must have a valid cosign signature"
```

Policy validates fine on creation; the error only appears during evaluation for a Pod in `security-webhooks` namespace. [page:1][web:39]

---

### What Works

1. **cosign verify**

```bash
COSIGN_PASSWORD=... \
COSIGN_DOCKER_USERNAME='robot$aispi+kyverno' \
COSIGN_DOCKER_PASSWORD='11111111111111111' \
cosign verify --key cosign.pub \
  aispi-harbor.nces.by/aispi/security-webhook:1.2
```

→ succeeds, signature is found and valid. [web:94]

2. **Kubernetes Pod with the same imagePullSecret**

```bash
kubectl run test-pull \
  --image=aispi-harbor.nces.by/aispi/security-webhook:1.2 \
  --restart=Never \
  --overrides='{
    "apiVersion":"v1",
    "kind":"Pod",
    "metadata":{"name":"test-pull"},
    "spec":{
      "securityContext":{
        "runAsNonRoot": true,
        "seccompProfile":{"type":"RuntimeDefault"}
      },
      "containers":[
        {
          "name":"c",
          "image":"aispi-harbor.nces.by/aispi/security-webhook:1.2",
          "securityContext":{
            "allowPrivilegeEscalation": false,
            "runAsNonRoot": true,
            "seccompProfile":{"type":"RuntimeDefault"},
            "capabilities":{"drop":["ALL"]}
          }
        }
      ],
      "imagePullSecrets":[{"name":"harbor-aispi-robot"}]
    }
  }'
```

`kubectl describe pod test-pull` shows:

```text
Normal  Pulled  ...  Container image "aispi-harbor.nces.by/aispi/security-webhook:1.2" already present on machine
Warning Failed ...  Error: container has runAsNonRoot and image will run as root
```

No `ErrImagePull` or `UNAUTHORIZED` from kubelet; the image pull succeeds. [web:166][web:165]

---

### What Fails

Deploying a workload in `security-webhooks` that uses the image triggers the ImageValidatingPolicy and fails admission:

```bash
kubectl -n security-webhooks rollout restart deploy securitycontext-validator
```

Error:

```text
error: failed to patch: admission webhook "ivpol.validate.kyverno.svc-fail-finegrained-verify-security-webhook-image" denied the request:
Policy verify-security-webhook-image error:
failed to evaluate policy:
GET https://aispi-harbor.nces.by/v2/aispi/security-webhook/manifests/1.2:
UNAUTHORIZED: unauthorized to access repository: aispi/security-webhook, action: pull:
unauthorized to access repository: aispi/security-webhook, action: pull
```

Kyverno logs (with `--v=4`):

```text
2026-04-28T12:41:31Z ... ivpol/evaluator ... "message":
"failed to evaluate policy: GET https://aispi-harbor.nces.by/v2/aispi/security-webhook/manifests/1.2:
UNAUTHORIZED: unauthorized to access repository: aispi/security-webhook, action: pull:
unauthorized to access repository: aispi/security-webhook, action: pull",
"status":"error","emitWarning":true}
```

Prior to adding RBAC for secrets, I also saw:

```text
secrets "harbor-aispi-robot" is forbidden:
User "system:serviceaccount:kyverno:kyverno-admission-controller" cannot get resource "secrets" at the cluster scope
```

After adding the Role/RoleBinding in `kyverno` namespace, the `forbidden` error disappeared, but `UNAUTHORIZED` remains. [file:122][web:115]

---

### Expected Behavior

Given that:

- Kyverno admission controller is configured with `--imagePullSecrets=harbor-aispi-robot`.
- ImageValidatingPolicy uses `credentials.secrets: [harbor-aispi-robot]`.
- The same secret allows kubelet to pull the image.
- Cosign verify succeeds with the same Harbor robot credentials.

I would expect the image verification library to authenticate successfully to Harbor and either:

- find and verify the Cosign signature, or  
- return a signature-related error (e.g. `no signatures found`), but **not** an `UNAUTHORIZED` from Harbor.

---

### Additional Context

This looks similar to issues #6673 and #7699 where verify images against a private Harbor registry fails with `UNAUTHORIZED` even though cosign and kubelet work. [web:53][web:20][web:71]  

The main difference is that I'm using the new ImageValidatingPolicy with the image verification library instead of the legacy `verifyImages`. The behavior suggests that:

- `--imagePullSecrets` and/or `credentials.secrets` are not being applied correctly by the image verification library when contacting Harbor, or
- there is a mismatch in how the dockerconfig is interpreted (hostname/URL) between kubelet and Kyverno.
```

***

### Slack discussion

title: [Bug] [CLI] Fails offline for CEL/ValidatingPolicy when resources include CRDs
body:
### Kyverno CLI Version

1.17.1

### Description

We run `kyverno apply` in offline mode against rendered manifests (YAML file) as part of a CI linter. This worked reliably with classic Kyverno policies, but after migrating policies to CEL-based ValidatingPolicy, the CLI now fails whenever the input manifests include Custom Resources (e.g., External Secrets or VPA).

The failure happens even though the CR objects are present in the input file. The CLI errors out while trying to map GVK → GVR and reports “no matches for kind …”, which normally requires Kubernetes API discovery. In our CI environment we intentionally do not have cluster access, so we need an offline-friendly behavior.

This looks the same class of problem as other CLI/CEL + CRD mapping issues (for example kyverno/kyverno#15384), but in our case it happens with kyverno apply (not kyverno test).

Environment / Context
Use case: CI linter for GitOps apps (Argo CD)
Manifest source: argocd app manifests ... output saved to a file
Kyverno invocation: kyverno apply <policies> --resource <manifest.yaml> --detailed-results
No cluster access: cannot use --cluster against a real kube-apiserver
Input resources include CRDs (e.g. ExternalSecret, VerticalPodAutoscaler)

### Steps to reproduce

1. 
```
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  labels:
    argocd.argoproj.io/instance: test-staging
  name: mtest-secrets
  namespace: test
spec:
  dataFrom:
  - extract:
      key: /test
  refreshInterval: 5m
  secretStoreRef:
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
    name: ssm-secret-store
  target:
    name: test-secrets
    template:
      metadata:
        annotations:
          konghq.com/basic-auth-credential: "true"
        labels:
          konghq.com/credential: basic-auth
```
2.Prepare a CEL-based Kyverno policy set (ValidatingPolicy) that is applied using kyverno apply (directory or file).

```
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: ValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-requests-limits
  annotations:
    policies.kyverno.io/title: Require Limits and Requests
    policies.kyverno.io/category: Best Practices
    policies.kyverno.io/description: >-
      As application workloads share cluster resources, it is important to limit resources
      requested and consumed by each pod. It is recommended to require 'resources.requests'
      and 'resources.limits.memory' per pod. If a namespace level request or limit is specified,
      defaults will automatically be applied to each pod based on the 'LimitRange' configuration.
spec:
  failurePolicy: Ignore
  validationActions:
    - Deny
  autogen:
    podControllers:
      controllers:
        - deployments
        - daemonsets
        - statefulsets
        - cronjobs
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: ['']
        apiVersions: ['v1']
        operations: [CREATE, UPDATE]
        resources: ['pods']
  variables:
    - name: containers
      expression: >-
        object.spec.containers
  validations:
    - expression: >-
        variables.containers.all(c,
          has(c.resources) && has(c.resources.requests) &&
          has(c.resources.requests.memory) && c.resources.requests.memory != '' &&
          has(c.resources.requests.cpu) && c.resources.requests.cpu != '' &&
          has(c.resources.limits) && has(c.resources.limits.memory) && c.resources.limits.memory != ''
        )
      message: "CPU and memory resource requests and limits are required."
```

3. In our real setup, this came from migrating legacy ClusterPolicy rules to CEL/ValidatingPolicy.
Run kyverno apply offline against the manifest file:
`kyverno apply ./policies --resource=helm-manifest.yaml --detailed-results`

4. Output:
```
╰─ kyverno apply ./policies/require-requests-limits.yaml --resource=helm-manifest.yaml --detailed-results                                                                                                                ─╯

Applying 1 policy rule(s) to 1 resource(s)...
Error: failed to apply policies on resource mtest-secrets (failed to map gvk to gvr external-secrets.io/v1, Kind=ExternalSecret (no matches for kind "ExternalSecret" in version "external-secrets.io/v1")
)
```

### Expected behavior

In offline mode (resources loaded from local YAML), we expect one of the following:

- Kyverno CLI can evaluate CEL/ValidatingPolicy policies without requiring Kubernetes API discovery for CRDs, or
- Kyverno CLI provides a way to supply CRD information locally (e.g., `--crd-dir`, `--openapi,` or similar) so    GVK→GVR mapping works offline, or
- At minimum, Kyverno CLI should not hard-fail on GVK→GVR mapping when the resource is already fully provided as YAML input (unless the policy explicitly requires live API lookups).

Please advise if:

- offline CRD mapping for kyverno apply is expected to work for CEL/ValidatingPolicy,
- there is an existing flag or recommended pattern to provide CRD discovery offline,
- or this is a known limitation/bug to be addressed.

Why this matters
Many CI pipelines lint rendered manifests without cluster access (for security/isolation). Migrating to CEL-based ValidatingPolicy is recommended, but currently this breaks offline linting when apps contain CRDs.

title: [Bug] Duplicate CRDs rendered by both crds subchart and kyverno-api dependency cause ArgoCD warnings
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.0

### Description

## Kyverno Version

1.17.0

## Kubernetes Version

1.33 (OpenShift 4.20.16)

## Kubernetes Platform

Red Hat OpenShift 4.20.16

## Kyverno Helm Chart Version

3.7.0

## Description

The `kyverno` Helm chart declares two dependencies in `Chart.yaml` that both
render the same set of CRDs in the `policies.kyverno.io` API group:

1. The local `crds` subchart (at `charts/kyverno-crds/`)
2. The external `kyverno-api` chart from `https://kyverno.github.io/api`

Both dependencies are gated by the single `crds.install` condition, so any user
who installs the chart with the default `crds.install: true` gets every CRD in
`policies.kyverno.io` rendered twice.

For plain `helm install`/`helm upgrade` with client-side apply this is silent
(the later one overwrites the earlier), so the bug is invisible to most users.
However, ArgoCD parses rendered manifests into a resource graph and surfaces a
warning for every duplicated resource:

> Resource apiextensions.k8s.io/CustomResourceDefinition//deletingpolicies.policies.kyverno.io appeared 2 times among application resources.

This warning fires for every CRD in the `policies.kyverno.io` group
(`deletingpolicies`, `generatingpolicies`, `imagevalidatingpolicies`,
`mutatingpolicies`, `validatingpolicies`, the `namespaced*` variants, and
`policyexceptions`).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install the `kyverno` chart at version `<your version>` with default values,
   or via an ArgoCD Application pointing at `kyverno/kyverno`.
2. Run:
```bash
   helm template kyverno kyverno/kyverno --version <version> \
     | grep -B 20 "name: deletingpolicies.policies.kyverno.io"
```
3. Observe two `# Source:` lines for the same CRD, one from each subchart.

## Observed Output

```
helm template . > /tmp/kyverno-rendered.yaml
grep -n "name: deletingpolicies.policies.kyverno.io" /tmp/kyverno-rendered.yaml

49050:  name: deletingpolicies.policies.kyverno.io
69519:  name: deletingpolicies.policies.kyverno.io
```

## Expected Behavior

Each CRD should be rendered exactly once. Either:

- The `crds` subchart and `kyverno-api` dependency should partition CRDs
  cleanly by API group (e.g. `crds` renders only `kyverno.io` /
  `reports.kyverno.io` / `wgpolicyk8s.io`, and `kyverno-api` renders only
  `policies.kyverno.io`), or
- One dependency should be authoritative for all CRDs and the other should
  not ship CRDs at all, or
- The `crds.groups.policies.*` toggles should actually disable the
  overlapping CRDs in both subcharts, not just one.

## Attempted Workarounds

- `skipCrds: true` on the ArgoCD Application — no effect (the CRDs are
  rendered as regular templates, not from a `crds/` directory).

## Impact

Any user deploying the chart via ArgoCD (a supported and commonly used method,
documented in the Kyverno platform notes) sees persistent warnings on their
Application. While both rendered copies are byte-identical and sync still
completes, the warnings are noise that obscure real issues and make it harder
to trust the Application's health status.

This is particularly visible on OpenShift clusters where ArgoCD (via the
Red Hat GitOps Operator) is a common deployment path.

## Environment

- Kubernetes: 1.33 (OpenShift 4.20.16)
- ArgoCD version: 3.3.2
- Install method: Helm via ArgoCD Application

title: [Bug] generateExisting and synchronize fail when update requests are too large for kubernetes database
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.1

### Description

In very large clusters `generateExisting` and `synchronize` policies that apply to a large number of objects will create very large `UpdateRequest`s that cannot be applied.

I believe that updates need to be batched into multiple `UpdateRequest`s when a large number of objects need to be created/modified.

A minimal example to quickly reproduce this:

Install kyverno:
```bash
helm repo add kyverno https://kyverno.github.io/kyverno/
helm repo update
helm install kyverno kyverno/kyverno -n kyverno --create-namespace
```

Create many namespaces:
```bash
N=10000

for i in $(seq -w 1 "$N"); do
  kubectl create namespace test-ns-${i} || true
done
```

Apply the following policy that generates a `ConfigMap` in every namespace:
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: generate-configmap-all-namespaces
spec:
  generateExisting: true
  rules:
    - name: generate-example-configmap
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Namespace
      generate:
        apiVersion: v1
        kind: ConfigMap
        name: example-configmap
        namespace: "{{request.object.metadata.name}}"
        synchronize: true
        data:
          data:
            key: value
```

Notice that no configmaps are created:
```bash
kubectl get configmaps -A | grep example-configmap
```

Observe in the logs that the UR failed to apply:
```bash
kubectl logs deploy/kyverno-background-controller -nkyverno
```
shows errors like:
```
2026-04-14T12:42:20Z ERR github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/policy/generate.go:34 > failed to create UR for generateExisting error="etcdserver: request is too large" logger=PolicyController/handleGenerate/generate-configmap-all-namespaces
2026-04-14T12:42:20Z ERR github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/policy/policy_controller.go:426 > failed to updateUR on generate policy update error="etcdserver: request is too large" logger=PolicyController/syncPolicy
2026-04-14T12:42:20Z ERR github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/policy/policy_controller.go:389 > failed to sync policy error="etcdserver: request is too large" key=kpol/generate-configmap-all-namespaces logger=PolicyController

title: [Bug] : GlobalContextEntry referencing non-existent CRD prevents all GCEs from loading in ValidatingPolicy
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.1

### Description

## GlobalContextEntry referencing non-existent CRD prevents all GCEs from loading

### Environment

- Kyverno v1.17.1 (Helm chart 3.7.1)
- Kubernetes 1.33+ (GKE)

### Description

When a `GlobalContextEntry` with `kubernetesResource` references a CRD that doesn't exist on the cluster, it prevents **all** GlobalContextEntry resources from being loaded into the admission controller's in-memory store — not just the one referencing the missing CRD.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy to a cluster that does **not** have the Gateway API (HTTPRoute CRD) installed but **does** have standard Ingress and Istio VirtualService CRDs.

2. Create three GlobalContextEntry resources:

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v2
kind: GlobalContextEntry
metadata:
  name: gctx-httproutes
spec:
  kubernetesResource:
    group: gateway.networking.k8s.io  # This CRD does NOT exist on the cluster
    version: v1
    resource: httproutes
---
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v2
kind: GlobalContextEntry
metadata:
  name: gctx-virtualservices
spec:
  kubernetesResource:
    group: networking.istio.io
    version: v1
    resource: virtualservices
---
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v2
kind: GlobalContextEntry
metadata:
  name: gctx-ingresses
spec:
  kubernetesResource:
    group: networking.k8s.io
    version: v1
    resource: ingresses
```

3. Create a ValidatingPolicy that references these GCEs:

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: ValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: test-gce-null
spec:
  failurePolicy: Ignore
  validationActions: [Deny]
  evaluation:
    background:
      enabled: false
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: ['networking.k8s.io']
        apiVersions: ['*']
        resources: ['ingresses']
        operations: ['CREATE', 'UPDATE']
  matchConditions:
    - name: scope
      expression: "true"
  variables:
    - name: allIngresses
      expression: "globalContext.Get('gctx-ingresses', '') != null ? globalContext.Get('gctx-ingresses', '') : []"
  validations:
    - expression: "size(variables.allIngresses) >= 0"
      message: "test"
```

4. Create an Ingress resource.

### Expected behavior

- `gctx-httproutes` fails to cache (CRD doesn't exist) and returns null — handled by the null check in the variable
- `gctx-ingresses` and `gctx-virtualservices` load normally and return cached resource data
- The policy evaluates successfully using available data

### Actual behavior

**All three** GCEs return nil — including `gctx-ingresses` which references a CRD that exists and has resources:

```
TRC pkg/cel/libs/context.go:87 > global context entry not found, returning nil entry=gctx-ingresses
TRC pkg/cel/libs/context.go:87 > global context entry not found, returning nil entry=gctx-httproutes
TRC pkg/cel/libs/context.go:87 > global context entry not found, returning nil entry=gctx-virtualservices
```

All GCEs show `lastRefreshTime: <none>` indefinitely.

Without the null-safe variable check, the policy hard-fails with:

```
failed to load context: got 'types.Null', expected iterable type
```

### What I've tried

- Restarting the admission controller — no change
- Restarting the background controller — no change
- Deleting only the broken GCE (`gctx-httproutes`) — other GCEs still don't load
- Deploying via GitOps (Flux) instead of `kubectl apply` — same result
- Verified same Kyverno version and identical config on a working cluster where all CRDs exist — works fine there

### Impact

One `GlobalContextEntry` referencing a non-existent CRD makes all GCEs on the cluster unusable. This forces us to exclude any policy using `GlobalContextEntry` from clusters that don't have all referenced CRDs installed, even if the policy would work fine with a subset of the data.

### Workaround

Exclude the policy and all associated `GlobalContextEntry` resources from clusters missing the CRD using Kustomize patches.

title: [Bug] `matchImageReferences` does not filter `images.containers` in ImageValidatingPolicy — all images are evaluated
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.0

### Kubernetes Version

1.33.x

### Kubernetes Platform

AKS

### Kyverno Rule Type

verifyImages

### Description

`matchImageReferences` in `ImageValidatingPolicy` does not filter images from the `images.containers` CEL variable. According to the API documentation in [`kyverno/api`](https://github.com/kyverno/api/blob/main/api/policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1/imagevalidating_policy.go):

> MatchImageReferences is a list of Glob and CELExpressions to match images.
> Any image that matches one of the rules is considered for validation.
> **Any image that does not match a rule is skipped, even when they are passed as arguments to image verification functions.**

However, in practice, **all images** in a pod are included in `images.containers` and evaluated by the `validations` expression, regardless of whether they match `matchImageReferences`. Non-matching images fail signature verification because they are not signed with the expected key, causing the policy to deny pods that should be unaffected.

### Root Cause

After tracing the source code, the issue is in [`pkg/imageverification/evaluator/policy.go`](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/pkg/imageverification/evaluator/policy.go) in the `Evaluate` method of `compiledPolicy`.

The `matchImageReferences` filter is only used to control which images get prefetched into the image context (`ictx.AddImages`), but `data[engine.ImagesKey]` (which populates `images.containers` in CEL) is set **before** the filtering and is **never modified**:

```go
// images is set BEFORE matchImageReferences filtering
images, err := engine.ExtractImages(data, c.imageExtractors)
data[engine.ImagesKey] = images  // <-- ALL images, unfiltered

// matchImageReferences only filters what gets added to ictx (registry prefetch)
imgList := []string{}
for _, v := range images {
    for _, img := range v {
        if apply, err := matching.MatchImage(img, c.matchImageReferences...); err != nil {
            return nil, err
        } else if apply {
            imgList = append(imgList, img)
        }
    }
}
if err := ictx.AddImages(ctx, imgList, ...); err != nil {
    return nil, err
}

// validations run against data which contains ALL images, not filtered ones
for i, v := range c.validations {
    out, _, err := v.Program.ContextEval(ctx, data)  // <-- uses unfiltered images
```

As a result, when a validation expression like `images.containers.map(image, verifyImageSignatures(image, [attestors.notary])).all(e, e > 0)` runs, it receives all images including ones that don't match `matchImageReferences`, causing policy validation failures for images that should have been skipped.

### Expected Fix

`data[engine.ImagesKey]` should be filtered by `matchImageReferences` before being passed to validation expressions, so that `images.containers` only contains images that match the policy's glob/CEL patterns.

### Workaround

Add a manual `.filter()` in the CEL validation expression:

```yaml
validations:
  - expression: >-
      images.containers
        .filter(image, image.contains("/myrepo/myapp"))
        .map(image, verifyImageSignatures(image, [attestors.notary]))
        .all(e, e > 0)
    message: "Image must be signed"
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an `ImageValidatingPolicy` with `matchImageReferences` scoped to specific images:

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: ImageValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: verify-image-signatures
spec:
  validationActions: [Deny]
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        resources: ["pods"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
  matchImageReferences:
    - glob: "*/myrepo/myapp*"
  attestors:
    - name: notary
      notary:
        certs:
          value: |
            -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
            ... (your signing certificate) ...
            -----END CERTIFICATE-----
  validations:
    - expression: >-
        images.containers.map(image,
        verifyImageSignatures(image, [attestors.notary])).all(e, e > 0)
      message: "Image must be signed"
```
2. Deploy a pod with a non-matching image:

```bash
kubectl run test-nginx --image=nginx:latest --dry-run=server
```



### Expected behavior

**Expected**: The pod should be allowed because `nginx:latest` does not match any `matchImageReferences` glob.

**Actual**: The pod is denied with the message "Image must be signed" because `nginx:latest` is included in `images.containers` and fails signature verification.

title: [Bug] `kyverno_policy_results` metric not emitted for ValidatingPolicy
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.1

### Description

## Summary

After migrating policies from `ClusterPolicy`/`Policy` to the new `ValidatingPolicy` format, the `kyverno_policy_results` metric is no longer populated. Only a duration histogram is emitted instead.

## Expected behavior

`kyverno_policy_results` is emitted for `ValidatingPolicy` results, with the same pass/fail/warn/error/skip label breakdown as for traditional policies.

## Actual behavior

No `kyverno_policy_results` data points are emitted. The only available metric for `ValidatingPolicy` is `kyverno_validating_policy_execution_duration_seconds`, which contains no result status breakdown.

## Root cause (investigation)

The new CEL-based policy types (`ValidatingPolicy`, `MutatingPolicy`, `ImageValidatingPolicy`, `GeneratingPolicy`) use a separate engine and metrics subsystem from traditional policies:

- **Traditional policies**: [`pkg/engine/engine.go` calls `metrics.RecordResponse()` → emits `kyverno_policy_results`](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/pkg/engine/engine.go#L102)
- **ValidatingPolicy**: [`pkg/cel/policies/vpol/engine/metrics.go` only records a duration histogram — `kyverno_policy_results` is never called](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/pkg/cel/policies/vpol/engine/metrics.go#L27)


## Question

**Is this by design?** Is `kyverno_policy_results` intentionally not supported for the new CEL-based policy types? Or is this an unintended gap that should be filled?

## Impact

Users migrating to `ValidatingPolicy` lose visibility into per-policy pass/fail/warn/error/skip counts, breaking existing dashboards and alerts that rely on `kyverno_policy_results`.

title: dpol: conditions cannot reference variables due to compilation order
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.15.2

### Description



## Body

The DeletingPolicy compiler compiles conditions before variables, so any condition that references variables.X fails at compile time with undefined field.

### Steps to Reproduce

Create a DeletingPolicy with variables referenced in conditions:

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1beta1
kind: DeletingPolicy
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  schedule: "* * * * *"
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        resources: ["configmaps"]
        operations: ["*"]
  variables:
    - name: targetEnv
      expression: '"test"'
  conditions:
    - name: check
      expression: 'variables.targetEnv == "test"'
```

Compilation fails with:

```
ERROR: <input>:1:10: undefined field 'targetEnv'
  variables.targetEnv == "test"
  .........^
```

### Root Cause

In `pkg/cel/policies/dpol/compiler/compiler.go`, conditions are compiled at line 72 and variables at line 78. The VariablesProvider (which registers variable names in the CEL type system) is populated by CompileVariables, but since conditions are compiled first, the provider doesn't know about any variable names yet.

### Expected Behavior

Conditions should be able to reference variables declared in the same policy (same as how vpol validations can reference variables).

### Suggested Fix

Swap the compilation order in compiler.go -- compile variables before conditions.

### Additional Context

Found while writing envtest integration tests for the dpol controller.

title: [Bug] ValidatingPolicy/MutatingPolicy webhook configuration updated every reconciliation cycle due to non-deterministic webhook ordering ?
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.1

### Kubernetes Version

1.33.x

### Kubernetes Platform

GKE

### Kyverno Rule Type

Validate

### Description

# Title

ValidatingPolicy/MutatingPolicy webhook configuration updated every reconciliation cycle due to non-deterministic webhook ordering

# Body

## Description

After deploying CEL-based ValidatingPolicies (`policies.kyverno.io/v1`), the `kyverno-resource-validating-webhook-cfg` ValidatingWebhookConfiguration is updated every ~15 seconds even when no policy changes have occurred. This causes policy `ready` status to oscillate between `true` and `false` when observed via `kubectl get -w`.

## Root Cause

The fine-grained webhook entries (one per policy with `matchConditions`) are written in non-deterministic order on each reconciliation cycle. This appears to be caused by Go map iteration ordering in the webhook construction code (`pkg/controllers/webhook/validating.go`).

Each cycle produces the same set of webhooks but in a different order → Kubernetes API server sees a change → increments `resourceVersion` → Kyverno detects the version change → reconciles again → infinite loop.

Additionally, `pkg/controllers/webhook/controller.go` in `reconcileValidatingWebhookConfiguration()` performs an unconditional update without comparing old vs new configuration.

## Evidence

### Webhook ordering changes every ~15 seconds

5 consecutive captures of the webhook names show the same 12 `finegrained` entries in different order each time:

```
Snapshot 1: policy-a, policy-b, policy-c, policy-d, ...
Snapshot 2: policy-b, policy-c, policy-d, policy-a, ...
Snapshot 3: policy-d, policy-a, policy-b, policy-c, ...
Snapshot 4: policy-a, policy-b, policy-c, policy-d, ...
Snapshot 5: policy-c, policy-a, policy-b, policy-d, ...
```

The first webhook (`validate.kyverno.svc-ignore`) and last two (`vpol...fail`, `vpol...ignore`) remain stable. Only the `finegrained` entries shuffle.

### Prometheus confirms continuous changes

```promql
sum by(cluster)(changes(kube_validatingwebhookconfiguration_metadata_resource_version{validatingwebhookconfiguration="kyverno-resource-validating-webhook-cfg"}[5m]))
```

Results over 30 days:
- **Before deploying ValidatingPolicies, we were on clusterpolicies**: 0 changes per 5 minutes
- **After deploying ValidatingPolicies**: 4 changes per 5 minutes (constant, 24/7)

### Enforcement is NOT affected

64 consecutive enforcement tests over 2 minutes during the oscillation period — all correctly blocked. The webhook stays registered regardless of status flapping.

## Environment

- Kyverno: v1.17.1
- Kubernetes: 1.33.x
- Number of ValidatingPolicies: ~30
- Number of MutatingPolicies: ~7
- Admission controller replicas: 3

## Expected Behavior

The webhook configuration should not be updated when no policies have changed. The `ready` status should remain stable at `true`.


## Impact

- **Enforcement**: Not sure it is impacted when status changes
- **API server load**: ~4 unnecessary writes/min per cluster
- **Monitoring**: Status flapping triggers false alerts
- **User confusion**: `ready: false` appears intermittently when watching policies


### Steps to reproduce

Deploy multiple validatingpolicy in cluster and try to see if policy status flaps

### Expected behavior

constant flapping should not happen

```

body:

### Description

The issue template forces me to enter a version, but I've actually tested this against the current main, which already includes the recent fixes for referencing the trigger object inside `mutations` expressions.

When using a MutatingPolicy that contains a `targetMatchExpression`, the policy will never be considered when also using `matchConditions` that try to reference the triggering object. These are my findings so far:

* When referencing `object` (like in `object.metadata.name`), the background-controller tries to match this expression against the target object. This seems like a bug in any way, because I cannot imagine anyone trying to use `matchConditions` this way. Maybe there should be a `targetMatchConditions`? * When referencing `request.object`, the admission-controller will always ignore the event, so it won't create `UpdateRequest` objects that would otherwise be picked up by the background-controller.

title: [Bug] GeneratingPolicy: generateExisting does not trigger for pre-existing resources
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.1

### Kubernetes Version

1.34.x

### Kubernetes Platform

EKS

### Kyverno Rule Type

Generate

### Description

When using GeneratingPolicy (policies.kyverno.io/v1) with spec.evaluation.generateExisting.enabled: true, Kyverno does not generate resources in namespaces that existed before the policy was applied.

The equivalent ClusterPolicy (kyverno.io/v1) with spec.generateExisting: true works correctly — the background controller creates UpdateRequest objects and generates the target resources in pre-existing namespaces within ~30 seconds of policy creation.

With GeneratingPolicy, no resources are generated in pre-existing namespaces. Resources ARE correctly generated when a new namespace is created after the policy exists (CREATE webhook trigger works), so generateExisting is effectively a no-op in the new API.

This is a regression: the same behaviour works correctly in ClusterPolicy on the same Kyverno version.

Related: #[14852](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/issues/14852) (skipBackgroundRequests support for GeneratingPolicy) is related but separate — this bug occurs independently of that field.

### Steps to reproduce

#### Environment

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Kyverno version | v1.17.1 |
| Helm chart version | 3.7.1 |
| Kubernetes version | v1.34.2-eks-ecaa3a6 |
| Cloud provider | AWS EKS |

#### Kyverno Components

```
kyverno-admission-controller    3 replicas   Running
kyverno-background-controller   2 replicas   Running
kyverno-cleanup-controller      2 replicas   Running
kyverno-reports-controller      2 replicas   Running
```

The following script reproduces the issue. It runs two isolated tests with different namespace prefixes to avoid cross-contamination:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Reproducer: generateExisting behavior difference between ClusterPolicy and GeneratingPolicy
# Kyverno version: v1.17.1 (Helm chart 3.7.1)
#
# Expected: Both policies should create a RoleBinding in a pre-existing namespace
# Actual:   ClusterPolicy works, GeneratingPolicy does not

set -euo pipefail

echo "======================================================"
echo " Kyverno generateExisting reproducer"
echo " Kyverno version: $(kubectl get deploy -n kyverno kyverno-admission-controller -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}' | cut -d: -f2)"
echo "======================================================"

# -------------------------------------------------------
# TEST 1: ClusterPolicy + generateExisting (OLD API)
# -------------------------------------------------------
echo ""

When a `GeneratingPolicy` with `spec.evaluation.generateExisting.enabled: true` is created, the background controller should:

1. Scan all existing resources matching `matchConstraints` + `matchConditions`
2. Create `UpdateRequest` objects for each matching resource
3. Generate the configured resources (RoleBinding) in those pre-existing namespaces

title: [Bug] Deleted cloned downstream secret is only recreated once
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.1

### Description

Hi,

I created a GeneratingPolicy to clone a secret from one namespace into others, similar to https://kyverno.io/docs/policy-types/generating-policy/#clone-single-resource. The only difference is that I added some label matching:
```
  matchConditions:

      expression: "object.metadata.?labels['foo.example.com/workload'].orValue('') == 'true'"

When I apply the policy and add the labels to the namespace the downstream secret gets created.

## Problem
When I deleted the downstream secret once, it gets recreated as expected and documented [here](https://kyverno.io/docs/policy-types/generating-policy/#synchronization-with-a-clone-source).

### Kyverno Version

1.17.1

### Description

A critical severity vulnerability (`Incorrect Authorization`) was found in `google.golang.org/grpc` bundled with Kyverno v1.17.1. This affects **all** Kyverno container images.

All images from `reg.kyverno.io/kyverno` at tag `v1.17.1` are affected:

title: [Bug] Broken and outdated ValidatingPolicy 'require-run-as-nonroot' in kyverno-policies Helm chart
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.1

### Description

The ValidatingPolicy resources within the `kyverno-policies` Helm chart should be updated with the latest working examples from the Kyverno Policies repository.

Example of a broken and outdated ValidatingPolicy:
- Broken: https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/charts/kyverno-policies/templates/restricted/require-run-as-nonroot.cel.yaml
- Working: https://github.com/kyverno/policies/blob/main/pod-security-vpol/restricted/require-run-as-nonroot/require-run-as-nonroot.yaml

The working policy from the Kyverno Policies repository has an optimized/simplified validation expression and actually performs the intended validation as documented in the validation message.

### To Reproduce
Install `kyverno` and `kyverno-policies` via Helm with the following versions:
- `kyverno` Helm chart: `3.7.1`
- `kyverno-policies` Helm chart: `3.7.1`
- Kubernetes version: `EKS v1.35`
- Installation method: Argo CD / Helm
- `kyverno-policies` values:
```
values:
  policyType: ValidatingPolicy
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  podSecurityStandard: restricted
```

### Expected behavior
If a pod defines only `.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot = true` but no securityContext within the container spec, it should still  pass the validation and be allowed to be scheduled.

As described in the policy message:
> Running as root is not allowed. Either the field spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot must be set to `true`, or the fields spec.containers[*].securityContext.runAsNonRoot, spec.initContainers[*].securityContext.runAsNonRoot, and spec.ephemeralContainers[*].securityContext.runAsNonRoot must be set to `true`.

### Actual behavior
The validation fails, unless the container also specify a securityContext with runAsNonRoot.

title: [Bug] MutatingPolicy with targetMatchConstraint uses matchConstraints object in ApplyConfiguration
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.14.5

### Kubernetes Version

1.35.x

### Kubernetes Platform

KinD

### Kyverno Rule Type

Mutate

### Description

When using a different trigger and target, the object in `ApplyConfiguration` is the trigger resource from `matchConstraints` rather than the target resource from `targetMatchConstraint`.

For example, when attempting to trigger on a ConfigMap, but update something within an object spec, the admission controller has the error: `failed to evaluate policy: error applying patch: failed to convert patch object to typed object: .spec: field not declared in schema`



### Steps to reproduce

I'm using the following `MutatingPolicy`, and updating a `kiali` object:

```
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: MutatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: kali-update-external-url
  annotations:
    policies.kyverno.io/title: Update Kali External URL
    policies.kyverno.io/category: Mutation
spec:
  evaluation:
    admission:
      enabled: true
    mutateExisting:
      enabled: true

  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups:
          - ""
        apiVersions:
          - v1
        resources:
          - configmaps
        operations:
          - CREATE
          - UPDATE
        resourceNames:
          - hostname-config
    namespaceSelector:
      matchLabels:
        kubernetes.io/metadata.name: istio-system

  targetMatchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups:
      - kiali.io
      apiVersions:
      - v1alpha1
      resources:
      - kialis
      operations:
      - CREATE
      - UPDATE
      resourceNames:
      - kiali

  variables:
  - name: hostname
    expression: >-
      resource.Get("v1", "configmaps", "istio-system", "hostname-config").data["hostname"]

  mutations:
  - patchType: ApplyConfiguration
    applyConfiguration:
      expression: >-
        Object{
          spec: Object.spec{
            external_services: Object.spec.external_services{
              grafana: Object.spec.external_services.grafana{
                external_url: "https://" + variables.hostname + "/grafana"
              }
            }
          }
        }
```

When updating the ConfigMap, the admission controller logs have an error as it's attempting to patch the ConfigMap rather than the Kiali.  See logs below.

### Expected behavior

`Object` in the `mutations` should refer to the target rather than the trigger.

body: ### Kyverno Version 1.17.1 (we see the issue since at least 1.16.1 in our logs) ### Description ## Setup We use kyverno in multiple Kubernetes clusters (currently Kubernetes v1.33) with backgroundScan enabled. ## Issue We see frequent crashes of the reports-controller with the following errors and stack traces (around 7k lines), causing a restart of the pod with exit code 2: - `fatal error: concurrent map writes` (see [stacktrace_concurrent-map-writes.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26050669/stacktrace_concurrent-map-writes.txt)) - `fatal error: concurrent map iteration and map write` (see [stacktrace_concurrent-map-iteration-and-map-write.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26050671/stacktrace_concurrent-map-iteration-and-map-write.txt)) Sometimes the pod restarts not only once but multiple times within a short time period. ## Troubleshooting - The issue did not occur when backgroundScan was disabled via `features.backgroundScan.enabled: false` - The issue did still occur when setting the `reportsController.featuresOverride.backgroundScan.backgroundScanWorkers: 1` In the image you can see all occurrences of `fatal error: concurrent` in the reports-controller logs within the last month in one of our Kubernetes clusters. title: [Bug] MutatingPolicy with targetMatchConstraints does not provide access to the original request object/oldObject
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.1

### Kubernetes Version

1.35.x

### Kubernetes Platform

EKS

### Kyverno Rule Type

Mutate

### Description

When migrating a `ClusterPolicy` that uses the [mutate existing resources](https://kyverno.io/docs/policy-types/mutating-policy/#mutating-existing-resources) pattern to the new CEL-based `MutatingPolicy` CRD with `targetMatchConstraints`, there is no way to access the object/oldObject from the original admission request that triggered the mutation.

When a `MutatingPolicy` with `targetMatchConstraints` is configured, execution is delegated to the `kyverno-background-controller`. In that context, `object` and `oldObject` refer to the **target** resource being mutated (e.g., a `ScaledObject`), not the resource that triggered the original admission request (e.g., a `ConfigMap`). In the legacy `ClusterPolicy`, this was addressed via the `target` variable, but no equivalent exists in the new `MutatingPolicy` CEL context.

This means policies that need to:
1. Filter execution based on properties of the triggering resource (via `matchConditions`)
2. Extract data from the triggering resource for use in mutations (via `variables`)

...cannot be expressed with the current `MutatingPolicy` API.

**Example use case:** A `ConfigMap` update triggers mutation of `ScaledObject` resources, where the policy needs to read data from the `ConfigMap` (the trigger) and apply it to the `ScaledObject` (the target). See: https://github.com/rodrigorfk/k8s-kyverno-mutating-policies/blob/main/src/examples/02-keda-prometheus-address/policy.yaml


### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a `MutatingPolicy` with `targetMatchConstraints` that references the triggering resource in `matchConditions` or `variables`:
```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: MutatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: keda-prometheus-serveraddress-configmap
spec:
  evaluation:
    mutateExisting:
      enabled: true
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        resources: ["configmaps"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
  targetMatchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: ["keda.sh"]
        apiVersions: ["v1alpha1"]
        resources: ["scaledobjects"]
  variables:
    - name: serverAddress
      expression: >-
        object.data["main"]
  mutations:
    - patchType: JSONPatch
      jsonPatch:
        expression: >-
          object.spec.triggers.filter(e,
            has(e.type) && e.type == "prometheus"
          ).map(e,
            JSONPatch{
              op: "replace",
              path: "/spec/triggers/" + string(object.spec.triggers.indexOf(e)) + "/metadata/serverAddress",
              value: string(variables.serverAddress)
            }
          )
```
2. The `variables.serverAddress` expression `object.data["main"]` fails because `object` now refers to the `ScaledObject` target, not the `ConfigMap` that triggered the mutation.
3. There is no variable available to access the original `ConfigMap` request data.

### Expected behavior

The original admission request's object/oldObject should be accessible within the `MutatingPolicy` CEL evaluation context when `targetMatchConstraints` is configured, enabling policies to reference both the triggering resource and the target resource.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Kyverno logs

```Shell

```

### Slack discussion

_No response_

### Troubleshooting

- [x] I have searched other issues in this repository and mine is not recorded.

title: [Bug] [CLI] GeneratingPolicy test fails with custom CRDs (GetRESTMapper ignores CRD-aware discovery for fake clients)
body:
### Kyverno CLI Version

1.17.1

### Description

When running Kyverno test for a GeneratingPolicy that matches custom CRD resources, the CLI fails with:

```
failed to map gvk to gvr storage.cnrm.cloud.google.com/v1beta1, Kind=StorageBucket
(no matches for kind "StorageBucket" in version "storage.cnrm.cloud.google.com/v1beta1")
```
Even when CRDs are provided via ClusterResource.spec.crds (introduced in v1.17.1 via #15194), the error persists.

#### Root cause
[pkg/utils/restmapper/restmapper.go#GetRESTMapper](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/pkg/utils/restmapper/restmapper.go) detects `*kubefake.Clientset` and unconditionally falls back to a static mapper built from `data.APIGroupResources()` (built-in k8s types only). It never consults the CRD-aware `FakeDiscoveryClient` that [ext/cluster/fake.go#DClient](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/ext/cluster/fake.go) sets up with `AddGVRToGVKMapping`.

```
// restmapper.go — the fake-client branch ignores CRDs entirely
if client != nil && !isFake {
    dc := client.GetKubeClient().Discovery()
    cachedDiscovery := memory.NewMemCacheClient(dc)
    restMapper = restmapper.NewDeferredDiscoveryRESTMapper(cachedDiscovery)
} else {
    // ← always lands here for kyverno test
    apiGroupResources, err := data.APIGroupResources()
    restMapper = restmapper.NewDiscoveryRESTMapper(apiGroupResources)
}
```

The `GeneratingPolicy` code path in [cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/commands/test/test.go](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/commands/test/test.go) calls `restMapper.RESTMapping(gvk)` for each input resource, which fails for any custom CRD.

ValidatingPolicy tests with custom CRDs work because they don't go through GetRESTMapper.

#### Possible fix

`GetRESTMapper` could use the `RESTMapper` built by `fakeCluster.RESTMapper(crds)` (which already includes CRDs) instead of creating a fresh static mapper. Alternatively, the `else` branch could query the dclient's discovery client rather than using static data.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a `GeneratingPolicy` that matches a custom CRD (e.g. `StorageBucket`):
```
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1beta1
kind: GeneratingPolicy
metadata:
  name: test-gpol
spec:
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: ['storage.cnrm.cloud.google.com']
        apiVersions: ['v1beta1']
        operations: ['CREATE']
        resources: ['storagebuckets']
  generate:
    - expression: |
        generator.Apply("default", [{
          "kind": dyn("ConfigMap"),
          "apiVersion": dyn("v1"),
          "metadata": dyn({"name": dyn("test"), "namespace": dyn("default")})
        }])
```
2. Create a CRD file (storagebucket-crd.yaml):
```
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: storagebuckets.storage.cnrm.cloud.google.com
spec:
  group: storage.cnrm.cloud.google.com
  names:
    kind: StorageBucket
    plural: storagebuckets
    singular: storagebucket
  scope: Namespaced
  versions:
    - name: v1beta1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
```
3. Create a ClusterResource file (clusterresources.yaml):
```
apiVersion: cli.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterResource
metadata:
  name: clusterresources
spec:
  crds:
    - storagebucket-crd.yaml
```
4. Create a test resource (resource.yaml):
```
apiVersion: storage.cnrm.cloud.google.com/v1beta1
kind: StorageBucket
metadata:
  name: test-bucket
  namespace: default
spec:
  location: us-west1
```
5. Create kyverno-test.yaml:
```
apiVersion: cli.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: test-gpol
clusterResources:
  - clusterresources.yaml
policies:
  - policy.yaml
resources:
  - resource.yaml
results:
  - isGeneratingPolicy: true
    kind: StorageBucket
    policy: test-gpol
    resources: ["default/test-bucket"]
    result: pass
```
6. Run: `kyverno test .`

### Expected behavior

The CLI should use the CRDs from `ClusterResource.spec.crds` to build the GVK→GVR mapping, allowing `GeneratingPolicy` tests with custom CRDs to work offline, the same way `ValidatingPolicy` tests with custom CRDs already work.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Kyverno logs

```Shell
Loading test  ( kyverno-test.yaml ) ...
  Loading values/variables ...
  Loading policies ...
  Loading resources ...
Loading Kubernetes resources ...
  Loading exceptions ...
  Applying 1 policy to 1 resources with 0 exceptions ...
Error: failed to run test (failed to apply policies on resource test-bucket
(failed to map gvk to gvr storage.cnrm.cloud.google.com/v1beta1, Kind=StorageBucket
(no matches for kind "StorageBucket" in version "storage.cnrm.cloud.google.com/v1beta1")))
```

title: [Bug] unable to clone a secret if it has an ownerReference
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.0

### Description

Good afternoon,

I'm trying to copy a secret that was synced from Hashicorp Vault using External Secrets.

The secret looks like this:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
data:
  .dockerconfigjson: <..removed..>
kind: Secret
metadata:
  annotations:
    reconcile.external-secrets.io/data-hash: ee027512ac46a14b119c747f39dabc6bd80fb78f87f3063b60cbda95
  labels:
    reconcile.external-secrets.io/created-by: 4a8632931f081dfd997d155b656a10bc829bdbeabd004c479310b09d
    reconcile.external-secrets.io/managed: "true"
  name: example
  namespace: kyverno
  ownerReferences:
  - apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1
    blockOwnerDeletion: true
    controller: true
    kind: ExternalSecret
    name: example
    uid: 16401acc-ab37-4b5d-b4e2-fbd6f952f602
type: kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson
```

And here's my policy:
```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: GeneratingPolicy
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups: [""]
      apiVersions: [v1]
      operations: [CREATE, UPDATE]
      resources: [namespaces]
  variables:
  - name: namespace
    expression: object.metadata.name
  - name: secret
    expression: resource.Get("v1", "secrets", "kyverno", "example")
  generate:
  - expression: generator.Apply(variables.namespace, [variables.secret])
```

However the secret never gets cloned.
I've changed my policy to only copy the data:

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: GeneratingPolicy
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups: [""]
      apiVersions: [v1]
      operations: [CREATE, UPDATE]
      resources: [namespaces]
  variables:
  - name: namespace
    expression: object.metadata.name
  - name: secret
    expression: resource.Get("v1", "secrets", "kyverno", "example")
  - name: source
    expression: |-
      [{
        "kind": dyn("Secret"),
        "apiVersion": dyn("v1"),
        "metadata": dyn({
          "name": "other-example",
        }),
        "data": dyn(variables.secret.data),
        "type": dyn("kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson")
      }]
  generate:
  - expression: generator.Apply(variables.namespace, variables.source)
```

This one works as expected. I believe this is due to the `ownerReferences` and I agree Kyverno shouldn't set any owner reference pointing at ESO. However I'm wondering if there's a better way to handle it, for example:
- keep it as it is, but i) display a warning and ii) add a few words in the documentation about this limitation?
- copy the secret, while ignoring the `ownerReferences` field (and maybe let users opt-in?)

Note I still need to test whether resource synchronization works with the proposed workaround (only cloning the data).

Finally, I don't know if the behavior is the same using the old-style generate ClusterPolicy.

title: [Bug] ValidatingPolicy resource.List() fails with RBAC forbidden despite correct ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding
body:
**Kyverno Version**: 1.17.1 (Helm chart 3.7.1)
**Kubernetes Platform and Version**: Amazon EKS

## **Description**
When migrating a ClusterPolicy (using apiCall context) to a ValidatingPolicy (using resource.List() CEL function), the background scan fails with an RBAC forbidden error, even though the correct ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding are in place.

The same logic works perfectly as a ClusterPolicy with apiCall, but fails as a ValidatingPolicy with resource.List().

## **Steps to Reproduce**

1. RBAC Configuration (in Kyverno Helm values)
```
  admissionController:
    rbac:
      clusterRole:
        extraResources:
          - apiGroups: ['networking.k8s.io']
            resources: ['ingresses']
            verbs: ['get', 'list', 'watch']

  reportsController:
    rbac:
      clusterRole:
        extraResources:
          - apiGroups: ['networking.k8s.io']
            resources: ['ingresses']
            verbs: ['get', 'list', 'watch']
```
2. Verified ClusterRole has the correct rules.
```
  rules:
    - apiGroups:
      - networking.k8s.io
      resources:
      - ingresses
      verbs:
      - get
      - list
      - watch
```
3. Verified ClusterRoleBinding is correct.
Confirmed kyverno:reports-controller ClusterRoleBinding binds the ClusterRole to ServiceAccount kyverno-reports-controller in namespace kyverno.
4. Created the ValidatingPolicy.
```
  apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
  kind: ValidatingPolicy
  metadata:
    name: enforce-service-type-based-on-ingress
  spec:
    matchConstraints:
      resourceRules:
        - apiGroups: ['']
          apiVersions: ['v1']
          operations: [CREATE, UPDATE]
          resources: [services]
    validationActions: [Audit]
    variables:
      - name: isReferencedByIngress
        expression: >-
          resource.List('networking.k8s.io/v1', 'Ingress', object.metadata.namespace)
            .items.orValue([]).exists(ing,
              has(ing.spec) && has(ing.spec.rules) &&
              ing.spec.rules.exists(rule,
                has(rule.http) && has(rule.http.paths) &&
                rule.http.paths.exists(path,
                  has(path.backend) && has(path.backend.service) &&
                  path.backend.service.name == object.metadata.name
                )
              )
            )
    validations:
      - message: "Services referenced in Ingress must be of type 'NodePort' or 'LoadBalancer'."
        expression: >-
          !variables.isReferencedByIngress ||
          (object.spec.type == 'NodePort' || object.spec.type == 'LoadBalancer')
      - message: "Services not referenced in Ingress must be of type 'ClusterIP' or 'LoadBalancer'."
        expression: >-
          variables.isReferencedByIngress ||
          (object.spec.type == 'ClusterIP' || object.spec.type == 'LoadBalancer')
```

## **Expected Behavior**
The resource.List() CEL function should use the reports controller's service account credentials to list Ingresses during background scans.

## **Actual Behavior**
PolicyReport shows an RBAC error on every Service evaluation:
```
  message: >-
    failed to load context: failed to list resource: Ingress.networking.k8s.io
    is forbidden: User
    "system:serviceaccount:kyverno:kyverno-reports-controller" cannot list
    resource "Ingress" in API group "networking.k8s.io" in the namespace "<namespace>"
  policy: enforce-service-type-based-on-ingress
  result: error
  rule: evaluation
  source: KyvernoValidatingPolicy
```

## **Troubleshooting Performed**

1. Verified ClusterRole — The aggregated kyverno:reports-controller ClusterRole includes networking.k8s.io/ingresses with get, list, watch.
2. Verified ClusterRoleBinding — Correctly binds to ServiceAccount kyverno-reports-controller in namespace kyverno.
3. Created an additional ClusterRoleBinding with the view ClusterRole — still fails.
4. Restarted all Kyverno controllers — still fails.
5. Deleted all PolicyReports to force rescan — still fails.
6. Tested as ClusterPolicy — The equivalent ClusterPolicy using apiCall context with the same RBAC works without errors.

## **Additional Notes**

- The source field in PolicyReport is KyvernoValidatingPolicy for the failing ValidatingPolicy vs kyverno for the working ClusterPolicy, suggesting different code paths for RBAC evaluation.
- We also discovered that spec.validations[].name is not a supported field in ValidatingPolicy (strict decoding error), unlike spec.variables[].name.
- This is relevant given the planned deprecation of ClusterPolicy — policies using resource.List() may not be migratable until this is resolved.

title: [Bug] Incorrect elementIndex resolution after prior patchStrategicMerge mutation
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.0

### Setup
- Kyverno Version: 1.17.0                                                                                                                                                                                                        
- Kubernetes Version: 1.31.x           
- Platform: K3d (reproduced) / AKS (discovered)
- Rule Type: Mutate

### Context
When two ClusterPolicy resources mutate the same Pod on CREATE, list index handling becomes inconsistent if both modify `spec.volumes[]`.
- One policy uses patchStrategicMerge to append volumes.
- Another policy (e.g., the official add-emptydir-sizelimit) uses foreach with elementIndex and patchesJson6902 to patch existing emptyDir volumes.

When both are applied, the elementIndex in the `foreach` loop may reference incorrect positions after the first mutation modifies the array.

### Impact
This can cause JSON6902 patches to target the wrong volume entries resulting in intermittent Pod creation errors such as: `may not specify more than 1 volume type`

The kyverno policy [add-emptydir-sizelimit](https://kyverno.io/policies/other/add-emptydir-sizelimit/add-emptydir-sizelimit/) works correctly in isolation but fails when another policy mutates the same list during admission.

### Reproduce
The attached [foreach-elementIndex-stale-after-prepend.tar.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25725688/foreach-elementIndex-stale-after-prepend.tar.gz) contains a chainsaw conformance test that reproduces this reliably. Extract it into the kyverno repo root:

This creates `test/conformance/chainsaw/mutate/e2e/foreach-elementIndex-stale-after-prepend/` with two policies, a Pod, and assertions.

Run with chainsaw against any cluster with Kyverno installed:

```bash
chainsaw test --test-dir test/conformance/chainsaw/mutate/e2e/foreach-elementIndex-stale-after-prepend/

	idc.RLock()

I think that developers thought about optimization, when he was writing this code, because using `defer` is not the best practise in case where you working with complex request. title: [Bug] source field in policy reports incorrectly set to kyverno for NamespacedValidatingPolicy
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.0

## Bug Report                                                                                                
                                                                                                               
  ### Description
                                                                                                               
  The `source` field in policy reports is not correctly set for `NamespacedValidatingPolicy` (nvpol). While
  `ValidatingPolicy` (vpol) correctly reports `KyvernoValidatingPolicy` as the source,                         
  `NamespacedValidatingPolicy` reports `kyverno` instead of the expected `KyvernoNamespacedValidatingPolicy`
  (or equivalent).

  ### Expected Behavior

  The `source` field in policy reports should reflect the policy kind. Based on the existing pattern for other
  policy types, `NamespacedValidatingPolicy` should have a distinct source value (e.g.,
  `KyvernoNamespacedValidatingPolicy`) to allow differentiation from other policy kinds in report results.

  Current mapping for reference:

  | Policy Kind | Source (actual) | Source (expected) |
  |---|---|---|
  | `ClusterPolicy` / `Policy` | `kyverno` | `kyverno` |
  | `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` | `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` | `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` |
  | `ValidatingPolicy` | `KyvernoValidatingPolicy` | `KyvernoValidatingPolicy` |
  | `NamespacedValidatingPolicy` | `kyverno` ❌ | `KyvernoNamespacedValidatingPolicy` (or similar) |

  ### Actual Behavior

  `source` is set to `kyverno` for `NamespacedValidatingPolicy`, making it indistinguishable from
  `ClusterPolicy`/`Policy` in report results.

  ### Steps to Reproduce

  1. Create a `NamespacedValidatingPolicy` resource
  2. Trigger policy evaluation

title: [Bug] DeletingPolicy -  "policy did not match" logged as error for every non-matching resource
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.0

### Description

When using a `DeletingPolicy` (e.g. to delete standalone pods after a delay), the controller logs one error line for every resource in the `matchConstraints` but does not satisfy the CEL conditions. With many pods in the cluster, this produces a lot of error logs at each run, regardless of log verbosity.

**Expected behavior**
Resources that match `matchConstraints` but not the CEL conditions are correctly not deleted as expected. I expect this "policy did not match" case to be logged at debug (or similar) verbosity level, not as an error.

**Actual behavior**
One error-level log entry per non-matching resource, e.g.:
```
...
kyverno-cleanup-controller-84949db6cd-jsh45 controller {"level":"error","id":1,"key":"cleanup-succeeded-standalone-pods","namespace":"","name":"cleanup-succeeded-standalone-pods","name":"metrics-server-7cc9c5b45b-hqpjm","namespace":"metrics-server","logger":"deleting-controller/worker","time":"2026-02-23T11:18:00Z","message":"policy did not match match"}
kyverno-cleanup-controller-84949db6cd-jsh45 controller {"level":"error","id":1,"key":"cleanup-succeeded-standalone-pods","namespace":"","name":"cleanup-succeeded-standalone-pods","name":"metrics-server-7cc9c5b45b-pwrww","namespace":"metrics-server","logger":"deleting-controller/worker","time":"2026-02-23T11:18:00Z","message":"policy did not match match"}
...
```
With hundreds of pods, this makes the cleanup controller very noisy on every execution.



The policy used for test:
```
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1

  name: cleanup-succeeded-standalone-pods
spec:
  schedule: "*/3 * * * *"

        (!has(object.metadata.ownerReferences) || size(object.metadata.ownerReferences) == 0) &&

title: [Bug] Policy namespaceSelector is applied to Webhooks
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.1

### Kubernetes Version

1.32.x

### Kubernetes Platform

OpenShift

### Kyverno Rule Type

Mutate

### Description

When creating a mutating policy, the spec.matchConstraints.namespaceSelector are used to also set the webhooks.namespaceSelector of the MutatingWebhookConfiguration (kyverno-resource-mutating-webhook-cfg) object, effectivelly limiting the webhook to firing only for resources in namespaces matching those labels.

When creating multiple mutating policies each with their own set of spec.matchConstraints.namespaceSelector i have observed that only the namespaceSelector from the last applied policy is used to configure the MutatingWebhookConfiguration. This effectively excludes all other mutating policies since the webhook will never fire for resources outside the namespaces selected by the last mpol. 

[mpol.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25482209/mpol.yaml)

This is a major issue!

This is a clear change in behaviour when going from version 1.15.3 -> 1.16.0. My guess it that it is related to the addition of https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pull/13890
It is clearly observable by just deleting/recreating mutation policies and watching the webhooks.namespaceSelector change to allign with whatever selector is in your last created policy.

MutatingWebhookConfiguration (1.15.3):
```yaml
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: MutatingWebhookConfiguration
metadata:
  annotations:
    admissions.enforcer/disabled: "true"
  creationTimestamp: "2026-02-23T08:03:25Z"
  generation: 24
  labels:
    webhook.kyverno.io/managed-by: kyverno
  name: kyverno-resource-mutating-webhook-cfg
webhooks:
- admissionReviewVersions:
  - v1
  clientConfig:
    caBundle: redacted
    service:
      name: kyverno-svc
      namespace: governance-cluster01
      path: /mpol/set-resources-product1-quota/set-resources-product2-quota
      port: 443
  failurePolicy: Fail
  matchPolicy: Equivalent
  name: mpol.validate.kyverno.svc-fail
  namespaceSelector:
    matchExpressions:
    - key: kubernetes.io/metadata.name
      operator: NotIn
      values:
      - kube-system
    - key: kubernetes.io/metadata.name
      operator: NotIn
      values:
      - governance-cluster01
  objectSelector: {}
  reinvocationPolicy: Never
  rules:
  - apiGroups:
    - ""
    apiVersions:
    - v1
    operations:
    - CREATE
    - UPDATE
    resources:
    - pods
    scope: '*'
  - apiGroups:
    - ""
    apiVersions:
    - v1
    operations:
    - CREATE
    - UPDATE
    resources:
    - pods
    scope: '*'
  sideEffects: NoneOnDryRun
  timeoutSeconds: 10
```

MutatingWebhookConfiguration (1.17.1):
```yaml
kind: MutatingWebhookConfiguration
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: kyverno-resource-mutating-webhook-cfg
  generation: 3
  creationTimestamp: '2026-02-23T11:07:24Z'
  labels:
    webhook.kyverno.io/managed-by: kyverno
  annotations:
    admissions.enforcer/disabled: 'true'
webhooks:
  - name: mpol.validate.kyverno.svc-fail
    sideEffects: NoneOnDryRun
    clientConfig:
      service:
        namespace: governance-cluster01
        name: kyverno-svc
        path: /mpol/set-resources-product1-quota/set-resources-product2-quota
        port: 443
      caBundle: redacted
    reinvocationPolicy: Never
    rules:
      - operations:
          - CREATE
          - UPDATE
        apiGroups:
          - ''
        apiVersions:
          - v1
        resources:
          - pods
        scope: '*'
    matchPolicy: Equivalent
    namespaceSelector:
      matchLabels:
        owner: team-a
        product: product1
      matchExpressions:
        - key: kubernetes.io/metadata.name
          operator: NotIn
          values:
            - kube-system
        - key: kubernetes.io/metadata.name
          operator: NotIn
          values:
            - governance-cluster01
    admissionReviewVersions:
      - v1
    failurePolicy: Fail
    objectSelector: {}
    timeoutSeconds: 10
```

Note the extra matchLabels block in the MutatingWebhookConfiguration (1.17.1) which limits mutation to those namespaces even if other policies with other namespaceSelector also exist in the cluster.


Side note on versions used:
Kubernetes version: 1.33 (Not selectable from the version dropdown)
This was also tested (and applicable for) kyverno version 1.16.X, 1.17.0



### Steps to reproduce

1. Apply mpol with spec.matchConstraints.namespaceSelector
2. Observe that MutatingWebhookConfiguration/kyverno-resource-mutating-webhook-cfg applies the same namespaceSelector to the webhook
3. Apply another mpol with a different set of spec.matchConstraints.namespaceSelector
4. Observe that MutatingWebhookConfiguration/kyverno-resource-mutating-webhook-cfg is updated to include only the namespaceSelector from the mpol applied in step 3.

### Expected behavior

The mutation webhook should trigger for resources in all namespaces, except those namespaces excluded in the chart values (kube-system and the Kyverno namespace by default). Narrowing down the _scope_ of a singel mpol should not narrow down the _scope_ of the webhook.

title: [Bug] 1.17.0: APICall: context-canceled
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.0

### Kubernetes Version

1.34.x

### Kubernetes Platform

EKS

### Kyverno Rule Type

Generate

### Description

As of Kyverno 1.17.0, we see the following error in the Kyverno admission controller logs when triggering a ClusterPolicy that uses apiCall to get a list of namespaces from the cluster:

```
ERR github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/engine/context/deferred.go:42 > failed to load data error="failed to fetch data for APICall: failed to GET resource with raw url\n: /api/v1/namespaces: Get \"[https://172.20.0.1:443/api/v1/namespaces](https://172.20.0.1/api/v1/namespaces)\": context canceled" logger=DefaultContextLoaderFactory name=namespaceCheck
```

When triggering the policy, there is no error sent to the client (kubectl), but the downstream generate rules are not applied.

The following ClusterPolicy is working in 1.16.3, but results in the above error in 1.17.0:

```
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: create-developers-rolebinding
spec:
  admission: true
  background: false
  emitWarning: false
  rules:
  - context:
    - apiCall:
        jmesPath: items[*].metadata.name
        method: GET
        urlPath: /api/v1/namespaces
      name: namespaceCheck
    exclude:
      any:
      - clusterRoles:
        - cluster-admin
    generate:
      apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
      data:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            kyverno.io/user: '{{request.userInfo.username}}'
        roleRef:
          apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
          kind: ClusterRole
          name: admin
        subjects:
        - kind: Group
          name: developers
        - kind: ServiceAccount
          name: gha-runner-scale-set-controller-gha-rs-controller
          namespace: github-actions
      kind: RoleBinding
      name: '{{request.object.metadata.name}}-admin-binding'
      namespace: '{{request.object.metadata.name}}'
      synchronize: false
    match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - Namespace
          operations:
          - CREATE
    name: create-developers-admin-rolebinding
    preconditions:
      all:
      - key: '{{namespaceCheck}}'
        operator: AnyNotIn
        value: '{{request.object.metadata.name}}'
      any:
      - key: '{{ request.userInfo.groups }}'
        operator: AnyIn
        value:
        - developers
      - key: '{{serviceAccountName}}'
        operator: AnyIn
        value:
        - gha-runner-scale-set-controller-gha-rs-controller
    skipBackgroundRequests: true
```


### Steps to reproduce

1. Apply previously mentioned ClusterPolicy, as a member of the groups defined in the preconditions, attempt to create a Namespace.
2. Observe this working in 1.16.3, and failing in 1.17.0

### Expected behavior

I expect Kyverno 1.17.0 to process the request and generate the associated resources defined in the ClusterPolicy.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Kyverno logs

```Shell
