title: [Bug]mutatingpolicy not working properly when mutateExisting is set to true ?
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.15.0

### Description

Hi,

I have this mutatingpolicy in cluster installed which works when we update the failed resource but doesn't fix automatically the resource which have this error and is in failed state already on cluster.


```
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: MutatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: remove-crossplane-external-create-pending
spec:
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups:
          - spanner.gcp.upbound.io
          - storage.gcp.upbound.io
          - sql.gcp.upbound.io
          - compute.gcp.upbound.io
          - bigquery.gcp.upbound.io
        apiVersions: ["*"]
        resources:
          - projectiammembers
          - buckets
          - projectservices
          - bucketiammembers
          - datasetiammembers
          - instanceiammembers

        operations: ["UPDATE"]

  evaluation:
    admission:
      enabled: true
    mutateExisting:
      enabled: true

  # Patch logic
  mutations:
    - patchType: JSONPatch
      jsonPatch:
        expression: |
          // Only mutate if the annotation exists AND Crossplane signals safe removal
          (
            has(object.metadata.annotations) &&
            "crossplane.io/external-create-pending" in object.metadata.annotations &&
            has(object.status) &&
            has(object.status.conditions) &&
            object.status.conditions.exists(c,
              c.type == "Synced" &&
              c.status == "False" &&
              c.reason == "ReconcileError" &&
              c.message.contains("remove the crossplane.io/external-create-pending annotation")
            )
          )
          ?
          [
            JSONPatch{
              op: "remove",
              path: "/metadata/annotations/crossplane.io~1external-create-pending"
            }
          ]
          :
          []
```

Have also added this clusterrole to fix rbac


```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: kyverno:background-controller:crossplane-gcp
  labels:
    rbac.kyverno.io/aggregate-to-background-controller: "true"
rules:
  - apiGroups:
      - cloudplatform.gcp.upbound.io
      - spanner.gcp.upbound.io
      - storage.gcp.upbound.io
      - sql.gcp.upbound.io
      - compute.gcp.upbound.io
      - bigquery.gcp.upbound.io
    resources:
      - projectiammembers
      - buckets
      - projectservices
      - bucketiammembers
      - datasetiammembers
      - instanceiammembers
      - serviceaccounts
    verbs:
      - get
      - list
      - watch
      - patch
      - update
```

This policy works just fine when i do update on the resources which are in failed state manually (update label, annotation etc on the resource) , however it doesn't work in background mode, i.e it doesn't fixes or removes in this case annotation when the resource is just there on cluster without any update operation ?
Are we missing anything or mutateExisting doesn't work as expected ?

### Slack discussion

_No response_

### Troubleshooting

- [x] I have read and followed the documentation AND the [troubleshooting guide](https://kyverno.io/docs/troubleshooting/).
- [x] I have searched other issues in this repository and mine is not recorded.

title: [Bug] CRDs are too big to be managed via HelmRelease
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.16.0

### Description

With the latest 1.16.0 version released last week, we are facing difficulties managing kyverno via HelmRelease + Flux

For our setup it is advantageous to manage all our deployments via HelmRelease and have HelmRelease manage CRDs as well. We have the helm chart that has kyverno chart as a dependency ( it is simply a wrapper for convenience, nothing extra added ). When trying to reconcile with the latest version, we get the following:

```
2025-11-20T10:59:17.689704263Z: successfully applied 20 CustomResourceDefinition(s)
2025-11-20T10:59:17.689707602Z: clearing REST mapper cache
  Warning  InstallFailed  1s  helm-controller  Helm install failed for release kyverno/kyverno with chart internal-kyverno@0.0.0-main:
 create: failed to create: Secret "sh.helm.release.v1.kyverno.v1" is invalid: data: Too long: may not be more than 1048576 bytes
 ```

Simply put, the CRDs inside the chart are just too big and helm fails when creating the versioning secret. 

Looking between this version ( 1.16.0 ) and the previous one, there seems to be a 20% increase approximately in the total size of the crd manifests.

We attempted separate out only the CRDs in a separate chart, the result is the same.

While there are alternatives to using a HelmRelease to manage the CRDs as well, for our needs it's a good strategy and would like to understand if there is something that can be done to reduce the size of those CRDs.

### Slack discussion

https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/CLGR9BJU9/p1763647069871299

### Troubleshooting

- [x] I have read and followed the documentation AND the [troubleshooting guide](https://kyverno.io/docs/troubleshooting/).
- [x] I have searched other issues in this repository and mine is not recorded.

### Description

title: [Bug] Kyverno install.yaml deploys Linux-Only pods without OS nodeSelector
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.11.0

### Description

In mixed Linux+Windows Kubernetes clusters, Kyverno pods created by install.yaml won't start unless their spec is customized. This occurs because the manifests create Linux-only pods but do not include an OS-specific nodeSelector. As a result, the scheduler attempts to place Kyverno pods on Windows nodes, where they cannot run, and the pods enter a crash loop.

Since the pods are Linux-only, they have to be created with {"nodeSelector":{"kubernetes.io/os":"linux"}}.

apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: add-runbook-annotation
spec:
  admission: true

    - match:
        resources:

                    value: "https://acme.domain/runbook/{{ request.object.spec.groups["{{elementIndex0}}"].name }}/{{ element.alert }}/"
                preconditions:
                  all:
                    - key: >-
                        {{ element.annotations.runbook_url || 'ABSENT'

            list: request.object.spec.groups[]
      name: add-runbook-annotation

title: [Bug] Special variable `image` doesn't work with imageVerify rule
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.15.0

### Description

I’ve got a ClusterPolicy that checks image signatures. It basically looks like this:

```
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
...
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  background: true
  rules:
    - name: verify-image-signature
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds:
                - Pod
      verifyImages:
        - type: Cosign
          imageReferences:
            - "[account_id].dkr.ecr.sa-east-1.amazonaws.com/*"
          attestors:
            - entries:
                - keys:
                    kms: "hashivault://{{ image.reference }}"
                    rekor:
                      ignoreTlog: true
```

The idea was to let the policy cover every image (app) in an ECR registry. Each image has its own signing key stored in Vault. I wanted to use the special `image` variable to build the key name automatically (`image.reference` is just an example), so I wouldn’t need a separate policy (or rule) for every image, and, most importantly, I wouldn’t have to maintain a list of them.

The `image` special variable is mentioned in the [documentation](https://kyverno.io/docs/policy-types/cluster-policy/verify-images/sigstore/#special-variables) and it looks like a perfect solution for my case, but unfortunately, it doesn't work. 

I tested that with the kyverno 1.16.0 and I'm getting the following error:

```
verify-image-signature:
  verify-image-signature: 'failed to substitute variables: failed to resolve image.reference
    at path /verifyImages/0/attestors/0/entries/0/keys/kms: JMESPath query failed:
    Unknown key "image" in path'
```

A similar issue was already reported (#10018), but it wasn't solved.

title: [Bug] Combination of synchronize:true and generateExisting:true seems to cause long objects create/update
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.11.5

### Kubernetes Version

1.32.x

### Kubernetes Platform

Other (specify in description)

### Kyverno Rule Type

Generate

### Description

Combination of generate.synchronize: true per object and and generateExisting: true seems to cause long objects create/update. 
I suspect that errors below indicate some kind of race condition inside controller. Therefore it terminates reconcile operation over and over.
If to wait 10-20-30 minutes, at some point all requested objects get created or updated.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Apply generate policy with both options enabled like
```
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: eso-bootstrap-policy
spec:
  generateExisting: true
  rules:
    - name: create-eso-sa
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Namespace
      generate:
        orphanDownstreamOnPolicyDelete: true
        synchronize: true
        apiVersion: v1
        kind: ServiceAccount
        name: vault-secret-store
        namespace: "{{request.object.metadata.name}}"

    - name: create-eso-crb
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Namespace
      generate:
        synchronize: true
        orphanDownstreamOnPolicyDelete: true
        apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
        kind: ClusterRoleBinding
        name: "vault-tokenreviewer-crb-{{ request.object.metadata.name }}"        
        data:
          roleRef:
            kind: ClusterRole
            name: vault-tokenreviewer
          subjects:
            - kind: ServiceAccount
              name: vault-secret-store
              namespace: "{{request.object.metadata.name}}"
```

### Expected behavior

I expect that objects will be created or updated according to policy with minumum delay.

title: [Bug] Wildcard policy does not match newly created CRs until Kyverno restarts
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.15.0

### Kubernetes Version

1.32.x

### Kubernetes Platform

KinD

### Kyverno Rule Type

Validate

### Description

A `ClusterPolicy` using `kinds: ["*/*/*"]` fails to match admission requests for Custom Resources (CRs) if the CRD for that resource was created *after* the policy was applied.

If the Kyverno admission controller pod is restarted, the policy matching works correctly, and the admission request is properly intercepted.

### Steps to reproduce

1.  **Start Kyverno v1.15.2** (with `crdWatcher` enabled).

2.  **Apply the `ClusterPolicy`:**

    ```bash
    kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
    apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
    kind: ClusterPolicy
    metadata:
      name: protect-critical-crds-and-crs
      annotations:
        policies.kyverno.io/title: Deny CR Deletion when critical label is set
        policies.kyverno.io/category: Protection

        policies.kyverno.io/subject: CustomResource
        policies.kyverno.io/minversion: 1.6.0
        policies.kyverno.io/description: >-
          This policy prevents the deletion of Custom Resources that have the
          'critical: true' label set, or whose parent CRD
          has the critical label set.
    spec:
      background: false
      rules:
        - name: cr-is-critical

            all:

                  kinds:

                    - policy/*/*

                    - scheduling.k8s.io/*/*
                    - snapshot.storage.k8s.io/*/*
                    - storage.k8s.io/*/*
                    - wgpolicyk8s.io/*/*
          validate:
            failureAction: Enforce
            message: "Deleting {{ request.object.metadata.name }} CR is not allowed since it has critical label."
            deny: {}
        - name: parent-crd-is-critical
          match:
            all:
              - resources:
                  kinds:
                    - "*/*"

                    - "apiextensions.k8s.io/v1/*"
                    - "apiregistration.k8s.io/*/*"
                    - "apps/*/*"

                    - scheduling.k8s.io/*/*
                    - snapshot.storage.k8s.io/*/*
                    - storage.k8s.io/*/*
                    - wgpolicyk8s.io/*/*
          context:
          - name: criticalLabels
            apiCall:
              urlPath: "/apis/apiextensions.k8s.io/v1/customresourcedefinitions/{{request.resource.resource}}.{{request.resource.group}}"
              jmesPath: "metadata.labels.\"critical\" || 'false'"  
          validate:

            deny:

                  value: "true"

          match:
            all:

                    - CustomResourceDefinition

    spec:

    EOF
    ```

7.  **Attempt to delete the `Widget` CR (this should fail):**

    ```bash
    kubectl delete widget widget-critical-true -n a-protection-test
    ```

### Expected behavior

The deletion should be **denied** by the `cr-is-critical` rule in the `ClusterPolicy`, as the resource `kind` matches `*/*/*`, the operation is `DELETE`, and it has the `critical: "true"` label.

title: [Bug] GeneratingPolicy with namespaceSelector fails to synchronize when objects are of kind Namespace
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.15.0

### Kubernetes Version

1.32.x

### Kubernetes Platform

Bare metal

### Kyverno Rule Type

GeneratingPolicy

### Description

GeneratingPolicys with namespaceSelector that apply to namespace objects fail to synchronize producing the error message:
```
2025-11-07T14:14:15Z ERR github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/policy/gpol.go:151 > failed to get namespace error="name is required" logger=PolicyController name=
```
For example,
```
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: GeneratingPolicy
metadata:
  name: generating-policy-with-namespace-selector
spec:
  evaluation:
    generateExisting:
      enabled: true  
    synchronize:
      enabled: true
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups:   [""]
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations:  ["CREATE"]
      resources:   ["namespaces"]
    namespaceSelector:
      matchLabels:
          app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: my-app
  variables:
    - name: targetNs
      expression: "object.metadata.name"
    - name: sourceSecret
      expression: resource.Get("v1", "secrets", "source-namespace", "secret-name")
  generate:
    - expression: generator.Apply(variables.targetNs, [variables.sourceSecret])
```

A possible work around is to switch to use `objectSelector`. However, the documentation indicates that `namespaceSelector` should work on namespaces.
The documentation:
```
kubectl explain generatingpolicy.spec.matchConstraints.namespaceSelector
```
says:
```
If the object itself is a namespace, the matching is performed on object.metadata.labels. 
```

Reading the source code the problem is caused by this line:
https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/7411dabd32a87cce8d693bf90236de19f8860d4d/pkg/policy/gpol.go#L148
The current implementation of `resource.GetNamespace()` is `getNestedString(u.Object, "metadata", "namespace")`. 
`namespace` objects don't have a `metadata.namespace` so this fails to get the namespace name and returns an empty string.

The error message is logged and false is returned so that `triggerMatches` can never match `namespace` objects. 

### Steps to reproduce


1. On a cluster with kyverno installed, apply the following manifest:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: example-namespace
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: my-app
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: source-namespace
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: secret-name
  namespace: source-namespace
data:
  access-key: aWQ=
  secret-key: c2VjcmV0
```
2. Now apply the generating policy:
```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: GeneratingPolicy
metadata:
  name: generating-policy-with-namespace-selector
spec:
  evaluation:
    generateExisting:
      enabled: true  
    synchronize:
      enabled: true
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups:   [""]
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations:  ["CREATE"]
      resources:   ["namespaces"]
    namespaceSelector:
      matchLabels:
          app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: my-app
  variables:
    - name: targetNs
      expression: "object.metadata.name"
    - name: sourceSecret
      expression: resource.Get("v1", "secrets", "source-namespace", "secret-name")
  generate:
    - expression: generator.Apply(variables.targetNs, [variables.sourceSecret])
```
3. Observe error messages in the background controller logs and that the secret has not been copied to `example-namespace`.


### Expected behavior

The secret should be copied to the `example-namespace`. There should be no error messages produced by the background controller.

### Screenshots

### Kyverno logs

title: [Bug] [CLI] Error on mutate.foreach loop with precondition
body:
### Kyverno CLI Version

1.15.0

### Description

A mutate cluster policy with a `foreach` loop containing preconditions with existence/non-existence expressions throws the error `Failed to parse value type doesn't match key type`

This appears to be a similar bug to https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/issues/3131 (which has been resolved) but affecting mutate rather than validate. 

### Steps to reproduce

1. Apply this policy
```
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: all-mutate-vpa-enforce-resource-policy
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Audit
  rules:
    match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - VerticalPodAutoscaler
    mutate:
      foreach:
      - list: request.object.spec.resourcePolicy.containerPolicies[]
        patchesJson6902: |-
          - path: /spec/resourcePolicy/containerPolicies/{{elementIndex}}/maxAllowed/memory
            op: add
            value: '16Gi'
        preconditions:
          any:
          - key: '{{ element.maxAllowed.memory || '''' }}'
            message: maxAllowed.memory not found. Setting that to 16Gi
            operator: Equals
            value: ""
      - list: request.object.spec.resourcePolicy.containerPolicies[]
        patchesJson6902: |-
          - path: /spec/resourcePolicy/containerPolicies/{{elementIndex}}/maxAllowed/memory
            op: replace
            value: '16Gi'
        preconditions:
          any:
          - key: '{{ element.maxAllowed.memory || '''' }}'
            message: maxAllowed.memory specified is greater than maximum allowed.
              Setting that to 16Gi
            operator: GreaterThan
            value: 16Gi
    name: all-mutate-set-max-memory-allowed
```

2. Create a resource that will match the resource kind. In this example `VerticalPodAutoscaler`

`apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1

title: [Bug] Kyverno API docs should not document unsupported features
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.15.0

### Description

The new Kyverno policy types are inspired by the upstream VAP and MAP APIs, but the maintainers have chosen to deviate in one particular area: parameter objects. Policy parameter objects are currently unsupported by Kyverno, as a different model with custom CEL libs has been chosen instead.

Except for parameter objects, the new Kyverno policies are very similar to the upstream policy types, which is good. But it seems like the policy types Go types have copied the docs from the upstream Go types. And in some cases, reused Go types. This results in generated OpenAPI schemas in Kyverno CRDs with incorrect descriptions. Please see: https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Akyverno%2Fkyverno%20%22parameter%20object%22&type=code

I would expect the OpenAPI schemas in Kyverno CRDs to document how the Kyverno policies actually work.

title: [Bug] Devcontainer doesn't have make
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.15.0

### Description

I am trying to get started with contributing to kyverno, following the [development guide](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT.md). It mentions that the devcontainer is the recommended approach, which made me very happy as I use devcontainers in many other projects.

title: [Bug] Autogen for Pod validation policies creates rules that match non-Kubernetes resources
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.15.0

### Description

Kyverno Version
1.15.2 (chart 3.5.2)

Kubernetes Version
v1.32.x

The auto-generated rules for Pod Controllers in response to plain Pod validation policies are too broad, such that they match resource kinds from CRDs that share the same name as a Pod Controller, i.e. `Job`.

For example, in our cluster we have:

```
apiVersion: compute.databricks.crossplane.io/v1alpha1
kind: Job
```

When defining a Pod policy that triggers auto-generation, such as [restrict-image-registries](https://github.com/kyverno/policies/blob/main/best-practices/restrict-image-registries/restrict-image-registries.yaml), the auto-generated rules for the ClusterPolicy look like:

```
status:
  autogen:
    rules:
    - match:
        any:
        - resources:
            kinds:
            - DaemonSet
            - Deployment
            - Job
            - ReplicaSet
            - ReplicationController
            - StatefulSet
# (and CronJob further down)
```

Since `compute.databricks.crossplane.io` also defines a `Job` resource kind, the autogen rules match, causing policy violation reports on the CRD resource:

```
policy restrict-image-registries/autogen-validate-registries fail: validation error: Unknown image registry. rule autogen-validate-registries failed at path /spec/template/
```

### Workaround

Adding a precondition to the policy rules works, because the preconditions also get copied into the autogen rules:

```
    preconditions:
      any:
      - key: "{{ to_string(request.object.apiVersion) }}"
        operator: AnyIn
        value: ['v1', 'apps/v1', 'batch/v1']
```

This ensures that only builtin Kubernetes Pod Controllers match the autogen rules, and CRD kinds with the same name are ignored. Someone mentioned `exclude` as another workaround, but this didn't work for us as the `exclude` rules did not get copied into the autogen rules.

### Impacts

- Having to modify policies to restrict the scope of auto-generated rules makes it tedious and error prone to stay up to date with the best-practice policies developed and tested in the Kyverno policies repo
- The workaround depends on autogen precondition copying behavior not changing in the future

### Suggested fix

Auto-generated rules should use fully-qualified GVKs in the `match` resource kinds, so that only built-in Kubernetes resources are matched.

### Related issues

- Closed as not planned: https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/issues/11675

body:
### Kyverno Version

1.15.0

### Description

**Version**: 1.15.1

### What are you attempting?
I want to create a ClusterPolicy that adds an imagePullSecret to all ServiceAccounts lacking one, but only within a certain subset of namespaces (prefixed by "tn-"). Full policy:

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: patch-tenant-serviceaccounts-with-acr-pull-secret
  annotations:
    policies.kyverno.io/title: Add Image Pull Secret to ServiceAccounts
    policies.kyverno.io/category: ServiceAccount
    policies.kyverno.io/severity: medium
    policies.kyverno.io/subject: ServiceAccount
    policies.kyverno.io/description: >-
      Automatically adds the new acr-pull-secret to ServiceAccounts in tenant namespaces that don't have any
      imagePullSecrets defined. This ensures all pods can pull images from our
      Azure Container Registry.
    policies.kyverno.io/namespace: "tn-*"
spec:
  background: true
  mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate: true
  rules:
    - name: add-acr-pull-secret
      match:
        any:
        - resources:
            kinds:
              - ServiceAccount
            namespaces:
              - "tn-*"
      mutate:
        targets:
          - apiVersion: v1
            kind: ServiceAccount
            namespace: "{{ request.object.metadata.namespace }}"
            name: "{{ request.object.metadata.name }}"
            preconditions:
              all:
              - key: "{{ contains(keys(target), 'imagePullSecrets') }}"
                operator: Equals
                value: false
        patchStrategicMerge:
          imagePullSecrets:
            - name: acr-pull-secret
```

### What do you expect to happen?
All ServiceAccounts within "tn-*" namespaces that lack an ImagePullSecret will have one added. Additionally, all ServiceAccounts passing through the API server will be mutated with this policy as well.

### What actually happens?
Only the ServiceAccounts passing through the API server are mutated as desired.

### Suspected reason
The functionality for fetching preexisting resources doesn't do wildcard matching properly (at least for the namespaces, possibly other fields as well).

title: [Bug] config.webhooks in Helm values generates malformed JSON in ConfigMap
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.15.1

### Description

**Bug Description**
When configuring webhook namespace exclusions through the Kyverno Helm chart's config.webhooks section, the generated JSON in the Kyverno ConfigMap contains malformed syntax with extra brackets, causing parsing issues.

**Environment**
Kyverno Version: 3.5.1 (Helm chart)
Kubernetes Version: GKE Autopilot
Installation Method: Helm

**Expected Behavior**
The config.webhooks configuration in Helm values should generate valid JSON in the Kyverno ConfigMap that matches the documented format:
```[{"namespaceSelector":{"matchExpressions":[{"key":"kubernetes.io/metadata.name","operator":"NotIn","values":["kube-system","kyverno"]}]}}]```

**Actual Behavior**
The generated JSON in the ConfigMap contains malformed syntax with extra brackets:
```{"namespaceSelector":{"matchExpressions":[{"key":"kubernetes.io/metadata.name","operator":"NotIn","values":["gke-gmp-system","gke-managed-filestorecsi","gke-managed-system","gmp-public","kube-system","kube-public","kube-node-lease","namespace-a","namespace-b","namespace-c","namespace-d"[]}]}}```
Note the extra [ before the closing ]} at the end.

**Helm Configuration**
```
config:
  excludeKyvernoNamespace: false
  webhooks:
    namespaceSelector:
      matchExpressions:
      - key: kubernetes.io/metadata.name
        operator: NotIn
        values:
          - gke-gmp-system
          - gke-managed-filestorecsi
          - gke-managed-system
          - gmp-public
          - kube-system
          - kube-public
          - kube-node-lease
          - namespace-a
          - namespace-b
          - namespace-c
          - namespace-d
```

**Steps to Reproduce**
Install Kyverno using Helm with the above config.webhooks configuration
Check the generated ConfigMap: `kubectl get configmap kyverno -n kyverno -o jsonpath='{.data.webhooks}'`
Observe the malformed JSON with extra brackets

**Additional Context**
The issue occurs regardless of whether namespace values are quoted or unquoted in the YAML
Using array syntax (webhooks: - namespaceSelector:) vs object syntax (webhooks: namespaceSelector:) doesn't resolve the issue
The malformed JSON prevents proper webhook configuration and namespace exclusions

**Documentation Reference**
According to the [Kyverno documentation](https://kyverno.io/docs/installation/customization/#webhooks), the  webhooks key should contain a JSON-formatted namespaceSelector object, but the Helm chart's YAML-to-JSON conversion appears to be generating malformed output.

title: [Bug] foreach with deny syntax not working in v1.15.1
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.15.0

**Environment Details:**
- **Platform**: OpenShift 4.19.7 (Kubernetes v1.32.6)
- **OpenShift Client**: 4.11.30
- **Installation Method**: Helm
- **Helm Chart**: kyverno-3.5.1
- **Kyverno Version**: v1.15.1
- **Installation Command**: 
  ```bash
  helm repo add kyverno https://kyverno.github.io/kyverno/
  helm repo update
  helm install kyverno kyverno/kyverno -n kyverno --create-namespace
  ```

### Description

When using `foreach` with `deny` syntax, the policy is accepted but the `deny` block becomes empty (`deny: {}`), causing the policy to not enforce any rules.

**Steps to Reproduce:**
1. Create a policy with `foreach` and `deny` syntax
2. Apply the policy
3. Check the policy status - `deny` block is empty
4. Policy doesn't block resources as expected

**Expected Behavior:**
Policy should validate each container and deny resources that match the conditions.

**Actual Behavior:**
Policy is accepted but `deny` block is empty, no validation occurs.

**Minimal Reproduction Case:**
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: test-foreach-deny
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  background: true
  rules:
    - name: test-foreach-deny-rule
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Deployment
      validate:
        message: "This should work but doesn't"
        foreach:
          - list: "spec.template.spec.containers[]"
            deny:
              any:
                - field: "{{ element.securityContext.privileged }}"
                  equals: true
```

**What Actually Gets Applied:**
```yaml
# The deny block becomes empty:
foreach:
  - list: "spec.template.spec.containers[]"
    deny: {} 
```
**Logs Analysis:**
The logs show that the `foreach` with `deny` syntax is being processed but not working correctly:

```bash
# All 4 rules fail at the SAME path (should be different containers):
rule deny-privileged-or-root-any-container[0] failed at path /spec/template/spec/containers/0/securityContext/
rule deny-privileged-or-root-any-container[1] failed at path /spec/template/spec/containers/0/securityContext/
rule deny-privileged-or-root-any-container[2] failed at path /spec/template/spec/containers/0/securityContext/
rule deny-privileged-or-root-any-container[3] failed at path /spec/template/spec/containers/0/securityContext/
```

- The `foreach` loop is creating multiple rule instances but they're all checking the same container
- This suggests the `foreach` iteration isn't working properly
- No explicit syntax errors are reported, making this a silent failure

title: [Bug] Generate Rule Attempts Execution for Rejected Resources
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.11.0

### Description

When using Kyverno, the generate rule is triggered in the background regardless of whether the resource creation is allowed by admission control policies. For example, if a policy rejects the creation of a namespace (e.g., bad-namespace), Kyverno still attempts to apply the generate rule for that namespace. This results in an error message such as:

```
2025-09-09T15:13:57Z ERR github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/background/generate/controller.go:301 > failed to apply generate rule error="namespaces \"bad-namespace\" not found" logger=background name=ur-86s5k policy=rolebinding-template trigger=/bad-namespace
```
**Expected Behavior:** If resource creation is blocked by an admission policy, Kyverno should not attempt to apply the generate rule for the rejected resource. Alternatively, if this check is necessary, the log level should be warning or info instead of error to avoid confusion.

title: [Bug] ClusterPolicy does not work if created before related CRD
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.15.1

### Kubernetes Version

1.34.0

### Kubernetes Platform

Bare metal

### Kyverno Rule Type

Mutate

### Description

Use case is to have kyverno cluster policy, related to a custom CRD, installed before the CRD in a k8s cluster. After upgrading to v1.15.1, it was noticed that the clusterpolicy no longer starts to work after installation of the CRD. This was working with v1.14.4. 

### Steps to reproduce

### Create a simple CRD
```
$ cat <<EOF > myresource-crd.yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: myresources.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              properties:
                message:
                  type: string
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: myresources
    singular: myresource
    kind: MyResource
    shortNames:
    - mr
EOF
```

### Create an example manifest of MyResource
```
$ cat <<EOF > myresource-1.yaml
apiVersion: example.com/v1
kind: MyResource
metadata:
  name: myresource-1
spec:
  message: "foo bar"
EOF

```

### Create a simple clusterpolicy that applies to the CRD
```
$ cat <<EOF > add-annotation-to-myresource-clusterpolicy.yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: add-annotation-in-myresources
spec:
  admission: true
  background: false
  emitWarning: false
  rules:
  - match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - MyResource
          operations:
          - CREATE
          - UPDATE
    mutate:
      patchStrategicMerge:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            example.annotation.io: foobar
    name: add-annotation
    skipBackgroundRequests: true
  validationFailureAction: Audit
EOF
```
## Command sequence 1:

### Create the clusterpolicy first:
`$ kubectl apply -f add-annotation-to-myresource-clusterpolicy.yaml`

### Then create the CRD and an example resource
```
# wait for over 10s after the cluster policy creation

$ kubectl apply -f myresource-crd.yaml
$ kubectl apply -f myresource-1.yaml

## Command sequence 2:

title: [Bug] PolicyReport for mutatingPolicy incorrectly reports a fail status
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.15.0

### Description

I think there is a problem with the way mutating policies are reported

I create one
```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: MutatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: debug-mutatingpolicy-polr

  autogen:
    mutatingAdmissionPolicy:
      enabled: false
    podControllers:
      controllers: []
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        operations: ["CREATE"]
        resources: ["pods"]
  mutations:
  - patchType: JSONPatch
    jsonPatch:
      expression: |
        has(object.metadata.labels) ?
        [
          JSONPatch{
            op: "add",
            path: "/metadata/labels/test",
            value: "foo"
          }
        ] :
        [
          JSONPatch{
            op: "add",
            path: "/metadata/labels",
            value: {"test": "foo"}
          }
        ]
```

I then create the following pod
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: dummy-pod
spec:
  containers:

      runAsNonRoot: true
      seccompProfile:
        type: "RuntimeDefault"
```

The mutation is applied as expected
```bash
$ kubectl get pod dummy-pod -ojsonpath='{.metadata.labels}'
{"test":"foo"}

At this point I do not have any policyreport in the namespace. After 5-10 seconds it appears

```bash
 $ kubectl get polr

body:
### Kyverno Version

### Description

I applied the following MutatingPolicy, and it is successfully accepted:

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1

  matchConstraints:

      expression: |

title: [Bug] remove webhookconfiguration helm hooks break with previously working release names.
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.15.0

### Description

Starting with the upgrade to helm chart version 3.5.1, our internal test pipeline showed errors on uninstalling the helm chart:

```
│ Error: warning: Hook pre-delete kyverno/templates/hooks/pre-delete-remove-mutatingwebhookconfiguration.yaml failed: 1 error occurred:
│ 	* Job.batch "kyverno-admission-controller3-remove-mutatingwebhookconfiguration" is invalid: spec.template.labels: Invalid value: "kyverno-admission-controller3-remove-mutatingwebhookconfiguration": must be no more than 63 characters
│ 
```

The new hooks from #13716 add a long suffix to the `kyverno.fullname` template, resulting in breakage for previously okay release names
```
  name: {{ template "kyverno.fullname" . }}-remove-mutatingwebhookconfiguration
```

I'll be happy to provide an MR to fix this issue but would like to discuss different options first.
My preferred fix would be to shorten the suffixes for these webhooks. Please let me know what you think of the issue.

### Fixes for the immediate problem

#### Option 1 - shorten suffixes

Previously longest suffix seems to be 26 characters: `background-controller:core` from `charts/kyverno/templates/background-controller/clusterrole.yaml`. Getting the length of these jobs to that should stop breaking anything.
Since these hooks are not persisted and only applied during deletion, this should not break anything.

#### Option 2 - truncate release name for these jobs

`-remove-validatingwebhookconfiguration` is 38 characters, truncating the fullname template to 25 characters makes the entire name short enough.

#### Option 3 - truncate fullname template globally

This option would disrupt releases for people who have longer release names now (and are unaware that uninstall will not work cleanly for them). In my opinion this is not a good change, as it is the most disruptive and has a high chance of unintended surprises.


### Avoiding issues like this in the future

There are two factors to detecting this earlier and avoiding it:
1. Dealing with varying name restrictions for Kubernetes objects.
2. Finding brokenness like this earlier

#### Name restrictions

For this bug report, summarizing the entire problem space of various Kubernetes name restrictions and different interactions of including release names in them, is too broad. There is some discussion of it around the web but I have not found definitive sources on it yet, even in helm documentation.

To provide a stable and reliable helm chart, it seems to make sense to decide on a limit for the release name and enforce it.

#### Covering this in pipelines

I spent a few minutes looking into the CI pipeline for Kyverno and it seems that while uninstall is tested, it's done with the `--no-hooks` parameter (https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/.github/workflows/conformance.yaml#L1179)

If this can be changed and a maximum release name is agreed upon, tests could be run with the max name, and resources that break with the maximum release name length would be found before release.

title: [Bug] Helm chart: Registry configured for webhooksCleanup.image.repository
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.15.0

### Description

In #13716 the kubectl image was changed from `bitnami/kubectl` to `registry.k8s.io/kubectl`, however, while `bitnami` is part of the repository, `registry.k8s.io` is a registry. Therefore, it should be configured as webhooksCleanup.image.registry:

```
webhooksCleanup:
  image:
    registry: registry.k8s.io
    repository: kubectl
```

Using a custom registry currently results in ImagePullBackOff for the hooks as `custom.registry.tld/registry.k8s.io/kubectl` cannot be found.

### Kyverno Version

1.15.0

### Description

Using the [Kyverno Helm Chart](https://artifacthub.io/packages/helm/kyverno/kyverno) following issue was noticed.

The `registry.k8s.io/kubectl` image used for the [webhooksCleanup.image](https://artifacthub.io/packages/helm/kyverno/kyverno?modal=values&path=webhooksCleanup.image) does not have a shell. It seems the container command being used is trying to use a shell though.

title: [Bug] new GlobalContext requires a restart of the reports-controller pods
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.15.0

### Description

If a new GC is created while the reports-controller pods are running, it is not recognized by the reports-controller pods until they are restarted

STEPS TO REPRODUCE

deploy kyverno and wait for everything to run
with the reports-controller running, create a new GlobalContext

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v2alpha1
kind: GlobalContextEntry
metadata:
  name: deployments
spec:
  kubernetesResource:
    group: "apps"
    version: v1
    resource: deployments
```

create a clusterpolicy and a validatingpolicy using this new GC

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: debug-gc-reports-controller
  annotations:
    pod-policies.kyverno.io/autogen-controllers: "none"
spec:
  emitWarning: true
  rules:
  - name: debug-gc-reports-controller
    context:
    - name: deployments
      globalReference:
        name: deployments
    match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - Pod
          operations:
          - CREATE
          - UPDATE
    validate:
      failureAction: Audit
      message: "debug: number of deployments in the globalcontext={{ deployments | length(@)}}"
      deny:
        conditions:
          any:
          - key: "{{request.object.metadata.name}}"
            operator: NotEquals
            value: "does_not_exists"

---
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: ValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: debug-gc-reports-controller
spec:
  validationActions:
    - Audit
  failurePolicy: Ignore
  autogen:
    podControllers:
      controllers: []
  evaluation:
    background:
      enabled: true
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
        resources: ["pods"]
  variables:
    - name: deployments
      expression: >-
        globalContext.Get("deployments", "")
  validations:
    - expression: "0 == 1"
      messageExpression: '"debug: number of deployment=" + string(variables.deployments.size())'

```

The logs of the reports-controller pods immediately show blocks of identcal lines, each of them like

```
2025-08-20T09:41:22Z ERR github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/engine/context/loaders/globalcontext.go:100 > error="failed to fetch entry key=deployments" logger=DefaultContextLoaderFactory
2025-08-20T09:41:22Z ERR github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/engine/context/loaders/globalcontext.go:56 > failed to marshal APICall data for context entry error="failed to fetch entry key=deployments" logger=DefaultContextLoaderFactory
2025-08-20T09:41:22Z ERR github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/engine/context/deferred.go:42 > failed to load data error="failed to marshal APICall data for context entry deployments: failed to fetch entry key=deployments" logger=DefaultContextLoaderFactory name=deployments
```

as well as plenty of lines like
```
2025-08-20T09:42:43Z TRC github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/cel/libs/context.go:82 > global context entry not found, returning nil entry=deployments projection= v=2
```

After some seconds for the background scans to run, the `polr` show

```yaml
apiVersion: wgpolicyk8s.io/v1alpha2
kind: PolicyReport
metadata:
  creationTimestamp: "2025-08-20T09:41:32Z"
  generation: 3
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: kyverno
  name: c7a65766-60d3-4625-8e92-825db90f3504
  namespace: foo
  ownerReferences:
  - apiVersion: v1
    kind: Pod
    name: foo-dep-66c6fd65fc-pjp5r
    uid: c7a65766-60d3-4625-8e92-825db90f3504
  resourceVersion: "494239"
  uid: 786b6766-315c-4741-80ac-1b60e95fd84f
results:
- message: 'failed to evaluate message expression: no such overload: size'
  policy: debug-gc-reports-controller
  properties:
    process: background scan
  result: fail
  scored: true
  source: KyvernoValidatingPolicy
  timestamp:
    nanos: 0
    seconds: 1755682964
- policy: debug-gc-reports-controller
  properties:
    process: background scan
  result: fail
  rule: debug-gc-reports-controller
  scored: true
  source: kyverno
  timestamp:
    nanos: 0
    seconds: 1755682964
scope:
  apiVersion: v1
  kind: Pod
  name: foo-dep-66c6fd65fc-pjp5r
  namespace: foo
  uid: c7a65766-60d3-4625-8e92-825db90f3504
summary:
  error: 0
  fail: 2
  pass: 0
  skip: 0
  warn: 0
```

You can wait for hours, with plenty of subsequent background scans, the same log lines will appear, and the `polr` will not contain the information you expect.
It will stay like this until you restart the reports-controller pods

```
kubectl rollout restart deployment kyverno-reports-controller -n kyverno
```

Only then will the policies work, and be able to use the new GC.

  properties:

  scored: true

    nanos: 0

title: [Bug] [CLI] userInfo not populated when testing ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
body:
### Kyverno CLI Version

1.15.0

### Description

Per <https://kyverno.io/blog/2023/10/04/applying-validating-admission-policies-using-kyverno-cli/#testing-validatingadmissionpolicies-using-kyverno-test> the Kyverno CLI allows you to use the `test` command to check a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy.

This works great except when you attempt to use the `userInfo` field on your `kyverno-test.yaml` file, in the evaluation of the CEL expression fields such as `request.userInfo.username` or `request.userInfo.groups` are not populated as expected.

I have verified that the file referenced by the userInfo field in `kyverno-test.yaml` is correctly loaded and parsed.

I believe this bug exists as there is a `nil` value here: https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/f73929c66f1563288e44178396e399ec44d94d4f/pkg/admissionpolicy/validate.go#L139 however the last parameter of NewAttributesRecord is where userInfo should be set per the [docs here](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission#NewAttributesRecord)

### Steps to reproduce

The below examples adapt the blog post examples <https://kyverno.io/blog/2023/10/04/applying-validating-admission-policies-using-kyverno-cli/#testing-validatingadmissionpolicies-using-kyverno-test> to add the userInfo field to `kyverno-test.yaml` and modify the CEL expression in the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy.

1. Create a new userInfo file e.g. myuser.yaml
```
apiVersion: cli.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: UserInfo
metadata:
  name: system-user
userInfo:
  username: example-system-masters
  groups:
  - system:masters
  - system:authenticated
```
2. Create modified examples from blog post:

```
cat << EOF > ./test-dir/disallow-host-path.yaml
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: disallow-host-path
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups:   ["apps"]
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations:  ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
      resources:   ["deployments"]
  validations:
    - expression: "has(request.userInfo.username)"
      message: "Request is missing userInfo.username."
EOF
```
```
cat << EOF > ./test-dir/deployments.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: deployment-pass
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx-server
        image: nginx
        volumeMounts:
          - name: temp
            mountPath: /scratch
      volumes:
      - name: temp
        emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: deployment-fail
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx-server
        image: nginx
        volumeMounts:
          - name: udev
            mountPath: /data
      volumes:
      - name: udev
        hostPath:
          path: /etc/udev
EOF
```
```
cat << EOF > ./test-dir/kyverno-test.yaml
name: disallow-host-path-test
policies:
  - disallow-host-path.yaml
resources:
  - deployments.yaml
userinfo: myuser.yaml
results:
  - policy: disallow-host-path
    resource: deployment-pass
    isValidatingAdmissionPolicy: true
    kind: Deployment
    result: pass
  - policy: disallow-host-path
    resource: deployment-fail
    isValidatingAdmissionPolicy: true
    kind: Deployment
    result: fail
EOF
```
3. Run tests `kyverno test ./test-dir`

### Expected behavior

We expect the above example will not fail with "Request is missing userInfo.username." because the username property should be set, however it currently does fail.

title: [Bug] Released CRDs are using the controller-gen development version
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.15.0

### Description

## Issue description

All single CRDs files appearing in the release since `1.13.0` are using a `controller-gen.kubebuilder.io/version: (devel)` tag when it should match the versions we are using (`0.17.3` as I'm writing this issue)


```
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  annotations:
    controller-gen.kubebuilder.io/version: (devel) # <=== THIS
  name: ephemeralreports.reports.kyverno.io
spec:
```

## Possible causes

During the release process we are not uploading the same CRDs files as the ones that are then to the `install.yaml` / helm chart. 

This is the code that upload said files: 

https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/2d801c563bdca1c879c5e1376c0b9b985d541fa6/.github/workflows/release.yaml#L286

```yaml
- name: Upload CRD manifest
  uses: svenstaro/upload-release-action@81c65b7cd4de9b2570615ce3aad67a41de5b1a13 # 2.11.2
  with:
  # ...
    file: config/crds/**/*.yaml
```

By default `config/crds` are uploaded without the version being updated

## Expected

Each single CRDs files that is uploaded should have a proper version like:

```
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  annotations:
    controller-gen.kubebuilder.io/version: v0.17.3
  name: ephemeralreports.reports.kyverno.io
```

title: [Bug] Delete only PolicyReports and ClusterPolicyReports that are managed by Kyverno
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.14.1

### Description

The `kyverno-clean-reports` job executed as a post-upgrade Helm hook deletes every PolicyReport and ClusterPolicyReport in all namespaces. When deploying Kyverno using ArgoCD, the post upgrade hook is executed after every synchronization and as a result reports that are not generated by Kyverno, such as the ones generated by the Trivy Operator PolicyReport Adapter will get deleted, which gives an inconsistent reporting.

Logs:

```
$ kubectl logs kyverno-clean-reports-pk6qf -n kyverno -f
...
deleting 14 policyreports in namespace argocd
policyreport.wgpolicyk8s.io "trivy-rbac-polr-role-argo-cd-argocd-application-controller" deleted
policyreport.wgpolicyk8s.io "trivy-rbac-polr-role-argo-cd-argocd-applicationset-controller" deleted
policyreport.wgpolicyk8s.io "trivy-rbac-polr-role-argo-cd-argocd-dex-server" deleted
...
```

The reports controller in Kyverno deletes only the reports that are managed by Kyverno, see #10794, and this job should follow the same logic too.

As a workaround, the deployment of this job can be disabled through the Helm chart (`.Values.policyReportsCleanup.enabled`).

title: [Bug] Unexpected behaviour using preconditions in one of the sample policies
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.14.1

### Description

I am trying to extend the sample cluster policy `disallow-privilege-escalation` with a precondition to avoid policy to be applied to pods (and pod controllers - autogen) with a given name. I want to use precondition for this because I am using PolicyReporter and I find very useful to have these reported as "skipped" rather than ignored. 

This is the policy I am using

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: disallow-privilege-escalation
  annotations:
    policies.kyverno.io/title: Disallow Privilege Escalation
    policies.kyverno.io/category: Security Standards
    policies.kyverno.io/severity: medium
    policies.kyverno.io/subject: Pod
    kyverno.io/kyverno-version: 1.6.0
    kyverno.io/kubernetes-version: "1.22-1.23"
    policies.kyverno.io/description: >-
      Privilege escalation, such as via set-user-ID or set-group-ID file mode, should not be allowed.
      This policy ensures the `allowPrivilegeEscalation` field is set to `false`.
spec:
  emitWarning: true
  background: true
  rules:
    - name: privilege-escalation
      match:
        any:
        - resources:
            kinds:
              - Pod
      exclude:
        any:
          - resources:
              namespaces:
                - "kube*"
      preconditions:
        all:
        - key: "{{ request.object.metadata.name }}"
          operator: AllNotIn
          value: 
            - "test-*"
            - "demo-*"
      validate:
        message: >-
          Privilege escalation is disallowed. The fields spec.containers[*].securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation,
          spec.initContainers[*].securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation and spec.ephemeralContainers[*].securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation must be set to `false`.
        pattern:
          spec:
            =(ephemeralContainers):
            - securityContext:
                allowPrivilegeEscalation: "false"
            =(initContainers):
            - securityContext:
                allowPrivilegeEscalation: "false"
            containers:
            - securityContext:
                allowPrivilegeEscalation: "false"
        failureAction: Enforce
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
```

This seems to work as expected for pods, and I see pods not compliant reported as "skipped". But for pod controllers, in this case a Deployment, I see errors like the one below: 

`failed to evaluate preconditions: failed to substitute variables in condition key: failed to resolve request.object.spec.template.metadata.name at path : JMESPath query failed: Unknown key "name" in path`

I am not sure why it's trying to resolve a path that is different to the one in the policy. E.g: 

`request.object.metadata.name != request.object.spec.template.metadata.name`

Is this expected? Is there any other way to achieve what I am trying to achieve? 

Thanks!

title: [Bug] [CLI] foreach in mutate policies breaks in test
body:
### Kyverno CLI Version

1.14.1

### Description

Trying to write tests for a mutate policy, and after getting a number of 'not found' errors, it seems that it is caused by the foreach functionality.

Policy:
```
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-security-context
spec:
  rules:
  - name: default-security-context
    match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - Deployment
          - StatefulSet
    mutate:
      patchStrategicMerge:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              securityContext:
                runAsUser: 1000
                runAsGroup: 1000
                runAsNonRoot: true
                fsGroup: 1000
                fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch
                seccompProfile:
                  type: RuntimeDefault
      foreach:
      - list: "spec.template.spec.containers"
        preconditions:
          all:
          - key: "{{ element.name }}"
            operator: NotEquals
            value: istio-proxy
          - key: "{{ element.name }}"
            operator: NotEquals
            value: istio-init
        patchStrategicMerge:
          securityContext:
            capabilities:
              drop:
                - ALL
            runAsUser: 1000
            runAsGroup: 1000
            runAsNonRoot: true
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            seccompProfile:
              type: RuntimeDefault
      - list: "spec.template.spec.initContainers"
        preconditions:
          all:
          - key: "{{ element.name }}"
            operator: NotEquals
            value: istio-proxy
          - key: "{{ element.name }}"
            operator: NotEquals
            value: istio-init
        patchStrategicMerge:
          securityContext:
            seccompProfile:
              type: RuntimeDefault
```

Commenting out the foreach sections, the test finally starts failing with diff issues (which are expected, the test is trying to prevent mutating istio sidecar resources). However, adding them back in results in a `not found` issue. Removing the primary `patchStrategicMerge` action results in the test having *zero output*, as if it silently fails and doesn't report a pass or a failure.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Try to run kyverno CLI on resource with the following test file and resource files
```
apiVersion: cli.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: default-security-context
policies:
  - default-security-context.yaml
resources:
  - resource.yaml
variables: values.yaml
results:
  - kind: Deployment
    policy: default-security-context
    rule: default-security-context
    patchedResources: case01-patched.yaml
    resources:
      - case01
    result: pass
```

resource.yaml
```
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: case01
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: nginx
          image: nginx:latest
        - name: istio-proxy
```

case01-patched.yaml
```
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: case01
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsUser: 1000
        runAsGroup: 1000
        runAsNonRoot: true
        fsGroup: 1000
        fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      containers:
        - name: nginx
          image: nginx:latest
          securityContext:
            capabilities:
              drop:
                - ALL
            runAsUser: 1000
            runAsGroup: 1000
            runAsNonRoot: true
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            seccompProfile:
              type: RuntimeDefault
        - name: istio-proxy
```

values.yaml
```
apiVersion: cli.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: Values
metadata:
  name: values
policies:
  - name: default-security-context
    resources:
      - name: case01
        values:
          request.operation: UPDATE
```

### Expected behavior

I expect the operation to either fail with a bad diff or report an error, rather than simply saying 'not found' without indicating what is not found.

title: [Bug] Helm template failing to parse webhooks configuration
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.14.1

### Description

(actually the version is 1.14.4 but I cannot choose that in the drop down above)

When configuring something like this:
```
Values:
  [...]
  config:
    webhooks:
      - name: kyverno-resource-mutating-webhook
        type: Mutating
        namespaceSelector:
          matchExpressions:
            - key: kubernetes.io/metadata.name
              operator: NotIn
              values: [list of some namespaces]
```
the resulting webhook only has the default namespaces excluded, i.e. kube-system and the namespace that Kyverno is installed in.

In version 1.12.x it was still working.

Reason seems to be the template in the Helm chart, see this line: https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/ad9e94f9ef660707518d61ef6e27ab2abba3acb9/charts/kyverno/templates/config/_helpers.tpl#L60

When you want to know whether something is a slice, do not use `typeIs` but instead use `kindIs`.
Now the execution goes to the else branch for our values, which does not find any namespaceSelector, so it uses the default.

I observe exactly the same issue as reported in https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/issues/10063 while running kyverno `v1.13.4`: The CAs have expired after 1 year of creation while the "children" certificates are still valid. Nothing triggers renewal, there is nothing in kyverno logs which would imply any issues

```
# kubectl get validatingwebhookconfiguration kyverno-resource-validating-webhook-cfg -o json  | jq -r '.webhooks[0].clientConfig.caBundle' | base64 -d | openssl x509 -noout -dates

title: [Bug] Doesnot handle generateName edge case in matchesResourceRules when GetName() is empty
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.14.1

### Kubernetes Version

1.30.x

### Kubernetes Platform

KinD

### Kyverno Rule Type

Other

### Description

**pkg/cel/matching/matcher.go**
Function: `matchesResourceRules`

The current implementation of `matchesResourceRules` includes a TODO for the following edge case:
```
// TODO: GetName() can return an empty string if the user is relying on
// the API server to generate the name... figure out what to do for this edge case
```
This happens when `.metadata.generateName` is used in the resource instead of `.metadata.name.` In such cases, `attr.GetName()` will return an empty string during admission time since the name is not yet generated by the API server.

If `namedRule.ResourceNames` is defined in a webhook configuration, this logic may fail to match resources where the name is autogenerated, resulting in unexpected admission behavior.

### Kyverno CLI Version

1.14.1

### Description

When creating a MutatingAdmissionPolicy that matches ConfigMaps named `zk-kafka-address`, the policy is applied to all configmaps without considering their names.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create the following MAP:
```
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: MutatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: add-label-to-configmap
spec:
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups:     [""]
      apiVersions:   ["v1"]
      operations:    ["CREATE"]
      resources:     ["configmaps"]
      resourceNames: ["zk-kafka-address"]
  failurePolicy: Fail
  reinvocationPolicy: Never
  mutations:
    - patchType: "ApplyConfiguration"
      applyConfiguration:
        expression: >
          object.metadata.?labels["lfx-mentorship"].hasValue() ? 
              Object{} :
              Object{ metadata: Object.metadata{ labels: {"lfx-mentorship": "kyverno"}}}

```
apiVersion: v1
data:

title: [Bug] [CLI] CRD Support for new Policy Types without Cluster connection
body:
### Kyverno CLI Version

1.14.0 / 1.15.0

### Description

Currently it is not possible to use the new Policy Types (ValidatingPolicy, ImageValidatingPolicy, MutatingPolicy, etc...) against a CRD if no cluster connection (with the required CRD installed) is available.

The used RESTMapper in this case only supports API Group based on a static file and can not be dynamically extended.

In case of MutatingPolicies the TypeConverter is a second limitation, it is based on an openapi.Client. This client needs, in case of no cluster connection, to be extended with the used CRD. This is currently also not possible.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Apply a new policy type against an CRD without cluster connection
2. gvk can not be mapped to the gvr

CLI except CRDs and can be used against them

title: [Bug] UpdateRequest can fail to create when mutating a resource
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.14.1

### Description

Tested on main branch. This looks to be similar to #8011 but in the background-controller.

If a mutate-update cluster policy is defined which mutates a resource that has a non-RFC1123 complaint name it will fail, because the name of the resource is stored in a label on the UpdateRequest which must be compliant.  For example, Roles commonly have a `:` in them and these can't be used as label values.

More specifically, this seems to only cause a problem if the only Roles defined contain a `:`. If any do not, then an UpdateRequest is created and will mutate *all* Roles limited by the namespace in the matcher.

Example ClusterPolicy, mutates a role:

```
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: add-label-to-roles
spec:
  mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate: true
  rules:
    - name: add-label-to-roles
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Role
          namespaces:
            - default
      mutate:
        targets:
          - apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
            kind: Role
        patchStrategicMerge:
          metadata:
            labels:
              processed-by-kyverno: "yes"
```

Example role:
```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: pod:reader
  namespace: default
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["pods"]
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
```

The result is that we don't get the `pod:reader` Role mutated. Logs show failure on the UpdateRequest label:
```
2025-06-10T17:31:36Z ERR github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/policy/mutate.go:49 > failed to create new UR on policy update error="UpdateRequest.kyverno.io \"ur-8wtjm\" is invalid: metadata.labels: Invalid value: \"pod:reader\": a valid label must be an empty string or consist of alphanumeric characters, '-', '_' or '.', and must start and end with an alphanumeric character (e.g. 'MyValue',  or 'my_value',  or '12345', regex used for validation is '(([A-Za-z0-9][-A-Za-z0-9_.]*)?[A-Za-z0-9])?')" logger=PolicyController policy=add-label-to-roles rule=add-label-to-roles rule type=mutate target=rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1/Role/default/pod:reader
```

title: [Bug] Kyverno admission controller fails to start in version 1.14.0 when using HostNetwork: true
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.14.0

### Description
Kyverno admission controller in version v1.14.0 fails to start metric server with port `8080`. The error states  address already in use error when using `hostNetwork: true` [configuration](https://kyverno.io/docs/troubleshooting/#kyverno-fails-on-eks).

**Environment**
Kyverno Version: 1.14.0
Helm Chart Version: 3.4.0
Kubernetes Version: 1.32
Platform: Amazon EKS
CNI: Calico (not AWS CNI)
Deployment Method: Helm via FluxCD

**Configuration**
```yaml
admissionController:
  replicas: 2
  hostNetwork: true
  serviceMonitor:
    enabled: true
  webhookServer:
    port: 10254
  startupProbe:
    httpGet:
      port: 10254
  livenessProbe:
    httpGet:
      port: 10254
  readinessProbe:
    httpGet:
      port: 10254
  metering:
    port: 10255
  podAntiAffinity:
    preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - podAffinityTerm:
          labelSelector:
            matchExpressions:
              - key: app.kubernetes.io/component
                operator: In
                values:
                  - admission-controller
          topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
        weight: 100
      - podAffinityTerm:
          labelSelector:
            matchExpressions:
              - key: app.kubernetes.io/component
                operator: In
                values:
                  - admission-controller
          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
        weight: 99
  priorityClassName: 'system-cluster-critical'
```

**Expected Behavior**
Kyverno should not attempt to bind to port 8080 unless specified or give the possibility to change the port number.

**Actual Behavior**
Kyverno admission controller fails to start with the following error:
`{"level":"error","error":"failed to start metrics server: failed to create listener: listen tcp :8080: bind: address already in use","logger":"setup","time":"2025-05-07T20:00:22Z","message":"failed to start manager"}`

**Steps to Reproduce**

1. Deploy Kyverno v1.14.0 using Helm chart v3.4.0 on EKS with Calico CNI
2. Configure hostNetwork: true for admission controller
3. Attempt to upgrade/install Kyverno
4. Observe the port conflict error

**Troubleshooting and workaround Attempted**
Since the error message specifies the metrics server, we configured explicit metrics port via metricsService.port: 10256 for the admissionController. Issue persists despite configuration changes. We do have other applications outside of Kyverno using hostNetwork that might be using already port 8080.

title: [Bug] Wildcards in APIVersion not working when using CEL expression
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.14.1

### Description

When using a wildcard in `apiVersion` in the `resources.kinds` field of a Kyverno policy that only uses a CEL expression, the policy fails to deploy with the following error:
```
admission webhook "validate-policy.kyverno.svc" denied the request: no unique match for kind Cluster
```
However, the wildcard works as expected when:
- The policy uses only a pattern
- The policy uses both a pattern and a CEL expression

This behavior seems inconsistent and likely a bug.

#### Policy that Fails (CEL-only)
```
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: rds-cluster-policy-only-cel
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Audit
  background: false
  rules:
    - name: label-should-be-present-cel
      match:
        any:
        - resources:
            kinds:
              - rds.aws.upbound.io/*/Cluster
      validate:
        failureAction: Audit
        message: "The label `app.example.com/name` is required."
        cel:
          expressions:
            - expression: "has(request.object.metadata.labels['app.example.com/name']) && request.object.metadata.labels['app.example.com/name'].matches('^.+$')"
              message: "Label 'app.example.com/name' must be present and not empty"
```

#### Policy that Works (Pattern + CEL)
```
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: rds-cluster-policy-both
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Audit
  background: false
  rules:
    - name: label-should-be-present
      match:
        any:
        - resources:
            kinds:
              - rds.aws.upbound.io/*/Cluster
      validate:
        failureAction: Audit
        message: "The label `app.example.com/name` is required."
        pattern:
          metadata:
            labels:
              app.example.com/name: "?*"
    - name: label-should-be-present-cel
      match:
        any:
        - resources:
            kinds:
              - rds.aws.upbound.io/*/Cluster
      validate:
        failureAction: Audit
        message: "The label `app.example.com/name` is required."
        cel:
          expressions:
            - expression: "has(request.object.metadata.labels['app.example.com/name']) && request.object.metadata.labels['app.example.com/name'].matches('^.+$')"
              message: "Label 'app.example.com/name' must be present and not empty"
```

#### Policy that Works (Pattern-only)
```
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: rds-cluster-policy-only-pattern
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Audit
  background: false
  rules:
    - name: label-should-be-present
      match:
        any:
        - resources:
            kinds:
              - rds.aws.upbound.io/*/Cluster
      validate:
        failureAction: Audit
        message: "The label `app.example.com/name` is required."
        pattern:
          metadata:
            labels:
              app.example.com/name: "?*"
```

title: [Bug] patchesJson6902 mutation strips newlines from multiline string fields
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.11.0

### Kubernetes Version

1.28.x

### Kubernetes Platform

KinD

### Kyverno Rule Type

Mutate

### Description

having an issue with Kyverno mutations using patchesJson6902 on a multiline string field (like a YAML config stored as a string in a CR). The main problem is that the multiline string (element.config) doesn’t keep its newline characters (\n) when accessed inside the policy. Instead, it looks flattened into a single line, with spaces where the newlines used to be.

```yaml 
  - affinity:
      podAffinity:
        requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        - labelSelector:
            matchExpressions:
            - key: io.observer.persistence
              operator: In
              values:
              - "true"
          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
    config: |-
      plugins:
        io.observer.coordinator:
          namespace: default
          collect_interval: 2m
```

When I run the policy below. 

```yaml 
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: patch-collect-interval
spec:
  rules:
  - name: mutate-collect-interval
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Observer
    mutate:
      foreach:
      - list: "request.object.spec.topology"
        preconditions:
          all:
          - key: "{{ element.name }}"
            operator: Equals
            value: operator
        patchesJson6902: |-
          - op: replace
            path: '/spec/topology/{{ elementIndex }}/config'
            value: "{{ element.config, 'collect_interval: 2m', 'collect_interval: 30s',`1`) }}"
```

```yaml 
  - affinity:
      podAffinity:
        requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        - labelSelector:
            matchExpressions:
            - key: io.observer.persistence
              operator: In
              values:
              - "true"
          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
    config: 'plugins: io.observer.coordinator: namespace:
      default collect_interval: 30s'
```



### Steps to reproduce

See Description

### Expected behavior

The mutation policy should be able to replace or modify parts of multiline YAML strings without flattening or losing newline characters.

The original formatting of the multiline string field (e.g., element.config) should be preserved after mutation.

The replaced string should remain valid YAML with proper indentation and line breaks.

title: [Bug] Error Parsing attestations name with "-" in ImageValidatingPolicy
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.14.1

### Description

When following along the docs for setting up a cosign keyless image verification policy here: https://kyverno.io/docs/policy-types/image-validating-policy/#cosign-keyless-signature-and-attestation-verification, the attestations is defined as:
```yaml
  attestations:
    - name: cosign-attes
      intoto:
        type: cosign.sigstore.dev/attestation/vuln/v1
```

and the validations is defined as:
```yaml
  validations:
    - expression: >-
        images.containers.map(image, verifyImageSignatures(image,  [attestors.cosign])).all(e, e > 0)
      message: "Failed image signature verification"
    - expression: >-
        images.containers.map(image, verifyAttestationSignatures(image, attestations.cosign-attes, [attestors.cosign])).all(e, e > 0)
      message: "Failed to verify vulnerability scan attestation with Cosign keyless"
```

However when applying the policy one will get an error like this (this error is from Argo):
```
error when patching "/dev/shm/1364731121": admission webhook "validate-policy.kyverno.svc" denied the request: spec.validations[1].expression: Invalid value: "images.containers.map(image, verifyAttestationSignatures(image, attestations.cosign-attes, [attestors.cosign])).all(e, e > 0)": ERROR: <input>:1:84: found no matching overload for '_-_' applied to '(string, !error!)' | images.containers.map(image, verifyAttestationSignatures(image, attestations.cosign-attes, [attestors.cosign])).all(e, e > 0) | ...................................................................................^ ERROR: <input>:1:85: undeclared reference to 'attes' (in container '') | images.containers.map(image, verifyAttestationSignatures(image, attestations.cosign-attes, [attestors.cosign])).all(e, e > 0) | ....................................................................................^
```

It seems like the hyphen is causing parsing errors for `attestation.cosign-attes`. 
Possibly a documentation issue instead?

title: [Bug] kyverno-policies failing to install as part of an umbrella helm chart.
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.14.1

### Description

At my organisation we configure all the underlay infrastructure for kubernetes clusters via a single umbrella helm chart.

Installing charts `kyverno` and `kyverno-policies` as part of the same umbrella helm chart fails as the policies are applied before the `kyverno` chart is installed.

I've provided a minimal example here:
```bash
$ cat Chart.yaml
   1   apiVersion: v2
   2   name: umbrella
   3   description: A Helm chart for Kubernetes
   4   type: application
   5   version: 0.1.0
   6   dependencies:
   7     - name: kyverno
   8       version: 3.4.1
   9       repository: https://kyverno.github.io/kyverno
  10     - name: kyverno-policies
  11       version: 3.4.1
  12       repository: https://kyverno.github.io/kyverno

$ helm install -n kyverno --create-namespace kyverno-umbrella .
Error: INSTALLATION FAILED: unable to build kubernetes objects from release manifest: [resource mapping not found for name: "disallow-capabilities" namespace: "" from "": no matches for kind "ClusterPolicy" in version "kyverno.io/v1"
ensure CRDs are installed first, resource mapping not found for name: "disallow-host-namespaces" namespace: "" from "": no matches for kind "ClusterPolicy" in version "kyverno.io/v1"
ensure CRDs are installed first, resource mapping not found for name: "disallow-host-path" namespace: "" from "": no matches for kind "ClusterPolicy" in version "kyverno.io/v1"
ensure CRDs are installed first, resource mapping not found for name: "disallow-host-ports" namespace: "" from "": no matches for kind "ClusterPolicy" in version "kyverno.io/v1"
ensure CRDs are installed first, resource mapping not found for name: "disallow-host-process" namespace: "" from "": no matches for kind "ClusterPolicy" in version "kyverno.io/v1"
ensure CRDs are installed first, resource mapping not found for name: "disallow-privileged-containers" namespace: "" from "": no matches for kind "ClusterPolicy" in version "kyverno.io/v1"
ensure CRDs are installed first, resource mapping not found for name: "disallow-proc-mount" namespace: "" from "": no matches for kind "ClusterPolicy" in version "kyverno.io/v1"
ensure CRDs are installed first, resource mapping not found for name: "disallow-selinux" namespace: "" from "": no matches for kind "ClusterPolicy" in version "kyverno.io/v1"
ensure CRDs are installed first, resource mapping not found for name: "restrict-apparmor-profiles" namespace: "" from "": no matches for kind "ClusterPolicy" in version "kyverno.io/v1"
ensure CRDs are installed first, resource mapping not found for name: "restrict-seccomp" namespace: "" from "": no matches for kind "ClusterPolicy" in version "kyverno.io/v1"
ensure CRDs are installed first, resource mapping not found for name: "restrict-sysctls" namespace: "" from "": no matches for kind "ClusterPolicy" in version "kyverno.io/v1"
ensure CRDs are installed first]
```

Since helm does not offer installation ordering of depependencies and packaging crds with `kyverno-policies` would be undesirable, the easiest way to resolve this is to allow users to configure annotations to be passed to the `kyverno-policies` chart policies. This would allow users to make use of helm hooks to apply the policies post installation of the `kyverno` chart.

body:
### Kyverno CLI Version

1.14.2

### Description

`kyverno test` and `kyverno apply -r` fail with a cryptic error message when mutating existing resources of certain kinds, e.g. PersistentVolumeClaim.

The test reports `: not found`.

The reproducer succeeds after adding persistentvolumeclaims to fake discovery client:
```diff
diff --git a/pkg/clients/dclient/fake.go b/pkg/clients/dclient/fake.go
index 9baf85ca6..a7e09d2ec 100644
--- a/pkg/clients/dclient/fake.go
+++ b/pkg/clients/dclient/fake.go
@@ -74,6 +74,7 @@ func NewFakeDiscoveryClient(registeredResources []schema.GroupVersionResource) *
                {Version: "v1", Resource: "resourcequotas"},
                {Version: "v1", Resource: "secrets"},
                {Version: "v1", Resource: "serviceaccounts"},
+               {Version: "v1", Resource: "persistentvolumeclaims"},
                {Group: "apps", Version: "v1", Resource: "daemonsets"},
                {Group: "apps", Version: "v1", Resource: "deployments"},
                {Group: "apps", Version: "v1", Resource: "statefulsets"},
```

The same code path is taken when doing `kyverno apply -r` (applying to local files), it also fails with `: not found`.

I am confident that none of the resource kinds outside of the list in `fake.go` work in this situation, I'm just taking `PersistentVolumeClaim` as an example. 

I couldn't find any docs mentioning this restriction of `apply -r`/`test`.

Could be the same problem as in https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/issues/13140

### Steps to reproduce

## kyverno-test.yaml
```
apiVersion: cli.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: Test

  name: test-mutate-existing

- pod.yaml
targetResources:
- pvc.yaml

```

          kinds:
          - Pod
