```
      targets: # <-- mutate existing 
      - apiVersion: v1
        kind: PersistentVolumeClaim # <-- not in the list in fake.go
        name: pvc
      patchStrategicMerge:
        metadata:
          labels:
            foo: bar
```

## pod.yaml

```
apiVersion: v1

metadata:
  name: pod

  containers:
```

### Description

In the latest Kyverno version using image validating policy with OCI repository that requires credentials.

title: [Bug] Kyverno-clean-reports Job Completes Too Quickly, ArgoCD Hook Finalizer Never Removed
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.14.0

### Kubernetes Version

1.32.x

### Kubernetes Platform

GKE

### Kyverno Rule Type

Other

### Description

When deploying Kyverno via Helm and syncing with Argo CD, the kyverno-clean-reports Job (which is annotated as a post-upgrade hook) occasionally completes so quickly that Argo CD doesn’t observe its status transition to Succeeded.

This results in the Argo CD finalizer (argocd.argoproj.io/hook-finalizer) not being removed, which in turn causes the Job to remain in a deletionTimestamp state and blocks the application sync from completing


**Whatmakes this interesting**

In a second cluster, where the same Job runs more slowly (due to latency since cluster is based in US servers), the behavior is fine — Argo CD observes the transition and removes the finalizer properly.

This strongly suggests a race condition between the Job completing and Argo CD’s reconciliation loop observing its status.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install Kyverno via chart using ArgoCD
2. have a cluster with multiple namespaces
3. Update values or chart version for kyverno
4. Run a sync operation through ArgoCD
5. Observe that the Job kyverno-clean-reports starts and the pod finishes and get deleted but the Job gets stuck
6. Job keeps getting updated with new resource IDs
7. Sync operation is never marked as succeeded.

### Expected behavior

Argo CD should observe the Job’s completion and remove the finalizer, allowing the Job to be deleted according to the hook-delete-policy.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Kyverno logs

```Shell
waiting for deletion of batch/Job/kyverno-clean-reports

In the cluster, the Job is marked with deletionTimestamp, but is stuck because the finalizer remains:

finalizers:
  - argocd.argoproj.io/hook-finalizer
```

title: [Bug] Prometheus labels don't follow best practices
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.14.1

### Description

We noticed that Kyverno uses not recommended label names for its metric `kyverno_http_requests_duration_seconds_bucket` based on the error below from Prometheus which is trying to send metrics via remote_write to Mimir endpoint (redacted):

```json
{"time":"2025-05-12T08:10:20.118405883Z","level":"ERROR","source":"queue_manager.go:1694","msg":"non-recoverable error","component":"remote","remote_name":"ddd918","url":"http://mimir-gateway.mimir/api/v1/push","failedSampleCount":2000,"failedHistogramCount":0,"failedExemplarCount":0,"err":"server returned HTTP status 400 Bad Request: received a series with an invalid label: 'http.method' series: 'kyverno_http_requests_duration_seconds_bucket{clusterName=\"my-cluster\", container=\"kyverno\", endpoint=\"metrics-port\", http.method=\"POST\", http.url=\"/validate/fail?timeout=10s\", instance=\"1.2.3.4' (err-mimir-label-invalid)\n"}
```  
 
Based on documentation ([link](https://prometheus.io/docs/concepts/data_model/#metric-names-and-labels)), labels should match the regex `[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*` for the best experience and compatibility. However, `http.method` and `http.url` are being used here.  
This is causing issues as the metric is not accepted by Mimir, which is the central storage for our metrics.  
✋🏼 I know that Prometheus 3.x supports UTF-8 for labels and metrics, but I would prefer not to switch to these UTF-8 labels that quickly to ensure compatibility and user experience.

title: [Bug] [CLI] `VPOL/IVPOL` not resolving deprecated API versions due to missing client-go scheme registrations
body:
### Kyverno CLI Version

1.14.0

### Description

Deprecated API versions (e.g., batch/v1beta1, discovery.k8s.io/v1beta1, events.k8s.io/v1beta1, policy/v1beta1, etc.) are not registered by default in the client-go scheme for use with `ValidatingPolicy` (VPOL) or `ImageValidatingPolicy` (IVPOL) . title: [Bug] Mutating policy not applied to existing ServiceAccounts unless updated manually
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.13.4

### Kubernetes Version

1.30.x

### Kubernetes Platform

Other (specify in description)

### Kyverno Rule Type

Mutate

### Description

I'm observing an issue where a `Mutate` policy that adds image pull secrets to `ServiceAccount` resources is not being applied to existing ServiceAccounts. The mutation works correctly for:

- Newly created ServiceAccounts
- Existing ServiceAccounts when they are updated (e.g., via kubectl apply or patch)
- Existing ServiceAccounts when their namespace is modified or updated

However, the policy is not automatically applied to existing ServiceAccounts unless they are explicitly changed in some way. This seems to differ from how mutations are applied in some other resources via background processing.

I am encountering the Issue on RKE2 as well as on local Rancher Desktop and Minikube. Issue has also been reproduced on Kyverno 1.14.0.

### Kyverno Policy:

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: add-image-pull-secret
  annotations:
    policies.kyverno.io/title: Add ghcr Image Pull Secret to xyz-* ServiceAccounts
    policies.kyverno.io/category: Security
    policies.kyverno.io/severity: medium
    policies.kyverno.io/subject: ServiceAccount
    policies.kyverno.io/description: >-
      This policy adds the ghcr image pull secret to all xyz-* serviceaccounts.
spec:
  rules:
    - name: add-image-pull-secret
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds:
                - ServiceAccount
              namespaces:
                - "xyz-*"
      skipBackgroundRequests: false
      mutate:
        mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate: true
        targets:
          - apiVersion: v1
            kind: ServiceAccount
            name: "{{request.object.metadata.name}}"
            namespace: "{{request.object.metadata.namespace}}"
        patchStrategicMerge:
          imagePullSecrets:
            - name: ghcr-registry-creds
  # Policy behavior configuration
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  background: true
  admission: true
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a Kyverno `Mutate` policy that adds an `imagePullSecret` to all `ServiceAccounts` with `mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate: true` and `targets` set
2. Apply policy
3. Observe that
- Existing ServiceAccounts do not have the imagePullSecret added until they are manually updated.
4. Manually edit or create a namespace or ServiceAccount (e.g. add a label)
5. Observe that
- The edited/new ServiceAccounts created after the policy is in place get mutated as expected (as well as default ServiceAccounts when only Namespace is edited for example).


### Expected behavior

I'd expect the mutation to be applied to existing ServiceAccounts automatically via background processing, without requiring manual updates.

### Screenshots

```Shell

```

title: [Bug] PolicyException `match` changes not applied to existing generated resources
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.14.0

### Description

I'm trying to dynamically modify a list of excluded namespaces without having to recreate all network policies generated by a `ClusterPolicy`. 

Because `ClusterPolicy.spec.rules.exclude` and `ClusterPolicy.spec.rules.match` are immutable, I tried using `PolicyException` to add/exclude namespaces from my `ClusterPolicy`.

**Cpol.yaml**:
```YAML
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: netpol
spec:
  rules:
  - name: kyverno-egress
    match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - Namespace
    generate:
      generateExisting: true
      apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
      kind: NetworkPolicy
      name: kyverno-egress
      namespace: "{{request.object.metadata.name}}"
      synchronize: true
      data:
        spec:
          podSelector: {}
          policyTypes:
            - Egress
          egress:
            - to:
                - ipBlock:
                    cidr: 0.0.0.0/0
              ports:
                - port: 443
```

**Polex.yaml**:
```YAML
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v2
kind: PolicyException
metadata:
  name: netpol
  namespace: kyverno
spec:
  exceptions:
    - policyName: netpol
      ruleNames:
        - '*'
  match:
    any:
      - resources:
          namespaces:
            - applications
```

Adding/removing items in `PolicyException.spec.match.any.resources.namespaces` does not remove/generate (respectively) the `kyverno-egress` network policy in said namespaces.

verifyImages

### Description

When using `kubectl debug` to attach an ephemeral container to a pod, with a different image than the pod, the validation step fails, when starting the ephemeral container with the same image as the target pod - it validates successfully.

The logs show that the Notary signatures are successfully verified for both images (pod and ephemeral container images), what raises my suspicion is the `kyverno.io/verify-images` annotation. There's a call to add the second image (for the ephemeral container) to the annotation, but the admission-request-dump after it does not include this second image.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Create the policy
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-signed-images-only
spec:
  admission: true
  background: false
  emitWarning: false
  failurePolicy: Fail
  rules:
  - match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - Pod
    name: check-image
    skipBackgroundRequests: true
    verifyImages:
    - attestors:
      - count: 1
        entries:
        - certificates:
            cert: |-
              -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
              ...
              -----END CERTIFICATE-----
          signatureAlgorithm: sha256
      failureAction: Enforce
      imageReferences:
      - '*'
      mutateDigest: false
      required: true
      type: Notary
      useCache: false
      verifyDigest: false
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  webhookTimeoutSeconds: 30
```
2. Start a pod with a signed image `kubectl run test --image=ghcr.io/kyverno/test-verify-image:signed`
3. Attach an ephemeral container with another signed image `kubectl debug test --container=debug1 --image=ghcr.io/kyverno/test-verify-image:another-signed --target=test`

title: [Bug] [CLI] ValidatingPolicies don't work with `--cluster` flag
body:
### Kyverno CLI Version

1.14.0

### Description

ValidatingPolicies are not applied to resources deployed in the cluster when using the flag `--cluster`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create two deployments:
```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: good-deployment
  labels:
    app: nginx
    env: prod
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:latest
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: bad-deployment
  labels:
    app: nginx
    env: testing
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:latest
```

```
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: ValidatingPolicy
```

title: [Bug] podSecurity exception for Running as Non-root control doesn't work
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.13.4

### Description

Hello,

I have came across issue when defining exceptions for podSecurity subrules.

With policy:
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: podsecurity-subrule-restricted
spec:
  background: true
  validationFailureAction: Audit
  rules:
  - name: podsecurity-subrule-restricted
    match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - Pod
    validate:
      podSecurity:
        level: restricted
        version: latest
        exclude:
        - controlName: Running as Non-root
          images:
          - busybox:*
```

and resource:
```yaml
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  securityContext:
    runAsNonRoot: false
  containers:
  - image: busybox:latest
    name: test
```

Kyverno reports:
```
  Message:    Validation rule 'podsecurity-subrule-restricted' failed. It violates PodSecurity "restricted:latest": (Forbidden reason: runAsNonRoot != true, field error list: [spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot is forbidden, forbidden values found: false])
  Policy:     podsecurity-subrule-restricted
  Properties:
    Controls:       runAsNonRoot
    Controls JSON:  [{"ID":"runAsNonRoot","Name":"Running as Non-root","Images":["docker.io/busybox:latest"]}]
    Standard:       restricted
    Version:        latest
  Result:           fail
  Rule:             podsecurity-subrule-restricted
```

I included only relevant part, I am aware that presented resource lacks other securityContext values, and actual message would cover them too. The thing is this behaviour is very surprising because these exceptions work for any other control covered by podSecurity. That's why I wanted to highlight this particular one. In addition runAsNonRoot is defined at both pod and container level. Exception does not work only on pod level. I checked that by defining exclude part like:
```yaml
- controlName: Running as Non-root
  images:
  - busybox:*
  restrictedField: spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot # doesn't work
  values:
  - "false"
- controlName: Running as Non-root
  images:
  - busybox:*
  restrictedField: spec.containers[*].securityContext.runAsNonRoot # works
  values:
  - "false"
```
And as mentioned it is only not taken into consideration for pod level runAsNonRoot control, what seems unexpected. Therefore I report this as a bug.

I didn't find anything relevant reported in admission controller or reports controller logs.

Regards

title: [Bug] Autogen rules from IVPOL persist in webhook targeting Pod controllers (e.g., Deployment) after original policy deletion
body:
### Kyverno Version

`v1.14.0`

### Cluster Version

tested with  `v1.32.0` , `v1.28.13` , `v1.29.8` , `v1.31.0` and `v1.30.4` 

### Description

When an **ImageValidatingPolicy (IVPOL)** targets `Pod` with `autogen` enabled, Kyverno automatically generates additional rules for higher-level Pod controllers such as `Deployment`.

However, after deleting the original Pod-targeted policy, the autogen-generated rules are **not fully removed** from the webhook configuration.

If you then create a new IVPOL (**Policy B**) that explicitly targets a controller like `Deployment`, Kyverno incorrectly enforces **both** the newly created policy and the leftover autogen rules from the deleted policy. This results in **unexpected and incorrect enforcement** behavior.

In contrast, if a new policy is created that again targets `Pod` with autogen enabled, the autogen rules are properly rewritten, and no stale behavior is observed — confirming that the issue specifically affects scenarios where a Pod controller-targeted policy is applied after a Pod-targeted policy is deleted.

Also, if no new policy is created after deletion, the stale webhook rules do not trigger enforcement — indicating that stale autogen logic is only revived when a controller-targeted policy is introduced.

---

### Reproduction Steps

1. Apply any **ImageValidatingPolicy (IVPOL)** that targets `Pod` with `autogen` enabled.
2. Delete this Pod-targeted policy.
3. Apply a new IVPOL that explicitly targets `Deployment`.
4. Create a `Deployment` and observe whether it is enforced by the **deleted** Pod policy.

---

### Example

- Apply the [`image-data`](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/tree/main/test/conformance/chainsaw/image-validating-policies/context/imagedata/image-data) policy, which targets `Pod` with autogen enabled.
- Delete the `image-data` policy.
- Apply the [`imagereference`](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/tree/main/test/conformance/chainsaw/image-validating-policies/context/imagedata/imagereference) policy that explicitly targets `Deployment` ([policy.yaml](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/test/conformance/chainsaw/image-validating-policies/context/imagedata/imagereference/policy.yaml)).
- Observe that the deleted `Pod` policy continues to affect the `Deployment`.

This behavior confirms that **autogen-generated rules are not properly cleaned up** when a Pod-targeted policy is deleted and followed by a controller-targeted policy.

title: [Bug] policy reports failing to update/rescan
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.13.4

### Description

I have a Kyverno policy set to `Audit` that has been failing against some resources for some time.  Recently, I fixed these resources (such that they now pass the policy), but the policy report is not updating from `fail` to `pass`.

My understanding is that there are three triggers for performing a background scan for a policy:
- Updating the underlying resource
- Updating the policy itself
- The background scan interval for reports-controller

I have tried to use these triggers to re-evaluate the policy to produce an updated report, and have not been successful:
- I've updated the underlying resource to pass the policy
- I've updated the policy itself by changing some fields
- I've waited for the background scan to run at the configured interval (1 hour).

However, if I restart the reports-controller (via `kubectl rollout restart`), it eventually does a background scan and updates the policy within a few minutes

Extra debugging:

```bash
# see the last time this was updated
$ kubectl get policyreport -n cert-manager 0795f302-65b5-4f7c-a423-1cbcfc854bdf -ojsonpath='{.results[0].timestamp}'
{"nanos":0,"seconds":1743692302} # 8 days ago as of opening this issue

# see the policy summary
$ kubectl get policyreport -n cert-manager 0795f302-65b5-4f7c-a423-1cbcfc854bdf -ojsonpath='{.summary}'
{"error":0,"fail":1,"pass":0,"skip":0,"warn":0}

# restart the reports controller
$ kubectl -n kyverno rollout restart deploy/kyverno-reports-controller
deployment.apps/kyverno-reports-controller restarted

# wait a few minutes, then check policy timestamp again
$ kubectl get policyreport -n cert-manager 0795f302-65b5-4f7c-a423-1cbcfc854bdf -ojsonpath='{.results[0].timestamp}'
{"nanos":0,"seconds":1744405045}

# policy is now passing
$ kubectl get policyreport -n cert-manager 0795f302-65b5-4f7c-a423-1cbcfc854bdf -ojsonpath='{.summary}'
{"error":0,"fail":0,"pass":1,"skip":0,"warn":0}
```

title: [Bug] Critical vulnerability CVE-2025-22871 detected
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.13.4

### Description

Newly fixed vulnerability in Go's net/http package:

**Vulnerability details:**
https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-22871

**Description:**
The Golang Go standard net/http package is vulnerable to an HTTP request smuggling issue due to how bare line-feed (LF) characters can be accepted as a line terminator in chunk-size lines during chunked transfer encoding.

The acceptance of LF characters in chunk-size lines issue could allow for HTTP request smuggling when combined with implementations that incorrectly permit a bare carriage-return (CR) character in a chunk extension.

**Fix available in:**
• Go 1.24.2 – [commit](https://github.com/golang/go/commit/ac1f5aa3d6)

We have two mutation policies trying to append extra fields under envFrom using patchStrategicMerge. If any of them gets triggered standalone, it works as expected. However, if both of them get triggered, there is only one field gets appended. Looks like one will override the other one.

```
                    name: '{{ EnvConfigMapName }}'
                name: flink-main-container
```
2. The second mutation policy -

title: [Bug] VAP generation fails when `validationActions` is unset
body:
### Problem Statement

In case we have a ValidatingPolicy that doesn't set the `spec.validationActions`, there is no VAP generated.
```
2025-04-09T12:45:08+01:00 ERR ../../pkg/utils/controller/run.go:128 > Failed to process request error="failed to create validatingadmissionpolicybinding vpol-disallow-privilege-escalation-binding: ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding.admissionregistration.k8s.io \"vpol-disallow-privilege-escalation-binding\" is invalid: spec.validationActions: Required value: at least one validation action is required" id=1 logger=validatingadmissionpolicy-generate-controller/worker obj=ValidatingPolicy/disallow-privilege-escalation
```

To reproduce the issue:
1. Create the following ValidatingPolicy:
```
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: ValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: disallow-privilege-escalation
spec:
  autogen:
    validatingAdmissionPolicy:
      enabled: true
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups:   [""]
      apiVersions: [v1]
      operations:  [CREATE, UPDATE]
      resources:   ["pods"]
  matchConditions:
    - name: "check-prod-label"  
      expression: >- 
        has(object.metadata.labels) && has(object.metadata.labels.prod) && object.metadata.labels.prod == 'true'
  validations:
    - expression: >- 
        object.spec.containers.all(container, has(container.securityContext) &&
        has(container.securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation) &&
        container.securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation == false)
      message: >-
        Privilege escalation is disallowed. The field
        spec.containers[*].securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation must be set to `false`.
```
2. Check the policy status:
```
conditionStatus:
    conditions:
    - lastTransitionTime: "2025-04-09T11:45:06Z"
      message: Webhook configured.
      reason: Succeeded
      status: "True"
      type: WebhookConfigured
    - lastTransitionTime: "2025-04-09T11:45:06Z"
      message: Policy is ready for reporting.
      reason: Succeeded
      status: "True"
      type: RBACPermissionsGranted
    message: ""
    ready: true
  generated: false
```

### Solution Description

The `validationActions` field is required in the ValidatingPolicy CRD, but we don't check if it is set or not on the policy creation event.
https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/b0aa9a233581b409c9fea2de336140b67d10cbf3/api/policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1/validating_policy.go#L191-L194

title: [Bug] [CLI] Kyverno cant verify attestation from a manifest oci
body:
### Kyverno CLI Version

1.11.0

### Description

For Go applications built with ARM and AMD architectures, we create a Docker manifest. Basically:

`europe-docker.pkg.dev/hidden/http2back:0.8.0` (a Docker manifest that references the two images below)
`europe-docker.pkg.dev/hidden/http2back:0.8.0-amd64`
`europe-docker.pkg.dev/hidden/http2back:0.8.0-arm64`

Both `company_registry.com/images/toto:0.8.0-amd64` and `company_registry.com/images/toto:0.8.0-arm64` are signed during the CI process with Github Artifact Attestations feature, but not the manifest (because it can't be signed—it's a manifest, not an image).

When we reference the manifest `europe-docker.pkg.dev/hidden/http2back:0.8.0` (so that Kubernetes can download the ARM or AMD image based on the node architecture), Kyverno tells us that `europe-docker.pkg.dev/hidden/http2back:0.8.0` is not signed, which is true because it's not an image but a manifest. 


Kyverno policy:

```
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: sigstore-attestation-verification
spec:
  background: false
  webhookTimeoutSeconds: 30
  rules:
  - match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - Pod
    name: sigstore-attestation-verification
    verifyImages:
    - imageReferences:
      - "europe-docker.pkg.dev/hidden/*"
      failureAction: Audit
      mutateDigest: false # mutateDigest must be set to false for Audit failure action
      verifyDigest: false
      type: SigstoreBundle
      attestations:
      - attestors:
        - entries:
          - keyless:
              issuer: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
              subjectRegExp: https://github\.com\/company\/.+
              rekor:
                ignoreTlog: true
                url: https://fulcio.githubapp.com
        conditions:
        - all:
          - key: "{{`{{ buildDefinition.buildType }}`}}"
            operator: Equals
            value: https://actions.github.io/buildtypes/workflow/v1
        type: https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1
```

manifest:
```
{
   "schemaVersion": 2,
   "mediaType": "application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json",

      {
         "mediaType": "application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json",

         "platform": {
            "architecture": "amd64",
            "os": "linux"
         }
      },
      {

         "digest": "sha256:e7cf8eadfc7d55f1973227b0f1a0f226fdd49c027a42955868ce63a584a91742",

   ]
}
```

### Kyverno Version

1.13.4

### Description

Under high api-server pressure, the aggregate worker in kyverno-report-controller may occasionally fail to start, preventing proper creation of compliance reports. This results in PolicyReport resources not being created, causing the Web Console to either display no compliance violation information or only partial report data. To troubleshoot, check the kyverno-report-controller pod logs for the presence of "starting worker aggregate-report-controller/worker" messages to verify proper operation. title: [Bug] Background mutation breaks validation on Create
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.13.4

### Kubernetes Version

1.32.x

### Kubernetes Platform

Other (specify in description)

### Kyverno Rule Type

Mutate

### Description

There seems to be a but in the mutation logic, when background mutation is enabled.

We have a mutation - with background mutation enabled - adding a label when it does not exist to e.g. an Deployment. We also have a validation which checks this label against a whitelist.

- When background mutation is not enabled (no `target`/`mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate` present in the mutation rule), everything works fine. The label is added and the validation succeeds.
- When background mutation is enabled (see code below), then the label is NOT present during the validation message: 
```
validate-label:
  validate-label: |
    null not in msggroup whitelist: ["label1","label2","atestvalue"].
```
The mutation is actually working, when no validation is deployed.

It seems that mutation with enabled background mutations, are NOT mutated in the AdmissionReview process before the validation.

(This behavior is observed on K8s 1.32 on Tanzu and EKS).

### Steps to reproduce

Example muation:
```
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-label
spec:
  rules:
  - match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - Deployment
          namespaces:
          - default
    mutate:
      mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate: true
      patchStrategicMerge:
        metadata:
          labels:
            +(atestlabel): atestvalue
      targets:
      - apiVersion: apps/v1
        kind: Deployment
        namespace: default
    name: enforce-label
```

Example validation:
```
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-label
spec:
  rules:
  - match:
      any:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - Deployment
          namespaces:
          - default
    mutate:
      mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate: true
      patchStrategicMerge:
        metadata:
          labels:
            +(atestlabel): atestvalue
      targets:
      - apiVersion: apps/v1
        kind: Deployment
        namespace: default
    name: enforce-label
```


Example deployment:
```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: nginx
  name: nginx
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - image: nginx
        name: nginx
        resources: {}
```

### Expected behavior

The mutation should add the label on resource creation also if background muations are enabled.

title: [Bug] Rolebindings don't respect namespaces when referencing clusterRoles.
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.11.0

### Kubernetes Version

1.28.x

### Kubernetes Platform

EKS

### Kyverno Rule Type

Validate

### Description

request data is populated with clusterroles that don't apply in the namespace that the request is being made and RoleBindings don't respect namespace when referencing clusterRoles. Instead all clusterRoles are associated that the user belongs to are returned by kyverno; 

For example if I have a rolebinding referencing the `admin` clusterRole. If I make a request to a different namespace, kyverno still includes the same `admin` clusterRole as part of my request.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a rolebinding in the `default` namespace:
```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: my-role-binding
  namespace: default
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: admin
subjects:
- apiGroup: rbac.authroization.k8s.io
   kind: Group
   name: my-group
```
and a clusterPolicy
```
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: restrict-ephemeral-containers
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  background: false
  rules:
  - name: restrict-ephemeral-containers
    match:
      all:
      - resources:
          kinds:
          - Pod/ephemeralcontainers
          operations:
          - UPDATE
          - CREATE
    validate:
      message: "Debug info - User: {{ request.clusterRoles }}"
      deny: {}
```

when I make a request against a different namespace I get the following:
```
kubectl debug -n kube-system  my-pod   -it --image=nicolaka/netshoot

Defaulting debug container name to debugger-2n7lt.
Error from server: admission webhook "validate.kyverno.svc-fail" denied the request:

resource Pod/kube-system/my-pod was blocked due to the following policies

restrict-ephemeral-containers:
  restrict-envoy-ephemeral-images: 'Debug info - User: [..., "admin",..., "system:basic-user","system:discovery","system:public-info-viewer"]'
```

### Expected behavior

I would expect it to only include clusterRoles that belong to the namespace where the rolebinding exists. ex; `admin` should only be returned if I made a request against the `default` namespace... not `kube-system`. Otherwise there is no way to use this information to make decisions when defining clusterPolicies;

title: [Bug] mutate foreach reorders initContainers when using patchStrategicMerge if any are skipped by preconditions
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.13.4

### Description

When using `foreach` to loop over the `initContainers` of a pod and edit them with `patchStrategicMerge`, if the preconditions skip any of the containers, the resulting output has the `initContainers` reordered. We originally noticed this in our cluster, but can easily reproduce locally using the Kyverno cli.

Here is a simple example that reproduces the problem.

Test pod:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: testpod
spec:
  initContainers:
    - name: c
      image: busybox:latest
      command: [echo, c ]
    - name: b
      image: busybox:latest
      command: [echo, b ]
    - name: a
      image: busybox:latest
      command: [echo, a ]
  containers:
    - image: busybox:latest
      command: [tail, -f, /dev/null ]
      name: main
  restartPolicy: Never
```

Test policy:

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  rules:
    - name: test
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds:
                - Pod
      mutate:
        foreach:
          - list: request.object.spec.initContainers[]
            preconditions:
              all:
                - key: '{{ element.name }}'
                  operator: AnyIn
                  value:
                    - a
                    #- b   # <========================== if I uncomment these, the containers no longer reorder
                    #- c
            patchStrategicMerge:
              spec:
                initContainers:
                  - name: "{{ element.name }}"
                    imagePullPolicy: always
```

Use `kubectl kyverno` to apply the policy to the pod:

```
 $ kubectl kyverno apply policy.yaml --resource pod.yaml

Applying 3 policy rule(s) to 1 resource(s)...

policy test applied to default/Pod/testpod:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: testpod
  namespace: default
spec:
  containers:
  - command:
    - tail
    - -f
    - /dev/null
    image: busybox:latest
    name: main
  initContainers:
  - command:
    - echo
    - a
    image: busybox:latest
    imagePullPolicy: always
    name: a
  - command:
    - echo
    - c
    image: busybox:latest
    name: c
  - command:
    - echo
    - b
    image: busybox:latest
    name: b
  restartPolicy: Never

---


Mutation:
Mutation has been applied successfully.
pass: 1, fail: 0, warn: 0, error: 0, skip: 0
```

Notice the `initContainers` are reordered.  The containers that are _not_ skipped by preconditions appear first, followed by the ones that were skipped.

Note that if I use `patchesJson6902` instead of `patchStrategicMerge` the reordering does not occur. 

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  rules:
    - name: test
      match:
        any:
          - resources:
              kinds:
                - Pod
      mutate:
        foreach:
          - list: request.object.spec.initContainers[]
            preconditions:
              all:
                - key: '{{ element.name }}'
                  operator: AnyIn
                  value:
                    - a
            patchesJson6902: |-
              - path: /spec/initContainers/{{elementIndex}}/imagePullPolicy
                op: add
                value: always
```

```
 $ kubectl kyverno apply policy-json-patch.yaml --resource pod.yaml

Applying 1 policy rule(s) to 1 resource(s)...

policy test applied to default/Pod/testpod:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: testpod
  namespace: default
spec:
  containers:
  - command:
    - tail
    - -f
    - /dev/null
    image: busybox:latest
    name: main
  initContainers:
  - command:
    - echo
    - c
    image: busybox:latest
    name: c
  - command:
    - echo
    - b
    image: busybox:latest
    name: b
  - command:
    - echo
    - a
    image: busybox:latest
    imagePullPolicy: always
    name: a
  restartPolicy: Never

---


Mutation:
Mutation has been applied successfully.
pass: 1, fail: 0, warn: 0, error: 0, skip: 0

```

Here is a zip containing the test files shown above: [testfiles.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19473727/testfiles.zip)

While searching for previously reported issues, I did find #9863. The circumstances look very similar, but it was closed as being caused by Istio. In our case, we aren't using Istio and can reproduce both in Kubernetes and locally with the Kyverno cli.

### Steps to reproduce

title: [Bug] [CLI] Apply: multi-level repositories are not supported
body:
### Kyverno CLI Version

1.13.4

### Description

While working on #12510 I realized there is another issue with working with git repositories and retrieving policies from there. Currently, the URL parsing seems to rely on git URLs that have the Github structure, meaning `https://<host>/<owner>/<repository>/policies`. Anything after `<repository>` is interpreted as a path within the repository to the appropriate YAMLs -> `/policies`.

However, in for instance Gitlab, it is allowed to have multiple subgroups/levels. A Gitlab repository URL can for instance look like this: `https://<host>/group1/group2/<repository>/policies`. Now the path extraction fails, as it expects the repository to be `group2`, rather than `repository`. The YAML path is now interpreted as `/<repository>/policies`, while it should still be `/policies`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use the kyverno apply command with a non-Github git URL that uses subgroups, e.g. in Gitlab: `https://<host>/group1/group2/<repository>/policies`.
2. An error pops up that the repository is not found.

### Expected behavior

The repository and YAMLs should be found and correctly retrieved.

title: [Bug] mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate with targets applies to CRD services (e.g., services.serving.knative.dev), despite only targeting v1/Service
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.13.4

### Description

In Kyverno **1.13.4**, when using mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate: true with targets, the policy unexpectedly attempts to mutate CRD services, such as services.serving.knative.dev, even though only **v1/Service** is explicitly targeted.

This results in the following error message in the Kyverno background controller logs:

```
ERR github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/background/mutate/mutate.go:180 > error="failed to mutate existing resource, rule frontend, response error: : services.serving.knative.dev \"traefik\" not found"
```

The expected behavior is that only Kubernetes core services (v1/Service) should be mutated, and CRD-based services should be ignored.

### Reproduction Steps

Deploy the following ClusterPolicy in a Kyverno 1.13.4 environment:

```yaml
    apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
    kind: ClusterPolicy
    metadata:
      name: lb-service-labeling
    spec:
      background: true
      rules:
        - name: frontend
          match:
            any:
            - resources:
                kinds:
                - v1/Service  # Ensuring only Kubernetes core services should be affected
                namespaces:
                - traefik-system
          mutate:
            mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate: true
            targets:
            - kind: Service
              name: traefik
              namespace: traefik-system
            patchStrategicMerge:
              metadata:
                labels:
                  label1: foo
                  label2: bar
```

- Ensure that Knative Service CRDs (services.serving.knative.dev) are also present in the cluster.
- Apply the policy.
- Observe the Kyverno background controller logs.


### Expected Behavior

- Kyverno should only mutate v1/Service resources.
- The policy should not attempt to mutate CRD-based services like **services.serving.knative.dev**.
- No error related to services.serving.knative.dev should appear.


### Actual Behavior

Despite explicitly matching only **v1/Service**, Kyverno attempts to mutate **services.serving.knative.dev** ?
This results in errors because these resources do not exist in the cluster.

### Additional Information

- Running kubectl api-resources | grep services confirms that only v1/Service is present.

### Workarounds tried (but failed)

Explicitly using v1/Service in match.kinds

If we don't use the option `mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate:true` and targets Option, the rule is working fine, but we need to make sure existing resources will be mutated as well.

### Hypothesis

The background mutation logic (mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate) might be incorrectly resolving Service kinds across all API groups, not just v1/Service ?

### Environment Details

- Kyverno version: 1.13.4
- Kubernetes version: v1.28
- Installation method: Helm
- Cluster environment: On-prem

Would appreciate any feedback from the Kyverno team on this issue! Thanks in advance. 🙌
